\item \textbf{Two certified shapes, as \emph{valid} bounds} \mE: every Loewner step is certified by a
completed Cholesky ($-1.5\times10^{-14}$, $-2.3\times10^{-10}$). The additive Hardy chain dominates
$\rho(W)$ on $11/11$ (factor $3.074$--$10.758$); its own exact two-term Weyl split dominates too
($1.691$--$2.503$) and lies \emph{below} the chain everywhere, so it is the floor of the additive
family; the joint shape $\Lambda(H,Y)\cdot\Omega(Y)$ with a positive definite Jacobi Hardy form $Y$
dominates on $11/11$ with the closed-form geometric profile ($8.815$--$74.872$ at
$\Omega=8.33$--$36.2$) and on $11/11$ with the per-zone tridiagonal read-off of $K^{+}$. Promoted is
the \emph{dominance}; the factors are not. Controls: the same $Y$ without its mass term is singular
--- the constant vector lies in its kernel ($5.7\times10^{-17}$) while $H$ does not vanish there ---
so the certificate \emph{refuses} on $11/11$; and dropping the \emph{positive} part instead of the
negative one falls below $\rho(W)$ on $11/11$.
\item \textbf{The sign-versus-absolute separation, as a comparison} \mX: over the measured $D$ range
the exactly bounded object spreads by $1.36\times$ while every absolute variant spreads by at least
$54.94\times$ (Loewner drop $62.03$, Cauchy--Schwarz $54.94$, product $56.92$), and dropping the
positive part of $H$ costs $9.96$--$464.63\times$. The power laws are \emph{fits}, labelled as fits:
$D^{-0.138\pm0.094}$ (signed) against $D^{-0.776\pm0.352}$ (certified Muckenhoupt) and $D^{-2.748}$,
$D^{-2.820}$, $D^{-2.918}$ (absolute).
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows; nothing uniform in the zone
index or in $D$, and every exponent above is a fit that stays in the sandbox. The bound rows promote
\emph{validity} and not size: neither shape beats the target, the additive shape is dead as a
\emph{shape} by its own Weyl floor, and the joint shape is decided at the normalisation $\Omega$.
The finite-core row is an \emph{identity} and not a bound --- the zone-uniform discrete Hardy
inequality it reduces the question to stays open, and no marker moves toward it.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The capacity-chain identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v546}}{v546})}\label{sec:v546}
The identity spine of the capacity cycle T142--T145 of Section~\ref{sec:phase2}: what the
certified chain \emph{is}, per instance and machine-checked, with the one open lemma fenced
out \veri{v546\_capacity\_chain\_identities.py} ($26$ checks, ${\sim}0.5$\,s; promotion of
the identity blocks of T142--T145 on $12$ frame-A windows, $n=4\ldots139$, $h=26\ldots285\le300$,
$D=7.578\times10^{-3}\ldots2.789\times10^{-2}$, $32$--$5102$ positive off-diagonal edges; the
covering kernel is positive definite on $11$ of them, where the first two items run; each
statement carries a mutation control that must fail by $\ge10^{-3}$).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The capacity decomposition (T142)} \mE:
$K^{-1}=D^{\mathsf T}J^{-1}D+xx^{\mathsf T}/\mathrm{cap}$ with $J=DKD^{\mathsf T}$ (assembled
entrywise, $3.8\times10^{-15}$), $x=K^{-1}\mathbf 1$ the equilibrium charge and
$\mathrm{cap}=\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}\mathbf 1$, as a matrix identity ($1.4\times10^{-13}$);
under the congruence $u=K^{1/2}v$ the Dirichlet half is an \emph{orthogonal projection} ($P^2=P$
at $1.9\times10^{-12}$, $\Omega=\lambda_{\max}(P)=1$ to $5.1\times10^{-12}$ --- the T142
normalisation, where T141 had guessed $20.7$--$2724$), its complement \emph{is} the capacity
rank-one, and it annihilates the equilibrium direction $K^{-1/2}\mathbf 1$. Controls: dropping
the rank-one ($3.4\times10^{-1}$), a $1\%$ cap perturbation ($3.4\times10^{-3}$).
\item \textbf{The exact capacity--Rayleigh identity (T143)} \mE: with $H=\mathrm{diag}(s)+L_N$
($4.7\times10^{-16}$), $L_N=D^{\mathsf T}BD$ for the signed crossing kernel
($4.9\times10^{-16}$) and $\rho(W)=1-\lambda_{\min}(A,A_B)$ ($5.4\times10^{-14}$), the assembled
quotient
$[\,d^{\mathsf T}(J^{-1}-B)d+(x^{\mathsf T}v)^2/\mathrm{cap}-\sum_ks_kv_k^2\,]/[\,d^{\mathsf T}J^{-1}d+(x^{\mathsf T}v)^2/\mathrm{cap}\,]$
equals $v^{\mathsf T}(K^{-1}-H)v/v^{\mathsf T}K^{-1}v$ for \emph{every} $v$
($9.5\times10^{-14}$ on $24$ random vectors per window), reproduces $1-\rho(W)$ at the exact top
eigenvector ($1.7\times10^{-9}$ under the \emph{declared} $1/\mathrm{gap}$ conditioning bar
$5.4\times10^{-8}$), and every random quotient stays $\ge1-\rho(W)$ (the inf property); on the
constant vector the whole denominator \emph{is} the capacity term. Controls: dropping the cap
term (rel $=1$), the $|N|$ crossing kernel ($2.6\times10^{-1}$).
\item \textbf{Cholesky nestedness (T144)} \mE: $\mathrm{cap}_E([a,a{+}j))$ equals the prefix sum
of squared forward-substitution entries of \emph{one} triangular solve --- $3404$ interval
capacities from $36$ solves at $2.0\times10^{-14}$ against independent Schur solves, exhaustive
on the median window (every prefix, $2.8\times10^{-14}$), monotone in $b$ by construction.
Control: the reversed ordering computes \emph{suffix} capacities and deviates by
$\ge4.6\times10^{-1}$.
\item \textbf{The whitening certificate (T144)} \mE:
$\lambda_{\max}(W)\le\kappa_{\mathrm{up}}$ (completed Cholesky) $\le$ the Gershgorin ceiling on
every window ($\kappa_{\mathrm{up}}=1.2245$--$1.4236$ against $\le2.1213$); the licensed chain
direction $\lambda_{\min}(E)/\kappa_{\mathrm{up}}\le\lambda_{\min}(A,A_B)$ holds on every window
--- a \emph{denominator} comparison, untouched by T142's numerator obstruction --- and the
Cholesky refuses at the shrunken shift $0.995\,\lambda_{\max}(W)$.
\item \textbf{The M4 split and the certified chain (T145)} \mE: the mass half of Maz'ya's step
M4 --- $\sum_kf_k^2\le\psi^2$ \emph{pointwise} (a theorem for nonnegative truncations, exact
slack $\ge0$), the row-wise implication on rows with $(E\mathbf 1)_i\ge0$, and the full step
$\sigma_{\mathrm{tot}}=0.2197$--$0.4425<1$ on every window although the Markov hypothesis is
absent. Licence 4 is stated with $|R|$ and \emph{not} $R^{+}$, with the witness
$R=\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}1&-1/2\\-1/2&1\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$, $x=(1,-1)$ ($3.0>2.0$) built
in as a counterexample check. The sign-free chain is ordered on every window, and S1$'$ is
\emph{certified per window on both routes}:
$\mathrm{cert\_lam\_max}(R)\le12\,\sigma_{\mathrm{tot}}\Psi_{\mathrm{pos}}$ (energy,
$c_0=2.6369$--$5.3099$) and $\le G_{\mathrm{dy}}\Psi_{\mathrm{abs}}$ (sign-free,
$c_0=2.5154$--$6.1449$), better route $c_0=2.5154$--$4.2265$ against the classical Dirichlet
value $4$; the all-sets density bound carries Charikar's cited constant, bracketed by exhaustive
enumeration of all $4095$ subsets of a small block. Control: $c_0\times10^{-3}$ breaks the
certificate on every window.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows; nothing uniform in the
zone index or in $D$, and every T142--T145 exponent is a fit that stays in the sandbox. The
$c_0$ of the last row is \emph{measured} at the minimiser's own layer cake --- the a-priori
\emph{level lemma} (T145's L1) stays open, unclaimed and unapproached, and no marker moves
toward it. Maz'ya's strong-type half is \emph{not} used as a theorem anywhere: it is the thing
the cycle transcribes.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The level-lemma identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v547}}{v547})}\label{sec:v547}
The a-priori core of T146 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the same level constant that \vref{v546}
certified with a \emph{measured} input, now supplied as a functional of the form alone
\veri{v547\_level\_lemma\_identities.py} ($20$ checks, ${\sim}0.4$\,s; promotion of the four
a-priori pieces of T146 on $12$ frame-A windows, $n=4\ldots139$, $m=26\ldots285\le300$,
$D=7.578\times10^{-3}\ldots2.789\times10^{-2}$, plus $9$ random positive definite forms for the
form-independent items and a stress ladder $m=64\ldots288$; each statement carries a mutation
control that must fail by $\ge10^{-3}$).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The union identity for nested cakes (T146)} \mE: for a nested decreasing chain
with positive coefficients,
$\sum_{j,l}c_jc_l\,|S_j\cup S_l|=2T\|\psi_t\|_1-\|\psi_t\|^2$ with $T=\sum_jc_j$ and
$\psi_t=\sum_jc_j\mathbf 1_{S_j}$ --- form-independent and $O(m)$, the reason the cake base is
movable at all; checked against T145's $K\times K$ double sum on all $12$ window minimisers and
$9$ random vectors (max rel $0.0$) \emph{and} against the union sizes computed from the sets
themselves with no nestedness used. Controls: shuffling one proper level set breaks it
($3.2\times10^{-2}$), a $1\%$ perturbation of the heaviest coefficient breaks the double sum
($4.8\times10^{-3}$).
\item \textbf{The layer-cake counting lemma at a general base (T146)} \mE:
$G(b)\le2b^2\,\|v\|_\infty\|v\|_1/\|v\|^2+\varepsilon(b)$ for \emph{any} vector $v$ at all $6$
preregistered bases (margin $\ge1.08$ on the battery and on every window minimiser); at $b=2$
the leading constant is the classical dyadic $8$ \emph{exactly}, and the base is \emph{free}
because the chain consumes only the lower domination $|v|\le\psi_t$: the a-priori constant
gains $4/b_*^2=3.7612$ over base $2$ on every window. Controls: the bound $\times10^{-3}$
fails everywhere, and the one-level-down cake ($\psi_t/b$) breaks the domination on every draw
--- the $+1$ in the cake exponent is load-bearing.
\item \textbf{The resolvent delocalisation bound (T146)} \mE: $\psi=\lambda R\psi$ to
$9.0\times10^{-14}$ --- an \emph{identity}, so no Davis--Kahan transfer step appears anywhere
--- and per coordinate (Cauchy--Schwarz), with $\lambda_{\mathrm{up}}=\min_j
\mathrm{Rayleigh}(Re_j)\ge\lambda_{\min}$ (Rayleigh--Ritz; window ratio $1.0592$--$1.2883$) and
the column norms certified from above with the linear-solve residual paid for,
\[
\|\psi\|_\infty\;\le\;\lambda_{\mathrm{up}}\,\max_j\|R e_j\|\,\|\psi\|
\]
on every window, within a factor $1.061$--$1.337$ of the truth. \emph{The lever}: the trivial
ceiling $\max_j\|Re_j\|\le1/\lambda_{\min}$ would give $\Gamma\le\sqrt m=5.1$--$16.9$
(useless); the certified columns sit a factor $2.85$--$10.17$ \emph{below} it (preregistered
bar $2.0$), giving $\Gamma=1.8356$--$2.2797$ --- read off the form, never off the minimiser.
Controls: a $1\%$ $\lambda$ perturbation breaks the identity ($1.0\times10^{-2}$), the sup
bound $\times10^{-3}$ fails on every window.
\item \textbf{The composite level lemma (T146)} \mE:
$c_0^{\mathrm{ap}}=2b^2\,\Gamma\min(1,\Gamma_1)+\varepsilon=3.9042$--$4.8488$ dominates the
measured level constant on all $12$ windows (slack $1.986$--$2.418$) and stays under the
preregistered ceiling $16=4\times$ Maz'ya's Dirichlet value $4$; the certified window
inequality $\mathrm{cert\_lam\_max}(R)\le c_0^{\mathrm{ap}}\Psi_{\mathrm{abs}}$ holds on
$12/12$ (both sides by completed Cholesky, the density the $|R|$ one with Charikar's cited
constant), closing the chain at loss factor $0.0423$--$0.1272$ of the exact gap ---
\vref{v546}'s certified chain with its one measured input replaced by a functional of the
form. \emph{The built-in discriminator}: on T145's no-go form $R=aa^{\mathsf T}+\varepsilon I$,
$a_i=i^{-1/2}$, $\Gamma$ grows $3.676\to6.798$ over $m=64\ldots288$ (ratio $1.85\ge$ the
preregistered $1.5$) and $c_0^{\mathrm{ap}}=11.10$ \emph{exceeds} every window value --- the
bound must be worse there, since a candidate that did not fail on the no-go would prove a
false statement --- while the theorem half survives on every no-go size and the Dirichlet
path-Laplacian control stays flat (max/min $1.0063$). Control: $c_0^{\mathrm{ap}}\times
10^{-3}$ breaks the certificate on every window.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows --- a \emph{finite list}
of certified window inequalities with an explicit maximum; nothing uniform in the zone index
or in $D$, and explicitly \emph{no} statement for all $D$: the asymptotic delocalisation of
the Green columns (T146's remainder) stays open and typed open. Only the sign-free / Green
constant is bounded a priori --- the energy-route $\sigma_{\mathrm{tot}}$ stays
\emph{measured} --- and every T146 exponent is a fit that stays in the sandbox. Davis--Kahan
1970 is cited as the transfer step this route deliberately avoids; Maz'ya's strong-type half
is \emph{not} used as a theorem anywhere.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The Green/Szeg\H{o} identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v548}}{v548})}\label{sec:v548}
The identity/certificate core of T147 and T148 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the two scalars the
level constant of \vref{v547} is made of, certified on the same class of windows
\veri{v548\_green\_szego\_identities.py} ($21$ checks, ${\sim}0.4$\,s; promotion of the
identity/certificate pieces of T147+T148 on $12$ frame-A windows, $n=4\ldots139$,
$m=26\ldots285\le300$, $D=7.578\times10^{-3}\ldots2.789\times10^{-2}$, plus $7$ random positive
definite forms for the form-independent items and a weight-class model ladder $m=64\ldots288$;
each statement carries a mutation control that must fail by $\ge10^{-3}$).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The factorisation identity (T147)} \mE: for any symmetric positive definite form
with Green matrix $R$,
\[
\Gamma=\sqrt m\,\lambda_{\mathrm{up}}\max_j\|Re_j\|
\;=\;\sqrt{Q^\star}\cdot S_w\,,\qquad
S_w=\lambda_{\mathrm{up}}\|R\|_F\,,\qquad
Q^\star=m\,\max_j(R^2)_{jj}/\operatorname{tr}(R^2)\,,
\]
\emph{exact} at $2.2\times10^{-16}$ on all $12$ windows and $7$ random forms --- the all-$D$
question splits into a purely spectral and a purely geometric scalar and into nothing else; the
certified factorisation (residual-paid column norms, Frobenius bracket) dominates the true
$\Gamma$ everywhere, with $S_w=1.1186$--$1.5777$ and $Q^\star=2.0879$--$2.8634$ on this list.
Controls: a $1\%$ $Q^\star$ perturbation breaks the identity ($5.0\times10^{-3}$), perturbing
the largest Green column breaks the factorisation.
\item \textbf{The bottom-block equidistribution constant (T147)} \mE: with $\Pi_B$ the spectral
projector onto $B=\{k:\lambda_k\le10\hat\lambda\}$ (preregistered rule, $|B|=3\ldots5$),
$\sum_j(\Pi_B)_{jj}=|B|$ \emph{exactly} ($3.3\times10^{-16}$), hence
$Q_B=m\max_j(\Pi_B)_{jj}\ge|B|$ is a theorem (max $\ge$ mean) --- and the \emph{measured}
$Q_B/|B|=1.5091$--$1.7980$ lies in the preregistered band $[1,2.2]$ against the
Szeg\H{o}/Widom sharp reference $Q_B\le2|B|$ (a measurement on a finite list, typed as such;
T148's honest negative stands beside it: $f(0)<0$ on every surface window, so the mechanism
enters nowhere as a theorem). Controls: the rank-$|B|$ coordinate projector gives $Q_B=m$ and
overshoots the band by $\ge3.9$; a $1\%$ basis scaling breaks the trace identity.
\item \textbf{The second-difference $\ell^1$ ceiling (T148, the lever)} \mE: from the exact
Dirichlet eigenpair $L_0s_k=\mu_ks_k$ (KMS 1953) and $\mu_k\ge4k^2/(m+1)^2$
($\sin t\ge2t/\pi$), the coefficient bound
$|a_k|\le\min\bigl(1,\|s_k\|_\infty\|L_0^p\psi\|_1/\mu_k^p\bigr)$ for $p=1,2$ holds against the
\emph{true} coefficients on the bottom mode of every window and on random unit vectors (worst
excess $\le0$); the chain $\|a\|_1\le\mathrm{ceil}_\mu$,
$\mathrm{ceil}_\nu\le2\sqrt\nu+1$ with $\nu=(m+1)^{3/2}\|L_0\psi\|_1/(2\sqrt2)$ --- every power
of $m$ cancelled, $\nu$ alone carries the $m$-dependence --- and
$m\|\psi\|_\infty^2\le2\|a\|_1^2$ holds everywhere. \emph{Calibration}: for the Dirichlet
bottom mode $\|a\|_1=1$ exactly and $\nu=3.1415\to\pi$ at every size. Controls: the ceiling
$\times10^{-3}$ fails on every window, a one-index $\mu$ shift breaks the coefficient identity
($1.5\times10^{-1}$).
\item \textbf{The layer-cake $S_w$ certificate (T148)} \mE: the completed LDL$^{\mathsf T}$
inertia count at every rung of the preregistered ladder $\tau_i=\rho_i\lambda_{\mathrm{lo}}$
($\rho=1.5\ldots1024$, $\lambda_{\mathrm{lo}}$ a certified positive floor) equals the direct
spectral count \emph{exactly} on all $96$ (window, rung) pairs (Sylvester 1852; Bunch--Kaufman
1977 --- a certificate, never a sorted list), and the layer cake
$\sum_k\lambda_k^{-2}\le N_1/\lambda_{\mathrm{lo}}^2+\sum_i(N_{i+1}{-}N_i)/\tau_i^2
+(m{-}N_L)/\tau_L^2$ certifies $S_w\le1.3288$--$1.8220$ per window (true
$1.1186$--$1.5777$, slack $\le1.216$); nothing here says $m$-free --- that reading lives in the
sandbox as a labelled trend. Control: \emph{dropping the bottom layer} breaks the bound on
every window --- the bottom eigenvalue is the weight.
\item \textbf{The Liouville transform and the weight-class discriminator (T148)} \mE: the chain
\[
m\|\psi\|_\infty^2\;\le\;\kappa_\Lambda\,m\|\hat\varphi\|_\infty^2
\;\le\;2\kappa_\Lambda\,\|a(\hat\varphi)\|_1^2
\;\le\;2\kappa_\Lambda\,\mathrm{ceil}(\hat\varphi)^2\,,\qquad
\varphi=\Lambda^{-1/2}\psi\,,
\]
holds stepwise on every bottom-block mode of every window --- the exact pencil equivalence
$E\psi=\lambda\psi\Leftrightarrow A\varphi=\lambda\Lambda\varphi$ is a change of variables, not
a perturbation (Davis--Kahan 1970 cited as the route T148 computed to be vacuous and \emph{not}
used) --- with $\kappa_\Lambda=\max\Lambda/\min\Lambda=1.3868$--$2.5805$ \emph{a priori} (a
ratio of two diagonal entries of the form). \emph{The discriminator}: on a model section with a
genuine order-2 zero ($f(0)=0$, $f''(0)/2=1$, verified exactly), over the ladder $m=64\ldots288$
at matched $\kappa_\Lambda$ (mismatch $0.0013$), the bounded-variation multiplier keeps $\nu$
flat (max/min $1.003$) while the rough multiplier ($\mathrm{TV}(\log\Lambda)$ larger by
$162.6$) grows by $19.9$ --- the rough class \emph{must} be worse, and it is: the operative
hypothesis is the roughness of the multiplier, not its condition number. Control: the first
Liouville step $\times10^{-3}$ fails on every mode, provably (the step slack is bounded by
$\kappa_\Lambda^2$).
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows --- a \emph{finite list}
of certified window inequalities with an explicit maximum; nothing uniform in the zone index
or in $D$, and explicitly \emph{no} statement for all $D$: the one open lifting input
($\nu_L\le F(\text{form})$ with $F$ $m$-free; equivalently bounded $\mathrm{TV}(\log\Lambda)$
or any weaker smoothness of the multiplier) stays open and typed open. The symbol-level
order-2 hypothesis is \emph{refuted} (T148: $f(0)<0$ on every surface window) and enters
nowhere as a theorem; $\sigma_{\mathrm{tot}}$ stays retired as a route; every T147/T148
exponent is a fit that stays in the sandbox.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The gauge/parity identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v549}}{v549})}\label{sec:v549}
The identity/certificate core of T149 and T150 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the gauge
\emph{freedom} around the machinery \vref{v548} certified in the Jacobi gauge, and the parity
\emph{structure} underneath it \veri{v549\_gauge\_parity\_identities.py} ($21$ checks,
${\sim}0.3$\,s; promotion of the identity/certificate pieces of T149+T150 on $12$ frame-A
windows, $n=4\ldots139$, $m=26\ldots285\le300$,
$D=7.578\times10^{-3}\ldots2.789\times10^{-2}$, with $48$ gauge assemblies, the full-section
parity items on the $6$ windows with $M\le300$, and a parity control model at $m=2001$; each
statement carries a mutation control that must fail by $\ge10^{-3}$).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The gauge freedom (T149)} \mE: for \emph{any} positive diagonal
$\tilde\Lambda$ the whitening $\tilde E=\tilde\Lambda^{-1/2}A\tilde\Lambda^{-1/2}$ is an
exact congruence, so
$\lambda_{\min}(A)\ge\mathrm{cert\_lam\_min}(\tilde E)\cdot\min_j\tilde\Lambda_j$ is a
\emph{valid} certified lower bound for every gauge --- an identity plus one Rayleigh step ---
and the family maximum is valid too (all $48$ assemblies: Jacobi, const, moving-geometric-mean,
and the arithmetic-free archimedean diagonal); the factorisation identity
$\Gamma=\sqrt{Q^\star}S_w$ holds \emph{gauge-invariantly} (max rel $2.4\times10^{-16}$); the
const gauge (the geometric mean of the Jacobi diagonal) has $\mathrm{TV}(\log\tilde\Lambda)=0$
\emph{exactly} on every window --- T149's elimination, not reduction, of T148's blocking scalar
--- with the certified entrywise sandwich $\sigma=c_2/c_1=1.3868$--$2.5805$. Controls: a $1\%$
$Q^\star$ perturbation breaks the identity ($4.99\times10^{-3}$); on the shifted indefinite
form $A-1.05\lambda_{\min}I$ the completed-Cholesky floor \emph{refuses} on $12/12$.
\item \textbf{The two-regime discriminator (T149, the refutation as a check)} \mE: the
flutter-smoothing gauge (moving geometric mean, preregistered half-width $m/16$) removes
$\mathrm{TV}(\log\Lambda)$ by $\ge2.88\times$ on every window while moving the
Liouville-\emph{transported} bottom-block smoothness functional $\nu_{\tilde L}$ by at most
$0.0088$ --- and even the matched-amplitude \emph{rough} re-gauge (lattice-scale oscillation)
moves it by at most $0.0046$ (bar $0.01$ for both): the roughness $\nu_{\tilde L}$ responds to
is \emph{not} in the multiplier --- T149's withdrawal of the TV hypothesis, wired as a
per-instance check. Control: the same functional read \emph{without} the transport (on the
whitened modes $\psi$, which carry the multiplier) jumps by $0.41$--$9.76$ under the same rough
re-gauge --- the invariance is carried by the transport, not by numbness of the functional.
\item \textbf{The explicit zone diagonal (T150)} \mE:
\[
\Lambda_r\;=\;c_0-c_{M-1-2r}+\sum_{s\ne r}\max\bigl(c_{|r-s|}-c_{M-1-r-s},\,0\bigr)\,,
\]
assembled lagwise with no matrix anywhere, equals the lumped-pair diagonal on every window
(max rel $5.9\times10^{-16}$) --- the whitening diagonal is an \emph{explicit} functional of
the zone's lag arithmetic and of nothing else; the lag vector splits \emph{exactly} as
$c=c^{\mathrm{arch}}+c^{\mathrm{atom}}$ with $c^{\mathrm{atom}}\le0$ entrywise, and the
arithmetic mass carries the closed budget
$\|c^{\mathrm{atom}}\|_1\le\sum_j\mu_j\le4B\sqrt N$ with $B=1.038821$ the \emph{verified}
maximum of $\psi(n)/n$ over the whole atom table (Chebyshev 1852, computed and never assumed;
Abel summation carries the closed form). \emph{The honest negative as content}: the archimedean
section alone is \emph{indefinite} on $12/12$ windows (completed LDL$^{\mathsf T}$, up to $5$
negative eigenvalues) while the full section has zero --- the atoms are \emph{co-responsible}
for the positivity, so the additive perturbation reading (Weyl 1912 / Bauer--Fike 1960 /
Davis--Kahan 1970, cited, computed dead by T150 at $2.4$--$5.8$ orders, \emph{not} used) is
structurally empty and only the multiplicative / Loewner gauge step transfers. Control:
dropping the positive part in the zone formula breaks the identity ($4.25\times10^{-1}$).
\item \textbf{The parity compression (T150, the named mechanism)} \mE: with $U_-$, $U_+$ the
antisymmetric / symmetric parity isometries of the full window,
\[
U_-^{\mathsf T}\,T_M(c)\,U_-\;=\;T-H\,,\qquad
U_+^{\mathsf T}\,T_M(c)\,U_+\;=\;T+H\,,\qquad
U_+^{\mathsf T}\,T_M(c)\,U_-\;=\;0\,,
\]
\emph{exactly} (max rel $3.9\times10^{-16}$, cross block $1.4\times10^{-16}$) on all $6$
windows with $M\le300$: the reflection-odd section used since T106 \emph{is} the compression
of the full symmetric Toeplitz section onto its antisymmetric parity sector (Basor--Ehrhardt
2009: the parity sectors are the natural objects of the Toeplitz$+$Hankel algebra, cited as the
address and never as an authority); the completed LDL$^{\mathsf T}$ counts \emph{localise} the
negative inertia --- the full section's negative eigenvalues (forced by the sign-changing
symbol, $f(0)=-29.2\ldots-6.3<0$; T148's honest negative \emph{re-read}, never re-derived) sit
entirely in the \emph{even} sector while the odd sector counts zero: $f(0)<0$ is explained
rather than worked around. Control: the sign-flipped basis does not reproduce $T-H$
($3.99\times10^{-1}$).
\item \textbf{The parity-sine calibration and the ladder certificate (T150)} \mE: the parity
sines $t_k(r)=\tfrac{2}{\sqrt N}\sin(2\pi k(r{+}1)/N)$, $N=2m{+}1$, are the exact eigenpairs
of the parity Laplacian (reflecting corner $3$, forced by antisymmetry, not chosen) at
$\mu^P_k=4\sin^2(\pi k/N)$ --- eigen-residual $2.3\times10^{-13}$ --- and the smoothness
ladder \emph{calibrates} on the exact model: $\nu^P_k=\pi k^2$ for $k=1\ldots12$ at $m=2001$
(max deviation $3.0\times10^{-5}$), so the ladder form $\nu_k\le Ck^2$ is the right question
and $\pi$ its exact floor; on every window, in the const gauge ($\varphi=\psi$ exactly ---
the ladder of the \emph{pure} Toeplitz-minus-Hankel section, no multiplier, no arithmetic
weight), the parity coefficient licence holds, $\nu^P_k\le Ck^2$ with the per-window certified
constant $C=11.70$--$17.28$, and the derived per-mode ceiling
$m\|\psi_k\|_\infty^2\le2(2\sqrt Ck+1)^2$ is a certified instance inequality --- an
$m$-free $C$ is exactly the one open input and is \emph{not} claimed. Controls: the ladder
$\times10^{-3}$ fails everywhere, a one-index calibration shift misses by $0.75$.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows --- a \emph{finite list}
of certified window inequalities with an explicit maximum; nothing uniform in the zone index
or in $D$, and explicitly \emph{no} statement for all $D$: the one open input after T150 (an
$m$-free constant $C$ in the odd-parity-sector ladder $\nu_k\le Ck^2$ for a
sign-changing-symbol Toeplitz section) stays open and typed open;
$\mathrm{TV}(\log\Lambda)$ stays withdrawn as a hypothesis (T149),
$\sigma_{\mathrm{tot}}$ stays retired as a route (T148); every T149/T150 exponent is a fit
that stays in the sandbox.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The odd-sector identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v550}}{v550})}\label{sec:v550}
The identity/certificate core of T151 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the \emph{reroute} off the
quadratic $\nu$ ladder that \vref{v549} certified --- through the pencil against the parity
Laplacian and one elementary Sobolev step, to a per-mode bound \emph{linear} in $k$
\veri{v550\_odd\_sector\_identities.py} ($19$ checks, ${\sim}0.2$\,s; promotion of the
identity/certificate pieces of T151 on $12$ frame-A windows, $n=4\ldots139$,
$m=26\ldots285\le300$, $D=7.578\times10^{-3}\ldots2.789\times10^{-2}$, with parity control
models at $m=241$ and $m=2001$ and a no-go size ladder $m=64\ldots256$; each statement carries
a mutation control that must fail by $\ge10^{-3}$).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The grid step-over and the honest negative (T151)} \mE: the parity sines live
on the \emph{shifted} grid $\theta_k=2\pi k/N$, $N=2m{+}1$, which never contains $\theta=0$,
with $\mu^P_k=2-2\cos\theta_k$ \emph{exactly} ($2.2\times10^{-16}$; eigen-residual
$2.3\times10^{-13}$); the symbol has $f(0)=-47.6\ldots-6.3<0$ (T148's honest negative,
re-read and never re-derived) with a nonempty negative window $[0,\theta_c)$, and
$\theta_c/\theta_1=0.371$--$0.485\le0.9$ on \emph{every} window: the odd grid \emph{steps
over} the negative window --- odd-sector positivity is a grid fact, stepped over rather than
cancelled. \emph{The honest negative beside it, promoted as content} (T150's rest item 3
answered negatively): the symbol-only pencil floor $\kappa_{\mathrm{sym}}(1-\rho)$ is vacuous
($\rho\ge1$) on $12/12$ windows and the symbol moves by $0.45$--$3.27$ relative across
\emph{one} mode spacing --- no pointwise symbol statement is admissible at the bottom mode's
resolution: the local model is a \emph{matrix} statement, not a symbol statement. Controls:
the Dirichlet corner breaks the eigenpairs ($1.0$), a one-index shift misses by
$6.5\times10^{-3}$.
\item \textbf{The certified bottom ladder (T151)} \mE: $\lambda_k(A)\le S\mu^P_k$ for
$k\le8$, certified per window by $8$ completed LDL$^{\mathsf T}$ inertia counts (Sylvester
1852; Bunch--Kaufman 1977 --- a certificate, never a sorted list), $S=1.1019$--$6.4725$: the
odd sector's bottom spectrum \emph{is} the parity-Laplacian ladder up to a printed $O(1)$
factor --- order $2$ in $k$, with no trace of $f(0)<0$ in it (the Rayleigh floor
$L_P\ge\mu^P_1 I$ absorbs it); the count equals the direct spectral count on all $96$
(window, $k$) pairs. Control: $S\times10^{-3}$ certifies no eigenvalue below it anywhere.
\item \textbf{The discrete Sobolev step and the $\pi$ price (T151)} \mE:
$\|\nabla\psi\|_2^2=\langle\psi,L_0\psi\rangle-\psi_{\mathrm{last}}^2$ exactly
($7.6\times10^{-15}$), $\|\nabla\psi\|_2^2\le\langle\psi,L_P\psi\rangle$, and
$\|\psi\|_\infty^2\le2\|\psi\|_2\|\nabla\psi\|_2$ on the true window modes, the parity sines
and random unit vectors --- elementary, licensed by the odd sector's \emph{virtual node}
$\psi_{-1}=0$ (Hardy--Littlewood--P\'olya 1934 / Agmon 1965 the continuum address);
calibration: on the exact parity model the pencil is $(1,1)$ (certified
$|\kappa-1|=1.1\times10^{-12}$ at $m=241$) and the Sobolev per-mode price is $\pi$ to
$5.1\times10^{-8}$ at $m=2001$ --- the honest, $m$-free cost of leaving the $\ell^2$ world.
Controls: dropping the boundary term breaks the identity ($4.8\times10^{-2}$), the Neumann
energy undercounts a first-node vector by $0.50$.
\item \textbf{The closed archimedean minimum (T151; T150's rest item 2 closed and attained)}
\mE: the archimedean lag kernel has two shape properties, checked per window and never
assumed --- $c^{\mathrm{arch}}_i<0$ for $i\ge1$ and $c^{\mathrm{arch}}_i$ non-decreasing on
$i\ge1$ --- and given those,
$\min_r\Lambda^{\mathrm{arch}}_r=c^{\mathrm{arch}}_0-c^{\mathrm{arch}}_{M-1}$ \emph{exactly}
(max rel $0.0$; value $2.1719$--$3.4674$), attained at $r=0$: a closed two-term functional of
the smooth kernel, no matrix, no eigenvector, no loss. Control: the full atom-including
kernel violates the monotone shape on every window and the closed formula misses its minimum
by $\ge8.7\times10^{-2}$.
\item \textbf{The linear per-mode bound and the no-go discriminator (T151)} \mE: with
$\kappa=0.1939$--$0.3599$ the certified pencil floor (\emph{one} completed Cholesky of
$A-\kappa L_P$ per window, the floating-point floor carried as $\mathrm{fl}/\mu^P_1$; the
direction re-read on the actual bottom eigenvalue:
$\kappa\mu^P_1\le\lambda_1(A)\le S\mu^P_1$) and $K_{\mathrm{bot}}=S$, the chain
\[
\langle\psi_k,L_P\psi_k\rangle\;\le\;\frac{\lambda_k(A)}{\kappa}
\;\le\;\frac{K_{\mathrm{bot}}\,\mu^P_k}{\kappa}
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
b_k:=m\|\psi_k\|_\infty^2\;\le\;2m\sqrt{\frac{K_{\mathrm{bot}}\,\mu^P_k}{\kappa}}
\;\le\;C_S\,k
\]
holds with $C_S=12.081$--$26.953\le2\pi\sqrt{K_{\mathrm{bot}}/\kappa}$ on the bottom $8$
modes of every window --- \emph{linear} in $k$ where the quadratic $\nu$ ladder grew
(\vref{v549}), every $m$-power cancelled, nothing additive anywhere (the $\Theta(D^3)$ bottom
that killed the Weyl / Bauer--Fike / Davis--Kahan route never enters) --- and the bound
dominates the truth $m\|\psi_k\|_\infty^2$ and the parity Dirichlet energy on every read
mode; the bottom pencil ratio $R=K_{\mathrm{bot}}/\kappa=3.7362$--$18.6607$ is the \emph{one}
scalar the chain still owes, printed per window and typed \emph{open} in $m$. \emph{The
discriminator}: on the T145 no-go form the ratio \emph{explodes} on the size ladder
($1.686\times10^{3}\to2.667\times10^{4}$, factor $15.8$ over $m=64\ldots256$) while the exact
parity model holds $R=1$ to $1.1\times10^{-12}$ --- a route that did not fail there would
prove a false statement. Controls: the ladder $\times10^{-3}$ fails against the true sups,
the inflated floor $1.5\kappa$ makes the Cholesky \emph{refuse} on $12/12$.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows --- a \emph{finite
list} of certified window inequalities with an explicit maximum; nothing uniform in the zone
index or in $D$, and explicitly \emph{no} statement for all $D$: the one open input after
T151 (the $m$-freeness of the bottom pencil ratio $R=K_{\mathrm{bot}}/\kappa$ for the odd
parity sector of a sign-changing-symbol Toeplitz section) stays open and typed open --- its
flat trend ($x^{0.037\pm0.015}$) is a fit that stays in the sandbox; the symbol-only route
stays certified vacuous; $\mathrm{TV}(\log\Lambda)$ stays withdrawn as a hypothesis (T149),
$\sigma_{\mathrm{tot}}$ stays retired as a route (T148).
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The fixed-size Ritz ceiling certificate (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v551}}{v551})}\label{sec:v551}
The certificate core of T154 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the \emph{fixed-size} replacement
for the ceiling step that \vref{v550} certified by per-window LDL$^{\mathsf T}$ counts of
size $m$ --- the sixteen-column subspace
$\mathrm{span}\{t_1..t_8\}+A^{-1}L_P\,\mathrm{span}\{t_1..t_8\}$ carries a Courant--Fischer
ceiling that \emph{attains} the inertia-certified true bottom ladder constant, so the
ceiling step needs no factorisation of size $m$ and, by direction, no residual argument at
all \veri{v551\_ritz\_ceiling\_certificate.py} ($16$ checks, ${\sim}0.4$\,s; promotion of
the certificate core of T154 on the $12$ \emph{deepest} prime-power zones admitting a
frame-A window inside the cap, $n=29\ldots139$, $m=96\ldots291\le300$,
$D=7.248\times10^{-3}\ldots1.815\times10^{-2}$ --- the deep end of the accessible surface,
mirroring T154's own surface selection and declared rather than tuned: on the shallowest
zones $n\le11$ more than one bottom direction leaves the sine block, and the fixed-depth
certificate is \emph{not} claimed there; a no-go size ladder $m=48\ldots288$, parity
controls at $m=64,128,256$, and $3$ Dirichlet control windows; each statement carries a
mutation control that must fail by $\ge10^{-3}$).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The direction lemma (T154)} \mE: for orthonormal $Q$ and $W=Q^{\mathsf T}AQ$,
$\lambda_k(A)\le\theta_k$ for \emph{every} $k\le\dim$ --- Ritz values are \emph{upper}
bounds for the eigenvalues of the \emph{same index} (Courant--Fischer 1920 / Cauchy 1829),
verified against the exact spectrum on the certificate subspace of every window and on
$24$ random subspaces (one-sided excess $0.0$) --- so the fixed-size ceiling needs
\emph{no} residual argument; Temple 1928 / Kato 1949 is a floor device and is used nowhere
in the module. Control: the \emph{reversed} reading (Ritz values as lower bounds) is
recognised as false on $12/12$ windows, $\theta_k$ overshooting $\lambda_k$ by a factor
$\ge18.6$ somewhere on every window.
\item \textbf{The sixteen-column certificate (T154)} \mE: the subspace has \emph{fixed}
dimension $16$, independent of $m$ (one Green step $A^{-1}L_Pt_k$ by Cholesky back-solves,
no inverse formed), and its ceiling $K^F=\max_k\theta_k/\mu^P_k$ ($8$ completed Choleskys
of matrices $\le8\times8$) equals $K^F=1.1019$--$1.5845$ with $K^F\ge\max_k
\lambda_k/\mu^P_k$ on every window \emph{and} $|K^F/K_{\mathrm{bot}}-1|\le9.9\times10^{-7}$
against the declared cap $10^{-4}$ on $12/12$, where $K_{\mathrm{bot}}$ is the
inertia-certified true ladder constant ($8$ completed LDL$^{\mathsf T}$ counts of size $m$
per window; count $=$ direct spectral count on all $96$ pairs): the fixed-size ceiling
\emph{attains} the truth, and the size-$m$ counts are retired from the ceiling step.
Controls: the parity sines alone overshoot by $41.6$--$739$ (failing the cap everywhere
--- T152/T153's $O(m^2)$ overshoot reproduced at fixed size), and corrupting the Green
columns ($L_Pt_k$ instead of $A^{-1}L_Pt_k$) breaks the attainment on $12/12$ (Kaniel 1966
/ Paige 1971 quoted as the mechanism, never used as a bound).
\item \textbf{The one-direction anatomy (T154)} \mE\ (angles measured): the median of the
seven aligned principal angles between the bottom eight of $A$ and the bottom eight of
$L_P$ is $0.03$--$0.14^\circ$ while the largest is $83.79$--$89.70^\circ$ on every window
(Bj\"orck--Golub 1973) --- the misalignment is carried by \emph{one} nearly orthogonal
direction, and that single direction \emph{is} the collapse price
$\lambda_1(A)/(t\,\mu^P_1)=4.408$--$7.042$ ($t=0.2250$--$0.2500$ the certified Schur
two-block floor, $k_b=16$), recovered \emph{in full} per window by one completed Cholesky
of $A-\gamma I$ (size $m$, certified, not fixed size, labelled as such): the price is a
uniformity gap, not a size gap. Control: $A=L_P$ through the same instrument returns
$K_{\mathrm{bot}}=K^F=1$ and zero misalignment (deviations $<10^{-5}$, the inertia
ladder's backoff step), with the price exactly $1/t$.
\item \textbf{The no-go discriminator (T154)} \mE: on the T145 no-go reconstruction
$c(l)=1/(1+l)$ the odd section is positive definite and the Schur floor survives
($t=0.05$ on all $4$ sizes), but $K_{\mathrm{bot}}$ explodes ($\times35.4$) and the
sixteen-column ceiling explodes \emph{with} it ($\times57.5$) over $m=48\ldots288$ ---
the instrument does not report flatness where flatness is false and manufactures no
closure; the Courant--Fischer direction is violated nowhere ($16/16$ positive-definite
cases); and the \emph{Dirichlet} control (the Hankel half removed, arithmetic kept bit
for bit) stops being positive definite --- $\lambda_1=-5.60\ldots-3.55$ certified on
$3/3$ --- so no ceiling exists there: the reflection half is load-bearing for positivity
(T154's second refutation of the boundary-reflection reading).
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows --- a \emph{finite
list} of certified window inequalities with an explicit maximum; nothing uniform in the
zone index or in $D$, and explicitly \emph{no} statement for all $D$: the attainment
$K^F=K_{\mathrm{bot}}$ is exhibited per window and \emph{not} promoted to a theorem
(T154's no-go stress shows the certificate overshoots there by $1.12$--$2.19$ --- exact
attainment is a property of the real section, not of the instrument); the two open
inputs after T154 (R1$'$, an $m$-free floor for $\lambda_{\min}(B_{HH})$ on the bulk
parity block; R2$'$, an $m$-free lower bound for the $L_P$ floor on the complement of
the eight bottom Ritz directions --- arithmetic-free, worth $91$--$100\%$ of the
collapse price) stay open and typed open; every floor consumed is certified per window
at size $m$; \vref{v550}'s ladder stays as stated, and nothing is re-opened.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The four fixed-size angle instruments (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v552}}{v552})}\label{sec:v552}
The instrument cores of T155 and T157 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the four fixed-size
instruments the angle campaign produced --- none of them closes an angle, and none is
promoted as anything but a per-instance instrument
\veri{v552\_angle\_instruments.py} ($18$ checks, ${\sim}0.4$\,s; everything recomputed on
\vref{v551}'s declared surface, the $12$ deepest prime-power zones admitting a frame-A
window inside the cap, $n=29\ldots139$, $m=96\ldots291\le300$; a no-go size ladder
$m=48\ldots288$; parity and Dirichlet controls at $m=64,128,256$; each statement carries
at least one mutation control that must fail loudly).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The complement-floor certificate (T155)} \mE:
$\min_{v\perp W}v^{\mathsf T}L_Pv\ge\mu^P_{13}-\lambda_{\max}(M^{1/2}(I-GG^{\mathsf T})
M^{1/2})$ with $M=\mathrm{diag}(\mu^P_{13}-\mu^P_k)$ and $G=T_{12}Q_W$ --- an identity
plus \emph{one} certified Rayleigh bound on the high block, a theorem for every $m$ and
every subspace, direction checked: the certificate \emph{never} exceeds the exact size-$m$
complement bottom ($12/12$) and agrees with it to $1-\mathrm{ratio}\le1.01\times10^{-3}$
against the declared cap $2\times10^{-3}$ on this small surface (the agreement tightens
with depth: T155 measured $\le2.2\times10^{-7}$ at $h=142\ldots1293$, sandbox, not
consumed here). Exactness controls in \emph{both} known configurations:
$W=\mathrm{span}\{t_1..t_8\}$ returns $\mu^P_9$ and the \emph{worthless} configuration
$W=\mathrm{span}\{t_2..t_{13}\}$ returns $\mu^P_1$, both to $2.0\times10^{-11}$ --- the
instrument reports its own worthlessness. Mutation: one corrupted overlap row moves the
certificate by $\ge0.549$, only downward.
\item \textbf{The sine-block confinement (T157)} \mE: from the certified pencil floor
$A\succeq tL_P$ (Schur two-block, $k_b=16$) and the certified ladder ceiling
$\lambda_1\le S\mu^P_1$ (\vref{v551}'s sixteen-column certificate) \emph{alone}, with
$\gamma=Te_1(A)$ the parity coordinates of the bottom eigenvector,
$\|\gamma_H\|^2\le\lambda_1/(t\,\mu^P_{17})\le(S/t)/\rho_{17}=0.0153$--$0.0245<1$ on
$12/12$: $e_1(A)$ lives $97.5$--$98.5\%$ inside the first $16$ parity sines by a
\emph{per-instance theorem} (measured tail $6.7\times10^{-6}$--$3.0\times10^{-5}$; T146's
measured ``$98$ per cent'' replaced by one line). Negative control: substituting the
pencil ceiling $\kappa$ for the ladder $S$ makes the bound \emph{vacuous}
($17.6$--$477>1$ on $12/12$, at least $997\times$ above the $S$ form) --- $\kappa$ carries
the whole atom mass, and the choice of ceiling is the whole content. Mutation: the
inflated floor $\kappa L_P$ is refuted at $e_1(A)$ itself by
$3.3\times10^{3}$--$1.0\times10^{5}$.
\item \textbf{The Schur-entry identity (T157)} \mE:
$s=\mu^P_1\,t_1^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}t_1=(B^{-1})_{11}$ exactly (worst relative
$1.1\times10^{-11}$) and $(B^{-1})_{LL}S_L=I$ to $5.8\times10^{-11}$ with
$S_L=B_{LL}-B_{LH}B_{HH}^{-1}B_{HL}$ the \emph{same} fixed-size $16\times16$ Schur
complement the T152..T157 chain already forms, with the literal-entry direction
$1/s\le(S_L)_{11}$ on $12/12$: $1/s=4.0460$--$5.8962$ is an $O(1)$ number carried by
\emph{one} fixed-size object, so T156's R2$''$ loss ceiling $r\le1/(Ls)$ is a statement
about one entry. Negative control (T157's refutation wired as a check): the
inversion-free Cauchy--Schwarz ceiling $\hat a-\|b\|^4/(b^{\mathsf T}B_{HH}b)$ is valid
and \emph{useless}, off by $250$--$7.27\times10^{3}$ ($\hat
a=1.13\times10^{3}$--$3.11\times10^{4}$ is the same entry \emph{without} the Schur
subtraction) --- the cancellation in $b^{\mathsf T}B_{HH}^{-1}b$ is nearly complete and
Cauchy--Schwarz cannot see it. Mutation: a one-index shift breaks the identity by
$1.55$--$2.15$.
\item \textbf{The adaptive Lipschitz ceiling (T157)} \mE: interval bisection with the
\emph{local} Lipschitz constant $\mathrm{lip}(a)=d/g(a)+2f/g(a)^2$ certifies
$\inf f^{\mathrm{arch}}/(4\sin^2(\theta/2))\ge t=0.25$ on $12/12$ windows in
$519$--$1201$ symbol evaluations (certified floor $0.2505$--$0.3062$, never above the
fine-grid minimum --- direction checked): the arch one-variable statement carries an
\emph{executed} certificate per window, not a grid observation. The \emph{global}
$\theta_{\mathrm{lo}}$ constant is documented insufficient (a uniform grid would need
$2.14\times10^{3}$--$7.33\times10^{4}$ points, up to $61.4\times$ the adaptive cost).
Mutation: fed a target above the true grid minimum the certificate \emph{refuses} on
$12/12$ --- it cannot be talked into certifying a false floor.
\item \textbf{The no-go discriminator and the controls} \mE: on the T145 family
$c(l)=1/(1+l)$ the certified Schur floor \emph{survives} ($t=0.05$ on all $4$ sizes)
while both new instruments break --- the confinement bound goes vacuous
($7.93$--$413>1$, $\times52.0$ over $m=48\ldots288$) and $(S_L)_{11}$ explodes

instruments do not report confinement or $O(1)$ entries where both are false. Parity
control $A=L_P$ exact to $4.9\times10^{-14}$ ($B=I$, $s=1$, zero tail); the Dirichlet
residual hits the predicted $2/\sqrt N$ to $7.4\times10^{-5}$.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows --- a \emph{finite
list} with an explicit maximum; nothing uniform in the zone index or in $D$, and
explicitly \emph{no} statement for all $D$: \emph{nothing about the angles is closed} ---
the two open terms after T157 (an $m$-free lower bound on $\hat g_1^2$, equivalently an
$m$-free upper bound on the one Schur diagonal entry $1/s$, since the resolvent route is
a theorem times that one measured fixed-size number; and an $m$-free R1$''$ domination
with a non-shrinking margin, which T157 certifies per window with a $7.3\times10^{-4}$
margin at the largest window and a \emph{shrinking} trend) stay open and typed open;
every floor $t$ and ceiling $S$ consumed is certified per window and its $m$-freeness is
exactly what remains open; \vref{v551}'s ceiling and \vref{v550}'s ladder stay as stated,
and nothing is re-opened.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The exact-form identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v553}}{v553})}\label{sec:v553}
The theorem cores of T158 and T159 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the algebra of the
sixteen-form itself --- the dual variational structure, the exact lag sum with its gauge
identity, the two closed scalars, and the one exact sign law the campaign found --- and it
closes \emph{neither} open term
\veri{v553\_exact\_form\_identities.py} ($25$ checks, ${\sim}0.2$\,s; everything recomputed
on \vref{v551}/\vref{v552}'s declared surface, the $12$ deepest prime-power zones admitting
a frame-A window inside the cap, $n=29\ldots139$, $m=96\ldots291\le300$; no-go ladders
$m=48\ldots288$ on \emph{both} T145 forms; parity and Dirichlet controls at $m=64,128,256$;
each statement carries at least one mutation control that must fail loudly).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The Thomson dual form and the positive Cholesky ladder (T158, P1)} \mE:
$s=(B^{-1})_{11}=\max_x(2x_1-x^{\mathsf T}Bx)$ (Maz'ya 1985 / Miclo 1999) with the
direction \emph{executed}, not asserted --- $8$ random trial vectors per window never
exceed $s$, so every trial is an upper bound on the entry $1/s$: exactly the variational
structure Cauchy--Schwarz lacks. The ladder $g_K=\sum_{j\le K}y_j^2$, $y=L^{-1}e_1$ from
\emph{one} Cholesky of the leading $16\times16$ block (nested Schur complements, Schur
1917 / Haynsworth 1968): all $16$ terms strictly positive, partial sums strictly monotone,
every $g_K\le s$, and $1/s\le1/g_{16}\le1/g_1=B_{11}$ literally on $12/12$; tight to
$(1/g_{16})/(1/s)=1.0642$--$1.1522$ against the declared cap $1.5$ (T158 measured
$\le1.2738$ at $h=254\ldots1393$, sandbox, not consumed here). Mutation: a $5\%$
corruption of one off-diagonal entry destroys positive definiteness --- the Cholesky
\emph{refuses} on $12/12$.
\item \textbf{The two-dimensionality (T158, P2)} \mE:
$\mathrm{span}\{t_1,A^{-1}L_Pt_1\}$ attains the Dirichlet maximum $s$ exactly ($g/s=1$ to
$9.0\times10^{-13}$ on $12/12$) for the theorem reason $L_Pt_1=\mu^P_1t_1$ (KMS 1953;
eigenpair residual $8.1\times10^{-13}$) --- the entry is a \emph{two-dimensional} quantity
the moment one Green column is granted. Negative controls: $\mathrm{span}\{t_1,t_2\}$ (no
Green column) misses $s$ by a factor $1.42$--$4.8$, and the corrupted Green column
$L_Pt_1$ (no solve) misses by $255$--$7.7\times10^{3}$.
\item \textbf{The gauge identity and the TmH signature (T159, P4/P7)} \mE: the section map
annihilates constant lag vectors \emph{entrywise with zero tolerance}
($\mathrm{odd\_toeplitz}(\mathbf 1)=0$ exactly --- the mechanism in one line), hence the
gauge identity $\sum_d w_d=0$ holds to $1.1\times10^{-14}$ of $\sup|w|$ for the per-window
optimiser and $3$ random sixteen-vectors: the form is \emph{blind} to the lag mass of $c$,
and the lag mass is exactly where the arch and atom halves of the sixteen-form are of size
$h^2$ and cancel. The premise --- the Toeplitz-minus-Hankel signature
$A_{r,s}-A_{r+1,s+1}=f(r+s)$ --- is constant along every anti-diagonal to
$1.4\times10^{-16}$. Mutations: a one-index Hankel shift breaks the gauge identity by
$2.7\times10^{-7}$--$4.2\times10^{-5}$; the T145 form $R=aa^{\mathsf T}+\varepsilon I$ has
signature defect $7.4\times10^{-2}$ --- not a parity section, the gauge identity is not
even \emph{defined} for it.
\item \textbf{The exact lag sum and the two closed scalars (T159, P2/P5)} \mE:

\subsection{The sampling/harmonics identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v554}}{v554})}\label{sec:v554}
The closed theorem cores of T160 and T161 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): what the sixteen-form
\emph{pairs against} --- the atom half as a $\Lambda$-weighted sampling at the Fourier
harmonics of the log-window, the closed moment laws and the total-variation theorem of the
smooth half, the closed head split of the archimedean kernel with its scale-free Bernstein
rate, and the certified off-diagonal fraction bound that replaces the refuted sign law ---
and it closes \emph{no} open term
\veri{v554\_sampling\_harmonics\_identities.py} ($21$ checks, ${\sim}0.5$\,s; everything
recomputed on \vref{v551}--\vref{v553}'s declared surface, the $12$ deepest prime-power
zones admitting a frame-A window inside the cap, $n=29\ldots139$, $m=96\ldots291\le300$,
plus a declared $\Lambda$-battery of six log-spaced cut-offs $X=10^{3}\ldots3.2\times10^{5}$
for the PNT item --- finite von-Mangoldt sums only, no matrix anywhere; each statement
carries at least one mutation control that must fail loudly).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The sampling identity (T160, P2)} \mE:
$\sum_d c^{\mathrm{atom}}_d\,w_d=-\tfrac12\sum_{n\le X}(2\Lambda(n)/\sqrt n)\,
\widehat w(\log n)$ (plus one reflected term below the grid), $\widehat w$ the linear
interpolant of the lag weights --- exact to $5.6\times10^{-15}$ of the absolute atom scale
on $12/12$ windows: the atom half of the pairing \emph{is} a $\Lambda$-weighted sampling at
the prime-power positions, hence identically a finite combination of sums
$\sum_n\Lambda(n)\,n^{-1/2}\cos(t\log n)$ at $32$ explicit frequencies. Mutation: a
one-index shift of the sampling grid breaks by $5.1\times10^{-5}$--$3.1\times10^{-3}$.
\item \textbf{The moment laws and the TV theorem (T160, P1/P4)} \mE: $m_0=\sum_d w_d=0$
($1.0\times10^{-16}$ of $\|w\|_1$), $m_1=\sum_d d\,w_d=-[S_0^2+2\sum_jP_j^2]$
($9.2\times10^{-16}$) and $m_2=\sum_d d^2w_d=-[2S_1-(M{-}1)S_0]^2$ ($3.4\times10^{-14}$, a
perfect square), both sign-definite forms strictly negative on every window; and U3 as a
\emph{theorem with checked hypotheses} ($c^{\mathrm{arch}}\le0$ and monotone on $d\ge1$,
checked on $12/12$, never assumed): $\mathrm{TV}(c^{\mathrm{arch}})=3.9817$--$4.8991\le
|c^{\mathrm{arch}}_0|+2\sup_{d\ge1}|c^{\mathrm{arch}}_d|<6$, a closed window-independent
constant. Mutations: a one-index prefix shift breaks $m_1$ by $\ge1.25\times10^{-2}$, an
$(M{-}2)$ mis-normalisation breaks $m_2$ by $\ge6.1\times10^{-2}$, and the full
atom-including kernel violates the monotone hypothesis on $12/12$.
\item \textbf{The harmonic-frequency theorem and the PNT main term (T161, P3)} \mE:
$t_j\,(2\alpha)=2\pi j$ exactly ($2.8\times10^{-14}$) on every window and every battery
cut-off --- the $32$ frequencies are precisely the Fourier harmonics of the log-window
$[0,2\alpha]$, so the atom half is the vector of the first $32$ Fourier coefficients of the
measure $\sum_n(2\Lambda(n)/\sqrt n)\,\delta_{\log n}$; at those frequencies
$\theta=2\pi j$ collapses the partial-summation main term to the closed, parameter-free
prediction $(\sqrt X-1)/(\tfrac14+t^2)$ (de la Vall\'ee Poussin 1896; the Mellin factor of
$x^{-1/2}$), and on the battery the finite sums agree with it to $0.0007$--$0.097$ of the
trivial mass against the declared cap $0.12$, the subtraction reducing the aggregate
residual to $0.008$--$0.466\le0.5$ of $\sum|S|$ on every cut-off. Mutations: a wrong Mellin
pole worsens the aggregate residual by $\times1.8$--$\times95.8$, and a mass-matched
\emph{uniform} fake measure misses by $0.23$--$0.51\ge1.5\times$ the cap --- the agreement
is a property of the von-Mangoldt measure, not of any measure with the same mass.
\item \textbf{The head split and the scale-free Bernstein rate (T161, P1)} \mE:
$c^{\mathrm{arch}}_d=\Psi_d+D\,\widehat G(dD,D)$ with
$\Psi_d=-\tfrac12[(d{+}1)\log(d{+}1)-2d\log d+(d{-}1)\log(d{-}1)]$ closed, $D$-free and
$m$-free (the triangle-smeared simple pole; the $\log D$ cancels identically) and
$\widehat G$ the smear of the symbolically regularised $g_{\mathrm{reg}}=g-1/(2w)$ ---
exact to $3.2\times10^{-16}$ of $\sup|c^{\mathrm{arch}}|$ at every lag of every window, the
two $\Psi$ representations agreeing to $2.9\times10^{-14}$; and
$\rho^*=(3+\sqrt5)/2=2.618034$: the root of $x^2-3x+1$ ($0.0$), returned exactly by the
$D\to0$ limit of the peeled interval $[0.4\alpha,2\alpha]$, invariant under $\alpha\times10$
(it depends only on the interval ratio $5$), every window's $\rho(D)=2.588$--$2.608$ below
it (Bernstein 1912). Mutations: dropping $\Psi$ misses $c^{\mathrm{arch}}$ by
$0.99$--$1.00$; the wrong interval ratio moves the limit to $3.0$.
\item \textbf{The off-diagonal fraction bound and the sign refutation (T161, P2)} \mE: the
gauge identity licenses one boundary-free Abel step and
$Q^{\mathrm{arch}}=\sum_{k,l}a_ka_l\sum_{d\ge1}(\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}})_d\,R^1_{kl}(d)$
exactly ($2.0\times10^{-13}$); the certified per-window inequality is
$|\text{off-diagonal block}|\le\tfrac14\,|Q^{\mathrm{arch}}|$ (measured $0.171$--$0.212$ on

\item \textbf{The no-go discriminator and the controls} \mE: the head split is a statement

$1.0\times10^{-14}$ (KMS 1953); $\mathrm{odd\_toeplitz}(c^L)=L_P$ at zero tolerance.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows --- a \emph{finite
list} with an explicit maximum; nothing uniform in the zone index or in $D$; finite

fraction bound, Fej\'er 1915 / Schur 1917), R-C$'$ (\emph{one} split of the pairing with
$\delta_{\mathrm{eff}}<\tfrac12$; T161 refutes the arch/atom and arch+smooth/fluctuation

\subsection{The Pareto/total-variation identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v555}}{v555})}\label{sec:v555}
The closed theorem cores of T162 and T163 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the \emph{price
structure} of the pairing --- the exchange law that makes demand and price two coordinates
of one object, the total-variation floor that closes the flat-price route in the parity
sector, the chain-derived price axis of the Fej\'er knob, the Mellin cell moments and the
boundary-free Abel step with its closed loss reason, and the Lerch/Frullani log-moment on
three independent routes --- and it closes no open term beyond the negative closure of
R-C$'''$ that the floor inequality itself is
\veri{v555\_pareto\_tv\_identities.py} ($23$ checks, ${\sim}0.4$\,s; everything recomputed
on \vref{v551}--\vref{v554}'s declared surface, the $12$ deepest prime-power zones
admitting a frame-A window inside the cap, $n=29\ldots139$, $m=96\ldots291\le300$; the one
arithmetic input $\kappa=0.038821$ \emph{verified} at every jump point of $\psi(x)/x$ on
the von-Mangoldt table in $[100,3.2\times10^{5}]$, reproduced to $4.2\times10^{-7}$; each
statement carries at least one mutation control that must fail loudly).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The exchange law and the crossing criterion (T163, R1.2)} \mE:
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}(x)=\tfrac12+\log\!\bigl(2\kappa\,g_{16}\,\mathrm{TV}(x)/P(x)\bigr)/\log X$
is an identity at all $612$ grid points of the declared Fej\'er knob ($50$ geometric
$\sigma$ on $[1,4096]$ plus $\infty$, $12$ windows; $5.1\times10^{-16}$ relative,
admissibility $Q(x)>0$ everywhere), and the crossing criterion
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}(x)<\tfrac12\iff P(x)>2\kappa\,g_{16}\,\mathrm{TV}(x)$ holds as an
exact equivalence at every point: price and demand are two coordinates on \emph{one}
object, and the crossing price is a closed formula. Mutation: the wrong constant
($\kappa$ for $2\kappa$) moves the law by $6.5\times10^{-2}$--$3.4$ at every grid point.
\item \textbf{The total-variation floor (T163, R2.2 --- the theorem that carries the
verdict)} \mE: (T1) $w_0(x)=\|a(x)\|^2$ to $4.9\times10^{-16}$ (the parity rows are
orthonormal); (T2) $\mathrm{TV}(x)\ge|w_0(x)|$ by telescoping with $w_M=0$; (T3) the
normalisation $x_1=1$ forces $\|a\|^2\ge1/\mu^P_1$, hence
$\mu^P_1\,\mathrm{TV}(x)=5.00$--$28.84\ge1$ on all $708$ trial vectors built in the module
($51$ knob settings plus $8$ random admissible sixteen-vectors per window), against the
closed floor $1/\mu^P_1=1/(4\sin^2(\pi/N))=943.6$--$8609.6\sim h^2$; (T4) with the
crossing criterion, every sub-$\tfrac12$ grid point pays
$P>2\kappa g_{16}/\mu^P_1=15.4$--$142.8$ (all $54$ sub-$\tfrac12$ points respect it) ---
a flat-price sub-$\tfrac12$ demand is impossible in the parity sector on this surface,
the inequality that closes R-C$'''$ negatively. Negative control: the \emph{inadmissible}
vector $0.01\,x^*$ ($x_1\ne1$) does undercut the floor
($\mu^P_1\mathrm{TV}=2.5$--$2.9\times10^{-3}$) and is recognised as inadmissible --- the
floor is a property of the normalisation meeting the smallest parity eigenvalue
(Kac--Murdock--Szeg\H{o} 1953), not of the machinery.
\item \textbf{The chain-derived price axis (T163, R1.0)} \mE: $\sigma=1$ gives $x=e_1$
exactly with $P=g_{16}/g_1$ (the $K=1$ rung of the T158 Cholesky ladder, the T157
route-(0) certificate; $4.1\times10^{-16}$) and $\sigma=\infty$ gives
$g_{16}\,Q(x^*)=1$ (the $K=16$ top rung; $1.2\times10^{-12}$) --- the Fej\'er sweep is a
path between two certificates the chain already owns; the ladder carries all $16$ terms
strictly positive with strictly monotone partial sums, and the knob is monotone in both
coordinates on every window (the knob curve \emph{is} the Pareto front). Mutation: a
corrupted off-diagonal sixteen-block entry makes the Cholesky \emph{refuse} on $12/12$.
\item \textbf{The Mellin cell moments and the Abel step (T162, C2/C5)} \mE: the $k$-th
rung of the archimedean Mellin ladder is the closed sum $\sum_dw_d\,C_d(-(2k+\tfrac12))$
with $C_d(s)$ the exact tent integral (Mellin 1896), reproduced by an independent
per-cell Gauss--Legendre quadrature to $2.8\times10^{-13}$ on every rung $k=1\ldots4$
(shifted tent centres break by $\ge1.3\times10^{-2}$); the boundary-free Abel identities
hold at levels $k=1\ldots3$ to $8.3\times10^{-17}$ (Abel 1826), the dropped-boundary
level-$1$ form --- the one the chain uses --- agrees because the gauge identity kills the
boundary term exactly, the optimal level is \emph{one} for T162's closed reason (net
factor $32\pi/\alpha=40.6$--$59.4>1$, confirmed by the measured level-$2$/level-$1$
bound ratio $30.8$--$69.1>1$), and a gauge violation breaks the dropped form by its
closed prediction $v_0c_0M$ to $1.2\times10^{-15}$ --- T162's positive control.
\item \textbf{The Lerch/Frullani log-moment (T162, R-A$'$)} \mE: $L=\sum_d\Psi_dw_d$
agrees on three independent routes on every window --- the direct sum with $\Psi_d$
closed; the double-Abel form \emph{with} its Wronskian boundary term
$-\tfrac12M\log M\,w_{M-1}$ ($2.8\times10^{-14}$; dropping the term breaks by
$2.2\times10^{-4}$--$1.3\times10^{-2}$); and the Lerch/Frullani integral with the $d=1$
term peeled in closed form ($1.8\times10^{-15}$; $44$ declared panels) --- the peel
constant $\int_0^\infty((1-e^{-y})/y)^2dy=2\log2$ reproduced to $2.2\times10^{-16}$ and

\item \textbf{The no-go staircase and the controls} \mE: coarsening the lag grid over
$\nu=4/2/1/0.5$ degrades the arch/atom cancellation \emph{monotonically} in the median
(damage $1.00\to3.49\to10.81\to24.98$, the $\nu=4$ column an exact null control) --- the
T145 resolution no-go breaks monotonically in the collision rate; the closed Dirichlet
cosine-sum identity to $2.4\times10^{-14}$ including the degenerate branch; KMS
eigenpairs to $1.4\times10^{-14}$; $\mathrm{odd\_toeplitz}(c^L)=L_P$ at zero tolerance.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows --- a \emph{finite
list} with an explicit maximum; nothing uniform in the zone index or in $D$; the T163
$h$-exponents ($P_{\mathrm{aff}}\sim h^{3.05}$, $P_{\mathrm{cross}}\sim h^{1.91}$, the
TV exponent $\sim h^{2.00}$) are sandbox fits and are \emph{not} consumed --- what is
consumed is the closed per-window floor; finite $\Lambda$-sums are allowed and used,
\emph{no} RH statement is made ($\tfrac12$ appears in exactly one role: as the strength
of a classical statement a required depth is compared against); the open terms after
T163 --- R-E (the successor, both arms prime-free: a growing $1/s$ ceiling for the
downstream chain, or a sector whose gap does not vanish like $h^{-2}$), R-B$'''$ (an
$h$-uniform positivity margin), R-D (a fifth R1$''$ device) --- stay open and typed
open; \vref{v554}'s identities stay as stated, and nothing is re-opened.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The gauge/\texorpdfstring{$P_{\mathrm{pr}}$}{Ppr} identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v556}}{v556})}\label{sec:v556}
The closed theorem cores of T164 and T165 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the \emph{gauge
structure} of the pairing --- the theorem that the entry normalisation is a gauge, the
exact conservation law that no sector shift can remove the $h^2$, the linearity that makes
the chain spend its entry ceiling at power exactly one, the gauge-invariant
$P_{\mathrm{pr}}$ identity that closes the successor question R-F by certificate, and the
Schur-cascade direction with its exact exponent closure --- and it does not close the one
remaining quantifier
\veri{v556\_gauge\_ppr\_identities.py} ($23$ checks, ${\sim}0.3$\,s; everything recomputed
on \vref{v551}--\vref{v555}'s declared surface, the $12$ deepest prime-power zones
admitting a frame-A window inside the cap, $n=29\ldots139$, $m=96\ldots291\le300$; the one
arithmetic input $\kappa=0.038821$ \emph{verified} at every jump point of $\psi(x)/x$ on
the von-Mangoldt table in $[100,3.2\times10^{5}]$; each statement carries at least one
mutation control that must fail loudly).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The gauge theorem (T164, S2.1)} \mE: $x_1=1$ fixes $a_1=1/\sqrt{\mu_1}$,
i.e.\ only the \emph{scale} of $a$; $Q$ and TV are homogeneous of degree two in $a$;
hence the demand ratio $Q/\mathrm{TV}$ of the same $a$-direction --- and with it
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}$ --- is the \emph{same number in every sector}: unchanged to
$2.9\times10^{-11}$ on $2520$ sector-by-trial-vector combinations ($5$ weight families
$\times$ $7$ shifts $\times$ $6$ Fej\'er taper widths on $12$ windows), with
$\mathrm{TV}\ge|w_0|$ in every sector and the pure shift scaling the certified value by
exactly $\theta=\mu^P_1/(\mu^P_1+\kappa_s)$ ($2.2\times10^{-11}$ on $432$ points) ---
the crossing criterion $Q/\mathrm{TV}>2\kappa$ contains no normalisation and cannot be
moved by \emph{any} sector change; candidate (i) is settled in closed form (the
unprojected spectrum has $\mu_0=0$ exactly, the lowest remaining eigenvalue is
$\le\mu^P_1$ on $12/12$ --- the full space is strictly worse). Mutation: the wrong
transport map (the $x$-coordinates carried unchanged instead of the $a$-direction)
moves the ratio by $2.0\times10^{2}$--$5.4\times10^{3}$.
\item \textbf{The $h^2$ conservation law (T164, S2.2)} \mE:
floor${}\times{}$transfer $=1/(\mu^P_1+\kappa_s)\cdot(1+\kappa_s/\mu^P_1)=1/\mu^P_1$
\emph{identically} at every shift on the declared grid ($72$ window-by-shift points,

\item \textbf{The power-one spend as an identity (T164, S1)} \mE: the $r$-ceiling of the

per instance from the full window --- \emph{linear} in the entry ceiling $U$, so

\item \textbf{The $P_{\mathrm{pr}}$ identity and the predicate equivalence (T165, T1 ---

\subsection{The cascade/vector identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v557}}{v557})}\label{sec:v557}
The closed theorem cores of T166 and T167 (Section~\ref{sec:phase2}): the \emph{anatomy of
the cascade} and the \emph{exactness of the closed vector at $K=2$} --- the prefix / minor /
regression identities that make the sixteen rungs closed objects of the raw arithmetic Gram
block, the diagonal invariance that makes the gain blind to the KMS normalisation, the exact
$K=2$ identity that makes the fast-null-vector free (the third dress collapses onto the
second), the pivot identity that makes every candidate excess an exact number, the
unification that makes the three dresses \emph{one} inequality, and the trial theorem with
the $L_P$ no-go and the scramble type-change as must-breaks --- and it does not close the one
remaining scalar
\veri{v557\_cascade\_vector\_identities.py} ($23$ checks, ${\sim}0.1$\,s; everything
recomputed on \vref{v551}--\vref{v556}'s declared surface, the $12$ deepest prime-power zones
admitting a frame-A window inside the cap, $n=29\ldots139$, $m=96\ldots291\le300$; the one
arithmetic input $\kappa=0.038821$ \emph{verified} at every jump point of $\psi(x)/x$ on the
von-Mangoldt table in $[100,3.2\times10^{5}]$; each statement carries at least one mutation
control that must fail loudly).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The cascade identities (T166, U1)} \mE: with $Q_K$ the leading $K\times K$
block of the normalised sixteen-block and $G=TAT^{\mathsf T}$ the raw arithmetic Gram
block --- the \emph{prefix} property ($g_K=\sum_{j\le K}y_j^2$ from \emph{one} Cholesky
equals the per-$K$ direct solves $e_1^{\mathsf T}Q_K^{-1}e_1$ at every $K=1\ldots16$;
$192$ comparisons, $1.1\times10^{-12}$), the \emph{minor} form
$1/g_K=\det G_{[1..K]}/(\mu^P_1\det G_{[2..K]})$ in log space to $2.7\times10^{-12}$ on
$36$ (window, $K$) pairs, $K\in\{2,6,16\}$ (the rungs are ratios of consecutive Gram
minors of the \emph{raw} block --- closed objects, not factorisation outputs; Schur 1917
/ Haynsworth 1968), and the \emph{regression} form $g_K/g_1=1/(1-R_K^2)$ with $R_K^2$
the squared multiple correlation of mode $1$ on modes $2\ldots K$
($8.8\times10^{-13}$) --- the open object \emph{is} a near-collinearity statement.
Mutation: the minor with the wrong row/column deleted misses by $0.99$--$1.45$.
\item \textbf{The diagonal invariance (T166, I4)} \mE: the gain
$g_K/g_1=B_{11}(Q_K^{-1})_{11}$ is unchanged under $B\to DBD$ on $144$ random positive
diagonals across $K\in\{2,6,16\}$ ($2.7\times10^{-12}$): the cascade does \emph{not} see
the KMS $1/\sqrt{\mu}$ normalisation --- the gain, and with it the whole $h^3$ of the
sandbox surface, is a property of the arithmetic Gram block alone (Kac--Murdock--Szeg\H{o}
1953 enters only through the spectrum). Mutation: a non-diagonal congruence moves the
gain by $2.7$--$3.8$.
\item \textbf{The exact $K=2$ identity (T167, V1 --- the central positive result)} \mE:
the \emph{closed} vector $u=(1,-Q_{21}/Q_{22})$ \emph{attains} the constrained minimum
on every window --- $u^{\mathsf T}Q_2u=1/g_2=Q_{11}(1-r_{12}^2)$ to
$1.1\times10^{-12}$ with $r_{12}^2=Q_{12}^2/(Q_{11}Q_{22})$, and
$B_{11}g_2=1/(1-r_{12}^2)$ \emph{identically} to $1.2\times10^{-12}$ (measured

$4r_{12}^2/(1-r_{12}^2)=6.7\times10^{2}$--$1.5\times10^{4}$.
\item \textbf{The pivot identity and the unification (T167, V1/V4)} \mE: for

$u^{\mathsf T}Q_Ku=1/g_K+\delta^{\mathsf T}Q_K\delta$ \emph{exactly}
($2.0\times10^{-12}$ on $252$ evaluations across three $\delta$ scales) --- every

\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Per instance on small windows --- a \emph{finite
list} with an explicit maximum; nothing uniform in the zone index or in $D$; the

scramble discriminator as must-breaks --- and it does not close that scalar
\veri{v558\_bilinear\_rank\_identities.py} ($27$ checks, ${\sim}0.2$\,s; everything
recomputed on \vref{v551}--\vref{v557}'s declared surface, the $12$ deepest prime-power zones
admitting a frame-A window inside the cap, $n=29\ldots139$, $m=96\ldots291\le300$; the one
arithmetic input $\kappa=0.038821$ \emph{verified} at every jump point of $\psi(x)/x$ on the
von-Mangoldt table in $[100,3.2\times10^{5}]$; each statement carries at least one mutation
control that must fail loudly).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]

identity $\hat a_{ij}=t_i^{\mathsf T}A_ht_j=\sum_d c_dW^{ij}_d$ with the closed T163
correlation weights, the $1/\sqrt{\mu}$-normalised block equal to

\emph{Euclidean orthogonality} $t_1\cdot t_2=0$ to $4.4\times10^{-16}$ --- the
near-parallelism $1-r_{12}^2\to0$ of the whole programme is created \emph{entirely} by
the arithmetic metric $A_h$ and not at all by the vectors; the \emph{Wronskian
telescope} $(\mu_1-\mu_2)u_rv_r=W_{r-1}-W_r$ with $W_r=u_{r+1}v_r-u_rv_{r+1}$ and
$W_{-1}=W_{h-1}=0$ (the telescope closes at the window edge; $1.9\times10^{-17}$), and

Mutation: dropping the $|\hat a_{12}|$ term fails on every window
($\nu_1-\max(\hat a_{11},\hat a_{22})=0.30$--$1.17>0$).

collapses in closed form,
$R(K7)=2\sqrt{\hat a_{11}\hat a_{22}}\,\det\hat A/[(\hat a_{11}+\hat a_{22})
(\sqrt{\hat a_{11}\hat a_{22}}+\hat a_{12})]$ ($8.7\times10^{-13}$) --- it meets the

\item \textbf{The rank-3 theorem and the Type II collapse (T170, TH4--TH5)} \mE: the

The capstone \emph{verifies the map and claims nothing new} (T171, contract

question through sixteen exact reformulations to \emph{one} object (R1); T171 reproduced
every link of that reduction in one connected sandbox run; this module is the
load-bearing version of that run --- the whole sixteen-link chain as one machine-checked
pass ($13$ links \textsc{theorem}: algebra for every $h$, checked on instances; $3$ links

classified dead route exhibited failing on an instance exactly as classified), and the
precision ledger with both self-similarity identities --- and it adds \emph{zero} new
uniform-in-$m$ statements, which is precisely why it is promotable
\veri{v559\_phase2\_capstone.py} ($35$ checks, ${\sim}0.3$\,s; everything recomputed on
\vref{v551}--\vref{v558}'s declared surface, the $12$ deepest prime-power zones admitting a

fact about finite matrices, never routed through the Weil criterion).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The chain, sixteen links in one pass} \mE: (1) the T152 Schur two-block

is an argument of any observable).

\subsection{The dense-limit identities (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v562}}{v562})}\label{sec:v562}
The exact cores of the phase-2 endgame (T176 \texttt{DENSE.LIMIT},
Section~\ref{sec:t176}) --- the probe that raised the sieve twentyfold, extended the
deficit(dens) curve to a densest bin consistent with zero, and closed the phase-2
measurement programme as planned. This module carries the identities, not the
measurement: everything is recomputed per instance on a small declared surface, and
the big sieve is \emph{not} rebuilt --- the identities are sieve-size-free, which is
their point \veri{v562\_dense\_limit\_identities.py} ($16$ checks, ${\sim}0.5$\,s,
deterministic; $18$ prime-power anchors in $[40,565]$ crossed with the declared
$2^{1/4}$ ladder $h=(128,152,181,215,256,304)$ $=108$ cells, comb complete, positive
definite on $108/108$; the one arithmetic input $\kappa=0.038821$ verified at every
jump point of $\psi(x)/x$ on the table).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{R1 closed: the Feynman--Hellmann identity} \mE\ (T176 P2, the
strongest): $d\log R/d\delta=v^{\mathsf T}d\tilde Av/\lambda_{\min}
-w^{\mathsf T}d\tilde Aw/\lambda_{\max}-d\mathrm{DEL}/\mathrm{DEL}$, with $d\tilde A$
the odd-Toeplitz image of the \emph{exact} lag derivative $dc/d\delta$ (the assembly
moves $0.5\mu_p$ per unit phase between two adjacent lag cells and nothing else;
piecewise linearity checked at $7.0\times10^{-12}$ of the increment), reproduces the
full nonlinear rebuild on $6/6$ declared instances at the minimum of the declared
step ladder ($2.3\times10^{-7}$ at $\delta=10^{-6}$; T176's own optimum
$3.37\times10^{-6}$) \emph{with the U-shape exhibited} --- round-off limited below,
truncation limited above, both $\ge3\times$ the minimum: a wrong formula has a floor,
not a minimum (mutations --- swapped eigenvectors, dropped
$d\mathrm{DEL}/\mathrm{DEL}$ --- miss by a factor $4\times10^{1}$ while the true form
sits at $5\times10^{-8}$). T175's measured intervention slope ($879$) is retired as a
separate claim, and the decomposition corrects the expected story: the near-degeneracy
channel $d\mathrm{DEL}/\mathrm{DEL}$ carries the largest share on every instance
($0.54$--$0.98$; T176: $84\%$ median).
\item \textbf{The phase pole} \mE\ (T176 P3): on the densest declared instances,
positive definiteness survives only $2\%$ of the phase period (declared $64$-point
grid, bisection to $40$ levels), the loss point satisfies
$\delta_{\mathrm{PD}}\cdot|d\log R/d\delta|=7.2$ median --- inside the declared
$O(1)$ band, a pole at the natural scale --- and the two lowest modes of the
normalised low block sit within $0.02$--$0.17$ of each other already at $\delta=0$:
the intervention walks along a crossing, it does not create one. The ${\sim}300\times$
harmonic anomaly of T175 is \emph{retired}: a first-harmonic regression over the
period estimates a Fourier coefficient of a function with a pole in the interval.
\item \textbf{Sieve consistency at construction level} \mE\ (T176 P4): a bigger sieve
adds atoms above the old cap and nothing else, so on anchors whose comb is complete
under the old cap the lag vectors agree \emph{bit for bit}, $R$ exactly, and the
cluster-robust bin deficit identically; the must-break moves exactly where it must
(the deepest declared anchor past the old cap). T176's cell-by-cell audit --- all six
T175 bins at $0.0\sigma$ under the $20.8\times$ sieve --- is this construction fact
plus statistics, and it is what lets any later probe raise the cap without
re-deriving the chain.
\item \textbf{The estimator $+$ the anti-promotion as a check} \mE\ (T176 P1): the
cluster-robust bin statistic is deterministic and exactly reproducible under a
permuted cell order --- and it is \emph{ladder-dependent}, exhibited per instance
(fine $2^{1/4}$ vs coarse $\sqrt2$ ladder shift $0.036$ on the module surface; T176
saw up to $0.20$): \textbf{any ledger row quoting a bin deficit must quote the rung
ladder with it}, and \texttt{PRIME.DENSE.LIMIT.01} does exactly that. The
occupancy-preserving phase scramble destroys positive definiteness on $6/6$ draws
(T176: $194/194$) --- a one-sided destruction control, never a calibrated null.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} T176's \textsc{sits-at-zero} verdict ---
pooled $+0.0496\pm0.0372$ over the two new bins, plateau window $0.074$ at $2\sigma$,
a $3.6\times$ narrowing --- stays a sandbox \textsc{measured} number on T176's
$2.5\times10^{7}$ surface \emph{with its rung ladder} (the ladder caveat is part of
the quote); the limit stays open and typed open (true zero at finite density,
power-law approach and low plateau remain indistinguishable under any
resource-reachable sieve --- one more decade of window would cost
$\mathtt{ATOM\_MAX}\sim2.5\times10^{9}$); the phase-2 closure is a closure of the
\emph{measurement programme}, not of the question; no RH statement anywhere, and the
open quantifier at link 16 is untouched.
\end{itemize}

\subsection{The relative pencil one-mode structure (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v569}}{v569})}\label{sec:v569}
The same declared surface, read through a new exact lens
\veri{v569\_lambda\_pencil\_onemode.py} ($6$ checks, ${\sim}2$\,s; construction
base: the T170 frame-A scan of \vref{v563}, imported read-only, bit for bit).
The rank-3 polarisation of Paper~II is exactly $(2{+}1)$-Lorentz geometry, and
the low $2\times2$ block carries the relative pencil $Z=B^{-1}S$ with the exact
identities $\det(B-S)=\det B\,(1-\lambda_1)(1-\lambda_2)$,
$D(B,S)=\det B\,(\lambda_1{+}\lambda_2)$, $\det S=\det B\,\lambda_1\lambda_2$
(proved symbolically in the parabolic self-code module; here executed on the
real surface at worst residual $2\times10^{-14}$ across all $70$ windows).

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The labels, corrected honestly} (\textsc{measured}): the \emph{locking} mode is
$\lambda_2$, hugging $1$ (median $1.000021$, range $[-0.85,\,1.0005]$), while
the spectator $\lambda_1$ is large --- $[4.53,\,180.64]$, every window above
$1$. (The review that motivated the question guessed the separated mode
\emph{below} $1$; on the real surface it sits far above.)
\item \textbf{The one-mode answer} (\textsc{measured}): $\min|1-\lambda_1|=3.53$ across all
$70$ windows, so $\det(I-Z)/(1-\lambda_2)=1-\lambda_1$ is uniformly bounded
away from zero on the reachable surface and the two-dimensional cancellation
reduces to the \emph{single scalar} $1-\lambda_2$: verdict \textsc{one-mode}.
\item \textbf{The reference window} \mE: on $h=540$ the locking factor is
$1-\lambda_2=-2.27\times10^{-5}$ and the pencil reproduces
$\det\hat A=4.22\times10^{-3}$ --- the $4.7$-order cancellation of Paper~II

explodes $|1-\lambda_2|$ by $\times1.9\times10^{6}$ and destroys the pencil
geometry (both eigenvalues negative) while every identity keeps holding: the
locking is arithmetic placement, not an identity artefact.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} Declared finite surface only ---
Problem~7.1 of Paper~II (the uniform quantifier) is \emph{untouched}: its
structure is typed (one scalar mode), not bounded; whether $\lambda_1$ stays
separated as $h$ grows is a new named open question, strictly weaker than

\subsection{The separation floor, certified (\texorpdfstring{\vref{v570}}{v570})}\label{sec:v570}
The open question \vref{v569} left behind, reduced and certified on the
surface \veri{v570\_separation\_floor.py} ($8$ checks, ${\sim}13$\,s;
construction base: the same T170 frame-A scan, read-only). Two one-line
theorems --- $P=\det Z=\det S/\det B>0$ and $T=\operatorname{tr}Z>0$ give
$\lambda_1\ge\sqrt P$ (since $\lambda_1^2-P=\lambda_1(\lambda_1-\lambda_2)$),
and $P\le0$ gives $\lambda_1=T-\lambda_2\ge T$ --- turn the spectator
separation into a \emph{closed per-window floor}.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.5em]
\item \textbf{The certification} \mE: on all $70$ declared windows the floor
is sound and clears the margin, $\min F=2.130\ge1.05$ --- the \vref{v569}
separation is no longer only a measured eigenvalue fact, it follows from
$\det S/\det B$ and $\operatorname{tr}Z$ alone (conservative against the
measured $\min\lambda_1=4.534$, as a floor should be).
\item \textbf{The dominance} (\textsc{measured}): $P=\det S/\det B$ lies in
$[4.5,\,120.6]$ (median $30.1$) and \emph{grows} with depth (log-log slope
$+0.900$ in $h$, with its surface ladder); the exact link
$1-T+P=\det(B-S)/\det B$ makes trace and determinant dominance one question.
\item \textbf{The cheap route is dead} \mE\ (honest negative): $\det S$ is
itself a pair-level cancellation object --- Cauchy--Binet exact, negative
pair mass up to $13.7\times\det S$ (median $8.0\times$), best single-pair
witness only $0.13$--$0.34\times\det B$ against the $\ge1.10$ it would need:
no two-atom witness certifies the dominance.
\item \textbf{Must-break} \mE: the position scramble flips the trace sign
($T=-78.28$ against $+32.15$ real) --- the $T>0$ gate detects the destroyed
geometry loudly; the dominance is arithmetic placement.
\item \textbf{Named limits as content.} The $h$-uniform dominance
$\det S\ge(1+c)^2\det B$ is the \emph{same} open question \vref{v569} named,
now in sharper closed-scalar form --- typed as pair-level
size-vs-cancellation (an $8{:}9$ cancellation, not a $4.7$-order one, but
not free); Problem~7.1 untouched; no rate, no bound, no RH statement.
\end{itemize}
