\subsection{The mode ladder and the parity mechanism (T150)}
T150 (\texttt{mode\_ladder\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{MODE.LADDER}, $36/36$, $48.0$\,s on
$72$ prime-power windows $m=50\ldots1393$, verdict \textsc{one-term-missing}, the verdict rule
wired constructively: ``proved'' cannot be returned in any branch) attacks the ladder
$\nu_k\le Ck^2$ through the flat flutter amplitude --- T149's rest (1) via rest (2) --- and
comes back with the mechanism's \emph{name}.

\emph{The parity compression.} The reflection-odd form that every probe since T106 works with
is \emph{exactly} the compression of the full symmetric Toeplitz section onto its
antisymmetric parity sector:
\[
U_-^{\mathsf T}\,T_M(c)\,U_-\;=\;T-H\,,\qquad
U_+^{\mathsf T}\,T_M(c)\,U_+\;=\;T+H\,,\qquad
U_+^{\mathsf T}\,T_M(c)\,U_-\;\le\;4.0\times10^{-16}
\]
also on real windows (Basor--Ehrhardt 2009: the parity sectors are the natural objects of the
Toeplitz$+$Hankel algebra) --- and the inertia \emph{localises}: \textbf{the entire negative
inertia of the sign-changing symbol sits in the even sector} (odd $0$, even $1$ on $72/72$,
LDL$^{\mathsf T}$ certified). T148's honest negative $f(0)<0$ is thereby \emph{explained
rather than worked around}: it is a statement about the \emph{other} parity sector. The
matched parity sines $t_k(r)=\tfrac{2}{\sqrt N}\sin(2\pi k(r{+}1)/N)$, $N=2m{+}1$ (exact
eigenpairs of the parity Laplacian, corner $3$ forced by the antisymmetry; control model exact,
$\nu_k=\pi k^2$ to $0.0002$) give a third valid ceiling, improving the ladder constant by
$1.000$--$1.130$ over the Dirichlet$+$Neumann minimum of T148/T149.

\emph{The zone diagonal, and who carries the positivity.} The whitening diagonal is an
\emph{explicit zone function},
$\Lambda_r=c_0-c_{M-1-2r}+\sum_{s\ne r}\max(c_{|r-s|}-c_{M-1-r-s},0)$ (residual $0.0$ on
$72/72$), and the lag vector splits exactly as $c=c^{\mathrm{arch}}+c^{\mathrm{atom}}$ with
$c^{\mathrm{atom}}\le0$. The flutter amplitude becomes a certified \emph{form} functional,
no fit anywhere: $\mathrm{amp}_{\mathrm{loc}}=0.0606$--$0.1993$ at trend $x^{-0.165\pm0.015}$
(T149's fit-based $0.064$--$0.182$ reproduced fit-free), with the certified chain
$\mathrm{amp}_{\mathrm{loc}}\le\mathrm{half}\cdot d_1^{\log}\le
\mathrm{half}\cdot d_1^\lambda/\min\Lambda$ ($1.345$--$3.954$) and the closed atom budget
$\|c^{\mathrm{atom}}\|_1\le4B\sqrt N$. The honest negative beside it: the archimedean
diagonal is \emph{not} the macro profile --- the level shift
$\|\log(\Lambda/\Lambda^{\mathrm{arch}})\|_\infty=0.734$--$2.647$ grows as $x^{0.244}$;
the flutter is small and a priori, the \emph{level} is not. And the perturbation step is
precisely dead, for two independent reasons: the multiplicative (Loewner) step transfers
scale-free with $\exp(\mathrm{amp})\le14.11$ --- the gauge step \emph{closes} --- while the
additive step (Weyl 1912 / Bauer--Fike 1960 / Davis--Kahan 1970) compares
$\|A^{\mathrm{atom}}\|=4.3$--$12.3\%$ of the section against a $\Theta(D^3)$ bottom and
misses by $2.4$--$5.8$ \emph{orders of magnitude}; moreover the archimedean-only section is
itself \emph{indefinite} ($2$--$7$ negative eigenvalues, LDL$^{\mathsf T}$ certified) while
the full section has none --- \textbf{the atoms are co-responsible for the positivity}, not a
perturbation of it.

\emph{The one gate, with its number.} The chain delivers $0.0680$--$0.1845$ of the true gap
certified (the best window reproduces T149's $0.1845$ exactly), a priori
$8.16\times10^{-3}$--$1.74\times10^{-2}$; the ladder-shaped $Q^\star$ ceiling is valid by
monotonicity ($38.76$--$261.3$ against the certified minimum $36.98$--$144.6$, price
$\le2.555\times$ for the reduction to \emph{one} constant). But
$C=14.24$--$43.39\;(=13.81\pi)$ with trend $x^{0.258\pm0.009}$: the gate ``ladder constant
non-growing'' falls --- the only one of all. The maximum sits at $k=1$ ($67/72$), the growth is
carried by the deeper modes, and the gap $\pi\to13.81\pi$ is exactly the \emph{arithmetic
leakage} of the bottom mode ($\ell^1$ mass $1.41$--$1.79$,
$m\|\psi\|_\infty^2=2.45$--$3.41$ against the model's $2$). The stress is now localised:
because the amplitude and the ladder are separate statements, the T145 no-go can be asked
\emph{which} it violates --- the answer is the ladder alone (its multiplier is smooth,
$\mathrm{TV}\le0.2334$; its ladder constant grows $x^{1.840\pm0.130}$), while the Dirichlet
and parity controls reproduce $C=\pi$ to $0.0004/0.0002$. The identity/certificate core of
T149+T150 --- the gauge freedom with the const gauge and its certified sandwich, the two-regime
discriminator, the explicit zone diagonal with the closed atom budget, the parity compression
with the inertia localisation, and the parity-sine calibration with the per-window ladder
certificate --- is load-bearing as \vref{v549} \veri{v549\_gauge\_parity\_identities.py}
(Section~\ref{sec:v549}).

\begin{keybox}[After T150: the mechanism is named --- one inequality remains]

\emph{odd parity sector} of a sign-changing-symbol Toeplitz section --- \emph{the} one
inequality; measured $C\le43.391=13.81\pi$ certified per stratum, trend $x^{0.258\pm0.009}$
against the flatness bar $0.25$. \emph{(K2)} a closed lower bound on
$\min\Lambda^{\mathrm{arch}}$ from the smooth kernel --- it would make the flutter-amplitude
ceiling closed rather than per-window certified. \emph{(K3)} the extension of Basor--Ehrhardt

T148's honest negative is explained (the negative inertia lives in the even sector), the

\subsection{The odd ladder and the Sobolev reroute (T151)}
T151 (\texttt{odd\_ladder\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{ODD.LADDER}, $27/27$, $43.4$\,s on
$72$ prime-power windows $m=96\ldots1491$, verdict \textsc{odd-carries}, the verdict rule
wired constructively: ``proved'' cannot be returned in any branch) attacks the one remaining
inequality --- and closes it by \emph{rerouting off the ladder}.

\emph{The grid step-over, and the matrix-versus-symbol lesson.} The positivity of the odd
sector is a \emph{grid} fact: the parity sines live on the shifted grid $\theta_k=2\pi k/N$
with $\mu^P_k=2-2\cos\theta_k$ exactly, and the symbol's negative window (width
$\theta_c=7.06\times10^{-4}$--$1.32\times10^{-2}$) lies \emph{below} the first odd grid point
$\theta_1$ on every window ($\theta_c/\theta_1=0.328$--$0.407$, trend $x^{-0.057}$): the
grid steps over it on $72/72$ --- stepped over rather than cancelled. But the pointwise
symbol \emph{language} fails at exactly this resolution: $f''(0)=3.8\times10^{5}$--$6.8\times
10^{8}$, $f$ moves by a relative $0.47$--$0.85$ across \emph{one} mode spacing, the section
form averages the symbol against a Fej\'er kernel of exactly that width instead of sampling
it (mode-by-mode deviation $1.39$--$1.83$ at $k=1$), and the one-parameter symbol margin is
vacuous ($\rho\ge1$) on $72/72$. \textbf{T150's rest item 3 --- extending Basor--Ehrhardt
2009 to $f(0)<0$ --- is thereby answered in the negative}: the local model at the symbol
minimum exists, but as a \emph{matrix} statement, not a symbol one ---
$\lambda_k(A)\le S\mu^P_k$ for $k\le8$ certified by completed LDL$^{\mathsf T}$ counts
(Sylvester 1852) with $S=1.1019$--$2.3870$: the odd effective minimum sits at $\theta_1$,
order $2$, $O(1)$ prefactor, $f(0)<0$ \emph{absorbed} by the Rayleigh floor
$L_P\ge\mu^P_1I$. The leakage T150 left as a bare number is anatomised: a \emph{low-$k$
rotation} of the bottom mode away from $t_1$ ($\sin\angle(\psi,t_1)=0.8156$--$0.8943$,
band shares $0.355$ at $k=1$, $0.687$ at $k=2$--$4$, $0.005$ beyond $k=64$; sideband peak at
$l^\ast=2$) --- not an arithmetic sideband.

\emph{The Sobolev step, and the linear bound.} The multiplicative mode comparison T150 asked
for \emph{is} the discrete Sobolev step: an odd-sector vector vanishes at the virtual node,
so $\|\psi\|_\infty^2\le2\|\psi\|_2\|\nabla\psi\|_2$; the certified pencil floor
$\kappa=0.2273$--$0.4502$ (\emph{one} completed Cholesky per window, floor carried, trend
$x^{0.047\pm0.009}$) bounds the gradient energy by $\lambda_k/\kappa$, and
\[
b_k\;:=\;m\|\psi_k\|_\infty^2\;\le\;2m\sqrt{\frac{K_{\mathrm{bot}}\,\mu^P_k}{\kappa}}
\;\le\;C_S\,k
\]
with $C_S=11.5137$--$19.5731$ (median $13.82$, trend $x^{0.020\pm0.007}$):
\textbf{linear in $k$ and non-growing} where T150's quadratic ladder grew ($C=13.81\pi$ at
$x^{0.258}$) --- nothing additive anywhere, so the $\Theta(D^3)$ bottom that killed Weyl /
Bauer--Fike / Davis--Kahan never enters, and the $\sqrt m$ that kills every rotation route
(the $\nu$ conversion costs $4\sqrt m$ and overshoots $\pi$ by $4.2\times10^{3}$--$1.0\times
10^{6}$) is never paid; at the bottom the gain over the $\nu$ route is a factor
$7.5$--$34.9$. The layer cake buys only $1.00$--$2.37$ and does not change the trend. The
honest negative beside it: the \emph{global} pencil ratio grows $x^{2.695}$ (useless ---
$L_P$ saturates at $4$ while the section's top does not); everything is carried by the
\emph{bottom} ratio $R=K_{\mathrm{bot}}/\kappa=3.3634$--$9.7108$ at $x^{0.037\pm0.015}$ ---
the \emph{one} remaining fit in the chain.

\emph{The large numbers, and the localised stress.} T150's rest item 2 is closed \emph{and
attained}: $\min_r\Lambda^{\mathrm{arch}}_r=c^{\mathrm{arch}}_0-c^{\mathrm{arch}}_{M-1}
=2.5928$--$4.8981$ at relative deviation $0.0$ (two per-window-checked shape properties).
$Q^\star_{\mathrm{sob}}=12.39$--$23.94$ ($x^{0.029\pm0.008}$) beats the $\ell^1$ ceiling
$43.66$--$158$ by $2.69$--$10.13$; end to end moves from
$7.88\times10^{-3}$--$1.74\times10^{-2}$ to
$2.01\times10^{-2}$--$3.52\times10^{-2}$ of the true gap (gain $1.64$--$3.18\times$), and the
dominant loss is now $\Psi=4.7\times10^{3}$--$6.1\times10^{6}$ --- never before the
bottleneck. The stress localises exactly where it must: the T145 no-go breaks \emph{in the

\subsection{The pencil ratio and the cancellation (T152)}
T152 (\texttt{pencil\_ratio\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{PENCIL.RATIO}, $37/37$, $33.2$\,s on
$60$ prime-power windows $m=149\ldots1445$, verdict \textsc{one-term-missing}, the verdict
rule wired constructively: ``proved'' cannot be returned in any branch) attacks the one
scalar T151 left as a fit --- the $m$-freeness of the bottom pencil ratio
$R=K_{\mathrm{bot}}/\kappa$ --- and returns the sharpest structural fact of the phase.

\emph{Both hoped-for gifts refuted: positivity is a cancellation.} $A^{\mathrm{arch}}$ is
\emph{not} positive in the odd sector on any of the $60$ windows
($\lambda_{\min}=-2.8132$--$-1.8396$, certified negative by a completed Cholesky of
$A^{\mathrm{arch}}-tI$ with the floor carried): the odd sector removes the constant mode but
not the negative archimedean mass near the origin. In pencil normalisation the failure is
catastrophic, not marginal --- $\kappa_{\mathrm{ar}}=\nu_{\min}(A^{\mathrm{arch}},L_P)
=-5.28\times10^{5}$--$-4.00\times10^{3}=O(-m^{2})$, because the lowest parity sine has
$L_P$-energy $\mu^P_1=O(m^{-2})$ while it sees an $O(1)$-negative form. And the atom part is
negative too ($\nu_{\min}(A^{\mathrm{atom}},L_P)=-1408$--$-25.6$ on $60/60$): \emph{neither}
summand of the exact split is positive, and the sum is --- \textbf{the positivity of the odd
section is a cancellation between the archimedean kernel and the prime-power atoms, not a
property of either half} (exhibited exactly at $t_1$: an archimedean part
$-5.26\times10^{5}$--$-3.98\times10^{3}$ plus an atom part
$8.19\times10^{3}$--$2.88\times10^{6}$ add to a near-$O(1)$ quotient --- the atoms even
\emph{overshoot} the archimedean hole). The additive Weyl route misses $\kappa$ by a measured
$1.5\times10^{4}$--$1.8\times10^{6}$ and the closed $\ell^1$ budget route by a further
$2.3\times10^{5}$--$9.9\times10^{7}$ --- the $O(m^{2})$ conversion $1/\mu^P_1$ kills both.
But the archimedean diagonal is negative on only an $m$-\emph{independent} number of parity
modes ($k\le4$--$7$ of up to $1445$), and above them its pencil quotient is $\ge0.989$ on
$60/60$: \textbf{the Schur two-block criterion (Schur 1917 --- an equivalence, with both
Cholesky floors subtracted) with a fixed $16$-mode low block certifies
$\kappa\ge t=0.2250$--$0.2500$ on every window}, at $m^{0.006\pm0.036}$ with identical
quartile medians --- the floor is no longer a fit. It consumes \emph{one} unproven
inequality --- $B_{HH}\succeq tI$ on the bulk block --- and entrywise routes are provably
insufficient for it: Gershgorin returns $-8.99\times10^{5}$--$-1.3\times10^{3}$ on the full
whitened parity block and still $-7189$--$-58$ after cutting at the last arch-negative mode,
the median row coupling being $3.9$--$19.6$ against a diagonal of $0.36$--$0.89$. What is
needed is a \emph{block} statement, not a bound on individual prime-power sums.

\emph{The ratio, certified on both ends.} The archimedean part does not carry the
\emph{ceiling} either: $K^{\mathrm{arch}}_{\mathrm{bot}}=24.6$--$1326$ at $m^{1.519}$, one
to two orders of magnitude above the true $K_{\mathrm{bot}}=1.102$--$2.118$ and growing
where the true one is flat --- the atoms do not perturb an archimedean alignment, they
\emph{create} it. The new number: \textbf{$R\le K_{\mathrm{bot}}/t=4.408$--$8.471$ at
$m^{0.099\pm0.167}$, certified on both ends} (inertia ladder above, Schur floor below), with
a quartile walk of $1.269$ over a $4.54\times$ $m$-range. Two structural $m$-free routes to
the ceiling lose four to six orders of magnitude: Courant--Fischer on the parity basis (the
atom overshoot is $O(m^{2})$), and the two-sided bulk block --- whose KMS ratio step \emph{is}
a theorem ($\sin a/\sin b\le a/b$, hence $\mu^P_{k+16}/\mu^P_k\le289$, verified
$285.95$--$288.97\le289$ on the table) but whose ingredient $T_{HH}=26.8$--$3116$ grows
$m^{2.044}$: the section's low \emph{eigenvalues} track the model's while its low
\emph{eigenvectors} do not. The no-go reconstruction breaks exactly at the unclosed step
(the floor survives; ceiling and $R$ grow $m^{1.994}$) --- the gap is real, not a tool loss;
the control ($L_P$ against itself) is $(1,1,1)$ to $3.5\times10^{-11}$.

\emph{The $\Psi$ map, and the honest dual reading.} $\Psi\le8.70\times10^{3}$--$6.24\times
10^{5}$ \emph{is} $1/\lambda_{\min}(E)$ to within $1.12$--$1.19$ --- the spectral bottom of
the whitened section and essentially nothing else; it grows $m^{2.18}$ because
$\mu^P_1=O(m^{-2})$, not because $\kappa$ degrades. The reserve: \textbf{$89$--$92\%$ of
$\operatorname{trace}(E^{-1})$ sits on the eight lowest modes --- exactly those the
certified ladder already controls}; rebuilding the subset supremum into a ladder sum is
worth $3.46$--$5.29\times$ end to end (it would lift T151's
$2.01\times10^{-2}$--$3.52\times10^{-2}$ into the
$8\times10^{-2}$--$1.4\times10^{-1}$ range) --- now the dominant loss, outranking any
further sharpening of $R$. The verdict is kept honest by printing both readings: on the
band estimator alone gate B would fail and the verdict would read \textsc{ratio-resists};
the quartile-median reading ($15$ windows per stratum, high variance of the band fit) is the
declared one, and both are in the output. Also on the record: T151's $R$ exponent $0.037$
was fitted against the zone variable (not monotone in $m$) --- the same quantity refit in
$m$ is $0.099$, so part of that flatness was the fit variable rather than the object. Ten
map entries are named; \emph{none is promoted} --- the strongest candidates consume the
unproven block positivity $B_{HH}\succeq tI$ and stay pending with exactly that reason.

\begin{keybox}[After T152: the floor is structural --- one term and one rebuild remain]
\emph{(M1)} \textbf{the block inequality}: $B_{HH}\succeq tI$ on the bulk block --- the
single unproven input the Schur certificate consumes; entrywise/Gershgorin bounds provably

$K_{\mathrm{bot}}$ --- every structural route loses four to six orders of magnitude because

$3.46$--$5.29\times$ end to end, now the dominant loss and ahead of any further work on $R$.
Only after these: frames beyond A, zones beyond prime powers. The honest state, in one
sentence: after T152 the positivity of the odd sector is known to be a cancellation between
geometry and arithmetic rather than a property of either half, the pencil floor is certified
by a fixed-size Schur block instead of a fit, the ratio is certified on both ends with one
$m$-free ceiling missing --- and the largest remaining loss sits on modes the certified
ladder already controls.
T153 (\texttt{psi\_ladder\_probe.py}) is running at exactly that rebuild and that block
inequality.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The $\Psi$ pinning and the two remaining terms (T153)}
T153 (\texttt{psi\_ladder\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{PSI.LADDER}, $33/33$, $7.6$\,s on
$18$ prime-power windows $m=96\ldots1430$, block anatomy on $11$ and the ceiling on $12$ of
them, verdict \textsc{rebuild-resists}, the gates \emph{evaluated} rather than chosen) carries
out the rebuild T152 mapped --- and refutes it by exactly its own factor.

\emph{The pinning: the reserve was never there.} The rebuild itself is real and comes in three
rigorous forms, each an upper bound on the same $\Psi$: the mode-resolved ladder sum (cost
$1.195$--$1.761\times$ against the T149 route), the arithmetic-free operator form
$(\mathrm{const}/t)\,\Psi_P$ against the pure Kac--Murdock--Szeg\H{o} model (cost
$3.73$--$9.70\times$), and the theorem-grade collapse $\Psi\le\mathrm{const}/(t\,\mu^P_1)$
(cost $3.73$--$9.70\times$). But the decisive measurement is a \emph{lower} bound: for the
subset that maximises the first mode, every term of
$\sum_k\lambda_k^{-1}\langle v_k,\mathbf 1_S\rangle^2$ is nonnegative, so
$a_1/\lambda_1\le\Psi\le1/\lambda_1$ with $a_1=0.7695$--$0.8306$ --- exactly the
$8/\pi^2=0.8106$ of the first parity sine. \textbf{$\Psi$ is pinned to within
$1/a_1=1.204$--$1.300$, so T152's mapped $3.46$--$5.29\times$ reserve never existed}; the
head/tail replacement T152 proposed lies $2.31$--$6.12\times$ \emph{below} the hard lower
bound and is not an upper bound at all --- the maximising subset is aligned with $v_1$ itself,
so the head \emph{is} the value of $\Psi$, not a redundancy. The bookkeeping is exact: the
rebuild retires the level constant $c_0^{\mathrm{ap}}=4.157$--$4.870$ and pays the collapse
cost $3.73$--$9.70$; on this surface the two cancel, the net end-to-end gain is
$0.50$--$1.11\times$ (median $0.62$), and the certified fraction moves from
$2.01\times10^{-2}$--$3.52\times10^{-2}$ to $1.01\times10^{-2}$--$3.92\times10^{-2}$ --- not
the targeted $8\times10^{-2}$ band. The collapse cost is named exactly:
$\lambda_1(A)/(t\,\mu^P_1)=3.25$--$8.40$ --- the pencil minimum is not attained at the bottom
mode, so a floor uniform over all modes is lossy for mode $1$ alone. What the rebuild does buy
is \emph{uniformity}: the collapse form contains nothing beyond an explicit arithmetic sum,
the one open block inequality $t$, and the exact $\mu^P_1$ --- it retires Charikar's licence
and every per-window diagonalisation from the $\Psi$ step. \textbf{$\Psi$ is closed as a
term.} The balance is clean: $t$ is flat ($x^{-0.004}$, certified $0.2400$--$0.2500$ on all
$18$ windows) and the gain is flat ($x^{-0.039}$).

\emph{The sign reversal, the four dead candidates, and the live route.} $B_{HH}\succeq tI$ is
the original pencil inequality restricted to $\mathrm{span}\{t_k:k>16\}$ --- an identity, not
an analogy: the Schur route relocates the question onto a subspace, it does not ease it. The
find of the zone reverses a T152 sign: \textbf{on the bulk parity block the archimedean part
is positive} ($\lambda_{\min}(B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH})=1.0362$--$1.4143>t=0.25$), after an
$m$-free peeling of at most $8$ modes on every window --- the archimedean negativity lives
entirely in the lowest parity modes, and on the bulk it is the \emph{atoms} that are negative
($-484.6$--$-14.95$): the obstruction has moved from a negative smooth kernel to an
arithmetic remainder. Four block candidates die: entrywise Gershgorin ($-1929$--$-21.35$ on
the bulk), block Gershgorin (Feingold--Varga 1962) on a dyadic partition
($-333.4$--$-7.68$; the coupling is long-range), a mode-index Toeplitz-plus-Hankel fit
(residual $0.70$--$0.95$ of the Frobenius mass --- no second-level Szeg\H{o}/Widom argument
exists), and a recursive Schur step, which certifies the same $t=0.25$ at levels $0/1/2$ ---
\emph{scale-invariant}, so recursion alone can never terminate. The one route that produces
positivity at all is a relative (Kato-type) bound in the archimedean metric:
$1+\lambda_{\min}(C)=8.3\times10^{-4}$--$2.9\times10^{-2}$, certified positive on every window
where all three additive candidates return a negative number --- but it shrinks as
$x^{-1.778}$: positivity per window, not a uniform floor. The whole of $t$ sits in how far
inside $-1$ the arch-whitened atom operator lies, and that distance is of the same order as
$\mu^P_1$ itself.

\emph{The inverse-iteration find.} No family fixed in advance carries the $K_{\mathrm{bot}}$
ceiling: the fixed-size band replacement grows exactly like the bulk ceiling it replaces
($T_{\mathrm{band}}$ at $x^{2.017}$ against $T_{HH}$ at $x^{2.019}$), the parity sines and

is an eigenvector of every convolution). The atom overshoot is located exactly: the Toeplitz

the Hankel reflection half is $+9.45$ --- a boundary-reflection effect, not a bulk-atom

$K_{\mathrm{bot}}=1.102$--$1.896$, on a certificate of fixed size $8$: the ceiling \emph{is}
carried by a fixed-size family --- just not by one written down in advance. Nine map entries
are named (v580--v588); \emph{nothing is promoted} --- the probe is exploration only, and the

\begin{keybox}[After T153: $\Psi$ is closed --- two terms remain, and they are one object]

T154 (\texttt{green\_align\_probe.py}) is running at exactly that estimate.

\subsection{The ceiling closes at fixed size, and the obstruction becomes geometry (T154)}
T154 (\texttt{green\_align\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{GREEN.ALIGN}, $29/29$, $5.0$\,s on
$12$ prime-power windows $h=50\ldots1077$, the Kato anatomy on $10$ of them, verdict
\textsc{align-resists}, the gates \emph{evaluated} rather than chosen) attacks the
Green/alignment estimate both T153 terms lose to --- and the ceiling half closes, exactly.

\emph{The ceiling, closed with a direction lesson.} The part opens with a correction to its
own commission, stated explicitly because it is easy to get backwards: the ceiling needs
\emph{no residual argument at all}. Ritz values are \emph{upper} bounds for the eigenvalues
of the \emph{same index} (Courant--Fischer 1920 / Cauchy 1829 interlacing), so a Ritz
quotient is a ceiling by a theorem; Temple 1928 / Kato 1949 is a \emph{floor} device and is
needed only there. The certificate:
$\mathrm{span}\{t_1..t_8\}+A^{-1}L_P\,\mathrm{span}\{t_1..t_8\}$ --- sixteen columns,
\emph{fixed} size, the whole certificate $8$ completed Choleskys of matrices
$\le8\times8$ --- carries $K^F=1.1019$--$1.9964$, flat ($x^{0.094\pm0.058}$), and
\textbf{agrees with the inertia-certified $K_{\mathrm{bot}}$ to a relative
$5.17\times10^{-7}$ on every window}: the sixteen-column certificate does not merely bound
the true bottom ladder, it \emph{attains} it, and the eight LDL$^{\mathsf T}$ counts of
size $m$ per window are retired from the ceiling step
\veri{v551\_ritz\_ceiling\_certificate.py}. The parity sines alone overshoot as
$K^F=11.2$--$2.1\times10^{4}$ at $x^{2.47}$ (T152's $O(m^2)$ reproduced), and the geometry
says why the Green step repairs them: the true bottom eight of $A$ lie inside the
twice-iterated subspace to $\le0.33^\circ$, the Green columns have only
$1.8$--$4.9\%$ of their mass outside the sine block, and their pencil Rayleigh quotients
sit at $0.287$--$0.681$, just above the certified floor $t=0.25$ --- precisely what an
inverse-iteration step should do (Kaniel 1966 / Paige 1971, quoted as the explanation,
never used as a bound).

\emph{The floor half, refuted at fixed size and recovered at full size.} The Temple/Kato
residual argument --- with the separation $\beta=t\,\mu^P_9$ that the containment of the
parity sines makes free, $\mu^P_9/\mu^P_1\to81$ exact --- fails by
$\|R\|^2/(\beta\lambda_1)=6.3\times10^{3}$--$5.6\times10^{9}$, growing as $x^{4.50}$: any
sine-containing subspace has residual $O(\|A\|)=O(1)$ against a target
$\lambda_1=O(\mu^P_1)=O(m^{-2})$, for \emph{every} fixed containment depth (the
preregistered scan over $k_c=8\ldots48$ closes $1$ of $12$ windows, and that one needs
$k_c/m=0.64$ --- not fixed size in effect; the scalar Temple form is vacuous on $12/12$).
\textbf{The obstruction is named}: seven of the eight bottom directions of $A$ agree with
the bottom of $L_P$ to $0.15$--$1.35^\circ$ (median), \emph{one} sits at
$82.93$--$89.79^\circ$ --- and that single misalignment \emph{is} the collapse price.
One completed Cholesky of $A-\gamma I$ per window recovers it \emph{in full},
$4.408$--$7.985$ --- certified per window, size $m$, not $m$-free, labelled as such. The
missing fixed-size ingredient reduces to \emph{one arithmetic-free number}: the $L_P$
floor on the complement of the eight bottom Ritz directions --- a question about the
tridiagonal $L_P$ and one eight-dimensional subspace, with no prime-power input anywhere
--- measured flat at $5.93$--$8.25\,\mu^P_1$, and feeding the measured value into the
fixed-size Temple step returns $4.408$--$7.617$ of the price $4.408$--$7.986$: worth
$91$--$100\%$, conditionally.

\emph{The Kato anatomy, and the double refutation.} The loss of the live R1 route is
\emph{not} the floor: $\lambda_{\min}(B_{HH})=0.266$--$0.415>t=0.25$, yet the Kato product
delivers only a factor $1.97$--$121$ less ($x^{1.635}$), because the two minima are
attained in different directions, $24.9$--$89.8^\circ$ apart --- the minimiser that ruins
the relative bound is a perfectly harmless direction for the block inequality itself.
Its mass sits $96.5$--$100\%$ on the eight modes \emph{directly above} the peel cut (only
$0.9$--$11.9\%$ at the boundary), so T153's Hankel-reflection culprit is refuted
\emph{twice}: at the minimiser both halves hurt (Toeplitz $-100.3\ldots-0.248$, Hankel
$-72.69\ldots-0.90$), and removing the reflection destroys positive definiteness
altogether ($\lambda_1=-7.49\ldots-2.64$) --- the reflection half is load-bearing, not a
nuisance term. Boundary peeling buys $1.08$--$1.38\times$, the norm route is dead by two
to three orders, and the only repair that moves the number needs a peel of $0.40$--$0.69$
of the window --- $m$-proportional, for a scale-free reason: the minimiser always sits on
the lowest eight modes of whatever block is left.

\emph{Two end-to-end numbers, never conflated.} $m$-free in shape: \emph{unchanged} at
$1.01\times10^{-2}$--$3.92\times10^{-2}$ --- the ceiling closure buys uniformity and cost
(eight size-$m$ factorisations retired), not size, because T153 already used the certified
$K_{\mathrm{bot}}$ and the certificate attains exactly that number. Per window certified,
with the collapse price recovered by one Cholesky:
$\mathbf{4.45\times10^{-2}}$--$\mathbf{3.13\times10^{-1}}$ --- inside the target band
$3\times10^{-2}$--$3\times10^{-1}$. The honest reading: the \emph{size} target is met and
the \emph{uniformity} target is not, and those are different targets. The obligatory
stress separates cleanly: on the T145 no-go reconstruction the floor survives ($t=0.05$)
while $K_{\mathrm{bot}}$ explodes at $x^{1.99}$ and the certificate explodes \emph{with}
it ($x^{2.29}$, overshooting the true constant by $1.12$--$2.19$) --- so the exact
attainment is a property of the \emph{real} section, not of the instrument --- and the
collapse price separates the families by orders of magnitude ($1.8\times10^{3}$--$2.1
\times10^{5}$ against $4.4$--$8.0$); the parity control is exact to $3.5\times10^{-6}$
and the Courant--Fischer direction is violated on $0/26$ positive-definite cases.

\begin{keybox}[After T154: the ceiling is closed --- two uniformity floors remain]
\emph{(O1)} \textbf{R1$'$, the $m$-free block floor}: an $m$-free lower bound for
$\lambda_{\min}(B_{HH})$ on the bulk parity block, now \emph{direction-aware} --- every
relative route is dead with a number (the Kato number
$1+\lambda_{\min}(C)=3.3\times10^{-3}$--$2.3\times10^{-1}$ shrinks as $x^{-1.69}$ against
a requirement $0.19$--$0.30$, and the loss is the misalignment, not the floor), and the
anatomy says where to look: $96.5$--$100\%$ of the offending direction sits on the eight
modes immediately above the cut, wherever the cut is put. \emph{(O2)} \textbf{R2$'$, the
$m$-free bottom-mode floor}: an $m$-free lower bound for
$\min_{v\perp\mathrm{bottom}}v^{\mathsf T}L_Pv/v^{\mathsf T}v$ --- arithmetic-free, only
the tridiagonal $L_P$ and one eight-dimensional subspace, measured flat at
$5.93$--$8.25\,\mu^P_1$ and worth $91$--$100\%$ of the collapse price at fixed size. Both
are now \emph{uniformity} terms: the numbers are certified per window, and what is
missing is the $m$-free argument. The verdict rule was applied honestly:
\textsc{one-term-missing} was deliberately \emph{not} taken --- the two terms are of the
same type but not the same statement (the pencil minimum demonstrably does not sit at the
bottom mode, which is exactly what the collapse price measures), and merging them would
be a silent upgrade. The honest state, in one sentence: after T154 the ceiling of the
bottom ladder is closed at fixed size and closed exactly, the collapse price is a named
geometric object recovered per window by one Cholesky, and what stands between the
per-window band $4.45\times10^{-2}$--$3.13\times10^{-1}$ and an $m$-free statement is the
uniformity of two floors.
T155 (\texttt{bottom\_floor\_probe.py}) is running at exactly those two floors.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The complement floor becomes exact at fixed size, and the block floor excludes
every symbol argument (T155)}
T155 (\texttt{bottom\_floor\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{BOTTOM.FLOOR}, $27/27$, $9.0$\,s on
$16$ prime-power windows $h=142\ldots1293$, the block surface on $14$ of them, verdict
\textsc{floors-resist}, the gates evaluated from the numbers) attacks the two uniformity
floors T154 left --- and reduces the first to its smallest form, exactly.

\emph{The exact $12\times12$ reduction.} The single $m$-sized object left in the bottom-mode
chain was the complement floor $L_c=\min_{v\perp Q_8}v^{\mathsf T}L_Pv/v^{\mathsf T}v$. The
new certificate is one identity plus one Rayleigh bound, a theorem for every $m$ and every
subspace $W$ with orthonormal basis $Q_W$:
\[
\min_{v\perp W,\ \|v\|=1} v^{\mathsf T}L_P\,v \;\ge\;
\mu^P_{K+1}-\lambda_{\max}\!\bigl(M^{1/2}\,(I-GG^{\mathsf T})\,M^{1/2}\bigr),
\qquad
M=\operatorname{diag}\bigl(\mu^P_{K+1}-\mu^P_k\bigr)_{k\le K},
\]
with $G=T_K\,Q_W$ and $T_K$ the first $K$ exact parity sines --- the direction is checked at every window
(the Cholesky-certified $\lambda_{\max}$ is \emph{subtracted} from a lower bound, and the
certificate never exceeds the exact value). It loses nothing: the ratio certificate/exact
is $\mathbf{0.999999783}$--$\mathbf{0.999999958}$ on $16$ of $16$ windows, and $K=12$
suffices everywhere (preregistered ladder $8\ldots64$) --- a $12\times12$ eigenvalue
problem in the exact Kac--Murdock--Szeg\H{o} numbers plus one $12\times8$ overlap matrix
replaces the $m$-sized eigenproblem T154 had to solve. Both closed-form controls are hit:
$W=\mathrm{span}\{t_1..t_8\}$ returns $\mu^P_9$ to $1.05\times10^{-12}$, and
$W=\mathrm{span}\{t_2..t_9\}$ --- the configuration in which the certificate is
\emph{worthless} --- returns $\mu^P_1$ to $8.89\times10^{-11}$: the instrument reports its
own worthlessness rather than something flattering. (This certificate is now
load-bearing: it is promoted, together with T157's three instruments, as
\vref{v552}, Section~\ref{sec:v552} --- \veri{v552\_angle\_instruments.py}.)

\emph{The defect is localised, and the $83$--$90^\circ$ direction is demystified.} If $Q_8$
covered the eight lowest $L_P$ modes, the floor would be $\mu^P_9=80.74$--$81.00\,\mu^P_1$
($m$-explicit, KMS); measured it is $5.82$--$7.86$, a factor $10.31$--$13.92$ lost --- and
the loss is \emph{not} spread over the eight modes: the largest uncovered fraction
$1-\|\mathrm{row}_k(G)\|^2$ sits at $k=1$, the bottom mode itself, at
$\mathbf{0.539}$--$\mathbf{0.611}$ (flat, $x^{-0.063\pm0.016}$). The reason is visible in
the same object: T154's misaligned direction ($82.08$--$89.70^\circ$ on this surface)
carries only $2.8\times10^{-5}$--$1.9\times10^{-2}$ of its mass on modes $1$--$8$, has
$L_P$ Rayleigh quotient $81.2$--$103.4\,\mu^P_1$ and peaks at mode $9$--$10$ --- the
certificate spends one of its eight directions on modes $9$--$12$ and pays for it at mode
$1$, which is exactly why it needs $K=12$ and not $K=8$. The payoff: feeding the fixed-size
floor into the unchanged Temple step recovers $3.250$--$7.226$ of the collapse price
$3.250$--$8.471$ --- $\mathbf{78.8}$--$\mathbf{100.0\%}$ \emph{at fixed size} (in full on
$12/16$ windows, at least ninety percent on $14/16$; the two remaining windows are
residual-limited, not floor-limited), with $32$ Green columns, an $8\times8$ Ritz block,
one $12\times12$ certificate and a Temple bisection --- nothing in the chain has a size
depending on $m$, where T154 needed one Cholesky of size $m$. Two repairs are refuted with
their mechanism: the pencil-ceiling chain --- a theorem in every step (projector-split
identity, Davis--Kahan 1970 transfer $s=5.2\times10^{-4}$--$1.0\times10^{-2}$) --- dies on
its one new input $\kappa=\lambda_{\max}(B)=3.1\times10^{3}$--$2.7\times10^{6}$ growing as
$x^{2.82}$ (the two-sided pencil is maximally ill-conditioned exactly at the bottom the
floor is about; peeling does not cure it), and widening the floor subspace to
$r=12/16/24$ raises the certified floor $\times1.19$--$3.71$ while the residual rises
$\times12.4$--$8514$ --- the Temple step returns a floor on $0$ of $32$ widened
configurations: floor and residual are bought from the same account, and at $r=8$ the
account is balanced.

\emph{The block floor, and the impossibility of a symbol argument.}
$\lambda_{\min}(B_{HH})=0.2430$--$0.4249$ is certified positive on every window (the
inequality holds against $t=0.25$ on $13/14$; on the rest the Schur ladder backs off to a
smaller certified $t$ --- reported, not smoothed). First, a correction \emph{of target}:
T154's anatomy (the minimiser sits $95.3$--$99.6\%$ on the eight modes above the cut,
confirmed here) belongs to the minimiser of the arch-whitened operator $C$ --- the
minimiser of $B_{HH}$ \emph{itself} puts only $1.5\times10^{-5}$--$0.69$ of its mass there:
a decomposition aimed at the $C$-minimiser is aimed away from $\lambda_{\min}(B_{HH})$.
The direction-aware $2\times2$ decomposition dies on the coupling (both diagonal blocks
healthy at $0.3518$--$0.5245$ and $0.2431$--$0.4273$, but
$\|B_{wd}\|=5.81$--$389.41$ against the allowed $0.292$--$0.456$ --- too large by
$16.8$--$908$, growing $x^{1.94}$: the atoms couple the mode index long-range); the local
atom norm on the eight-mode window exceeds the local arch reserve by $1.50$--$5.12$ on
every window; and the deeper cut does not terminate (the deep block's own floor is
$2.1\times10^{-3}$--$6.0\times10^{-2}<t$, with a Kato factor of the same order as at the
original cut --- moving the cut up by $8$ modes moves the problem up by $8$ modes). The one
positive result is a mechanism: \textbf{the arch reserve \emph{is} the symbol infimum} ---
$\min_{\theta\ge\theta_{k_b+1}}f^{\mathrm{arch}}(\theta)/(4\sin^2(\theta/2))$ equals
$\lambda_{\min}(B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH})$ to $1.000022$--$1.000521$ on $14/14$ windows (band
$1.0004$--$1.4049$, a factor $4.0$--$5.6$ above the target) --- a theorem \emph{candidate}
(Szeg\H{o} 1915 / Widom 1958 / KMS 1953): proving it means proving an inequality about one
function of one variable. And the same instrument delivers the strongest negative
statement of the series: \textbf{the full symbol infimum over the same bulk range is
$-714.2\ldots-7.6$, negative on every window} (the atom symbol alone reaches $-1148.5$),
while the section floor is positive --- any Szeg\H{o}/Widom-type argument returns the
symbol infimum and therefore a negative number here, so \emph{no symbol argument can ever
produce R1$'$}: whatever carries it must be a genuinely finite-section mechanism (the
Fej\'er averaging of the atom spikes against the section), and the diagonal already shows
the section is doing the work ($\min_k(B_{HH})_{kk}=0.3840$--$0.7444$, a factor
$1.33$--$1.89$ above the true minimum).

\emph{The honest miss, and the stress.} The end-to-end fraction reaches
$3.28\times10^{-2}$--$2.83\times10^{-1}$ with the label \emph{certified at fixed size}
(T154 left $1.01\times10^{-2}$--$3.92\times10^{-2}$ $m$-free in shape /
$4.45\times10^{-2}$--$3.13\times10^{-1}$ certified per window with a size-$m$ Cholesky).
The declared bar was $4\times10^{-2}$ and the bottom of the band is $3.28\times10^{-2}$
--- \textbf{missed by a factor $1.22$}, reported rather than repaired: the pairing of two
band minima from different and wider surfaces is deliberately pessimistic, and the
like-for-like number --- fixed size against size $m$, same window, same Temple step --- is
the share $78.8$--$100\%$, which is what this probe moved. Fixed size is \emph{not}
$m$-free: the certificate does not grow, but its value is measured on $16$ windows, not
bounded by an argument. Balance: $5$ theorem, $3$ certified-fixed-size, $2$
certified-per-window at size $m$, $1$ measured, $1$ theorem candidate --- T154's balance
had zero fixed-size entries below the ceiling row. The obligatory stress breaks on two
axes: on the T145 no-go family the ceiling explodes at $x^{2.010\pm0.003}$ (flat on the
real family), and the new instrument separates too --- the mode-1 uncovered fraction reads
$0.999$--$1.000$ (real: $0.539$--$0.611$), the misalignment is exactly $90.00^\circ$, and
the Temple recovery is $0/8$ against $16/16$ real. The parity sines are exact $L_P$
eigenvectors to $4.85\times10^{-14}$, and the Dirichlet negative control hits its own
rank-one prediction $2/\sqrt N$ to $4.1\times10^{-7}$.

\begin{keybox}[After T155: both floors resist --- two smaller open terms remain]
\emph{(O1)} \textbf{R2$''$, the $m$-free overlap defect}: an $m$-free \emph{upper} bound
for $\lambda_{\max}(M^{1/2}(I-GG^{\mathsf T})M^{1/2})$ at $K=12$ --- equivalently, a bound
on how much of $t_1$ the eight bottom Ritz directions of $A$ may miss (measured

$12\times8$ matrix: everything else in the bottom-mode chain is a theorem or a fixed-size

pencil --- is refuted by a factor $10^{-3}$ for a structural reason. \emph{(O2)}
\textbf{R1$''$, the $m$-free atom part on the bulk}: excluded are relative routes (T154),

(short by $1.50$--$5.12$), deeper cuts (scale-free), and \emph{every symbol argument} (the
full symbol infimum is negative while the section floor is positive); the one surviving

reads $-5.5$ against $t=0.25$, hence \textsc{floors-resist}; merging the terms would be
false --- R2$'$ is a question about $L_P$ and a subspace with the arithmetic compressed
into one $12\times8$ matrix, R1$'$ a question about prime-power sums against a finite
section, now provably outside the reach of the method that settles the first. The honest
state, in one sentence: after T155 the complement floor --- the one $m$-sized object of the
bottom-mode chain --- is reproduced exactly by a $12\times12$ certificate and the collapse
price is recovered $78.8$--$100\%$ at fixed size, while the block floor has acquired an
obstruction that closes off a whole family of methods; this probe bought size and
structure, not uniformity.
T156 (\texttt{twelve\_by\_eight\_probe.py}) is running at exactly those two objects.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{Both terms become single scalars: the $t_1$ loss is one angle, the block
positivity is alignment (T156)}
T156 (\texttt{twelve\_by\_eight\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{TWELVE.EIGHT}, $37/37$,
$6.1$\,s on $16$ prime-power windows $h=142\ldots1293$, the block surface on $12$ windows
$h=50\ldots1077$, verdict \textsc{terms-resist}, the gates evaluated from the numbers:
\textsc{terms-close} needs zero measured rungs, \textsc{one-term-missing} exactly one ---
there are three) attacks the two rest objects T155 left, and reduces both to single
scalars.

\emph{The exact $F(P,r)$ reduction.} The subspace $S_2$ contains $t_1$ \emph{and}
$y_1:=A^{-1}L_P\,t_1$, and the bottom Ritz direction of $A$ mixes them --- that mixing is
where $t_1$ is lost. On $\mathrm{span}\{t_1,y_1\}$ the mixing closes \emph{exactly},
because $L_Pt_1=\mu^P_1t_1$ turns the coupling into an identity with no $A$ in it:
\[
t_1^{\mathsf T}A\,y_1 \;=\; t_1^{\mathsf T}L_P\,t_1 \;=\; \mu^P_1 ,
\]
so the $t_1$-loss of the two-dimensional Ritz pair is a \emph{closed} function $F(P,r)$
of exactly two dimensionless scalars, both Rayleigh quantities of $A$ at the single
vector $t_1$: the Kantorovich product
$P=(t_1^{\mathsf T}At_1)(t_1^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}t_1)\ge1$ and the inverse moment ratio
$r=\|A^{-1}t_1\|^2/(t_1^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}t_1)^2\ge1$ (the reduction agrees with the
four-scalar form to $2.2\times10^{-16}$ and with the true $2\times2$ Ritz pair to
$4.4\times10^{-16}$ --- an identity, not a fit). Measured: $P=5.6\times10^{2}$--$1.0
\times10^{6}$ (enormous --- $A$ and $L_P$ differ by orders of magnitude at $t_1$, so $F$
is essentially $F(\infty,r)$) and $r=2.7158$--$3.4089$, flat ($x^{-0.047\pm0.020}$). The
box route over the admissible $(P,r)$ region is \emph{vacuous}, despite a new $m$-free
bound: the exact spectral-defect identity yields $P-1\ge L^2s^2(r-1)$ (with
$L=\lambda_1(A)/\mu^P_1$ and $s=\mu^P_1\,t_1^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}t_1$; it holds on $16/16$
windows with slack $2917$--$4.87\times10^{6}$) and cuts the region --- but $\sup F$ over
what remains is $1.0000$ where the chain needs at most $0.632$, attained at $P\to1$ with
$r-1$ of the same order: a genuine configuration the pencil does not exclude. The best
route is a two-line theorem,
\[
r \;\le\; \frac{1}{Ls} \;\le\; \frac{1}{p_1},
\qquad
Ls=\sum_j p_j\,\frac{\lambda_1}{\lambda_j}\in[p_1,1],
\]
and its ceiling $1/(Ls)=2.930$--$3.967$ is \emph{tight} to a factor $1.03$--$1.16$:
\textbf{R2$''$ is one $m$-free lower bound on the overlap
$p_1=\cos^2\angle(t_1,e_1(A))=\mathbf{0.2010}$--$\mathbf{0.3282}$}
($55.05$--$63.36^\circ$, flat, $x^{0.054\pm0.029}$). The loss at the cruder $1/p_1$
ceiling is $0.6718$--$0.7990$ against the model's $0.6318$--$0.7067$ against the truth
$d_1(\text{8 Ritz directions})=0.5392$--$0.6316$ --- the chain survives the cruder of the
two ceilings. The model \emph{dominates} the truth on $16/16$ windows (ratio
$0.833$--$0.917$) --- measured, no monotonicity theorem, and the stress below is exactly
about that. The interlacing route is refuted in both of its forms: at $K=12>\dim W=8$ the
matrix $I-GG^{\mathsf T}$ carries the eigenvalue $1$ \emph{exactly} (a rank hole --- the
$\sigma_{\min}$ form returns $\mu^P_1$ and nothing more, identically, for every $m$), and
at $K=8$ it is not vacuous but empty: $\sigma_{\min}(T_8Q_W)=1.7\times10^{-2}$--$1.4
\times10^{-1}$ yields a floor of $1.023$--$2.579\,\mu^P_1$ against the $5.78$--$7.83$ the
\emph{same} overlap matrix gives through the T155 certificate. T155's anatomy is
reproduced (object ratio $0.9533$--$0.9654$, $d_1=0.5392$--$0.6316$, the defect direction
peaking on modes $9$--$10$).

\emph{The J2a correction --- an honest negative.} The one-variable statement T155
expected is \emph{false}: the infimum of $f^{\mathrm{arch}}(\theta)/(4\sin^2(\theta/2))$
over the bulk range is $0.8226$--$1.3973$ ($x^{0.171\pm0.009}$), \textbf{below $1$ on $3$
of $12$ windows} --- T155's quoted $1.000022$--$1.000521$ was the upper surface of the
arch-reserve-equals-symbol-infimum identity (reproduced here to
$3.6\times10^{-5}$--$1.8\times10^{-3}$), not the floor of a $\ge1$ statement. What
survives, and what the chain actually needs, is the \emph{weaker} one-variable statement
$\inf\ge t=0.25$: a factor $3.29$--$5.59$ above target, non-decreasing in $h$, grid-stable
to $1.4\times10^{-5}$ under fourfold refinement, with the minimum at
$\theta/\pi=0.990$--$1.000$ --- the alternating lag sum, which is where a proof would have
to work. Status: a certified-per-window grid fact about a function of one variable, not a
theorem.

\emph{The mechanism of the block floor: alignment, not mass.} The lag decomposition
$v^{\mathsf T}Av=\sum_l c_l\,a_l(v)-\sum_k c_{M-1-k}\,b_k(v)$ is exact to
$6.9\times10^{-15}$ on every window (Fej\'er 1915 --- the weights below are the section's
true weights, not a model). The Fej\'er damping is real but worth \emph{one order of
magnitude}: on the minimiser the realised atom form is
$3.2\times10^{-2}$--$1.9\times10^{-1}$ of the naive $\ell^1$ budget ($x^{-0.501\pm0.024}$),
a factor $5$--$31$, where the split needs $3$--$1981$ \emph{and growing}; and the additive
split is \emph{divergent}: $\|B^{\mathrm{atom}}_{HH}\|=2.2$--$2673.4$ grows like
$h^{2.31}$ ($x^{2.314\pm0.082}$) and exceeds the arch reserve by $2.7$--$1.98\times10^{3}$,
closing $0$ of $12$ --- no bound of the shape
$\lambda_{\min}(B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH})-\|B^{\mathrm{atom}}_{HH}\|$ can close R1$''$ for
\emph{any} damping of the atom mass, because what is being subtracted is not bounded at
all. The mechanism, identified: \textbf{on the block minimiser an arch part of
$1.4685$--$91.7130$ and an atom part of $-91.2694\ldots-1.1151$ cancel to
$\lambda_{\min}(B_{HH})=0.2661$--$0.4436$; the minimiser sees only
$6.16\times10^{-3}$--$5.03\times10^{-1}$ of the atom operator ($x^{-1.044\pm0.109}$), at
$52.7$--$90.0^\circ$ from the atom-extremal vector --- the positivity is an
\emph{alignment} fact, not a size fact}, and diagonal dominance fails as well
($\min_k(B_{HH})_{kk}=0.3997$--$0.8186$; the off-diagonal atom coupling eats
$38$--$63\%$ of the diagonal).

\emph{The balance, the stress, and the unchanged end to end.} The end-to-end fraction is
$3.28\times10^{-2}$--$2.83\times10^{-1}$, \emph{unchanged}: J1 and J2 are statements about
what is missing, and neither adds a certified inequality to the chain. The recovery,
paired like for like ($K=12$ fixed by contract, a wider surface, the pairing declared
before the number): $49.5$--$100.0\%$, median $99.8\%$, at or above $75\%$ on $12/16$
windows. The balance: $9$ theorem rungs ($3$ new: the $F(P,r)$ reduction, the chain
$r\le1/(Ls)\le1/p_1$, the lag decomposition), $6$ certified, $\mathbf{3}$
\textbf{measured} --- the zero-measured target is \emph{not} met, two of the three are the
open terms themselves, and the third (the model domination) is a new debt created by the
reduction, counted rather than hidden. The obligatory stress breaks on \emph{three} axes,
two of them new and both J1's own: the ceiling explodes at $x^{2.047\pm0.009}$ (T154
confirmed); $p_1$ --- the one scalar J1 reduces to --- \emph{collapses} to
$7.4\times10^{-15}$--$6.6\times10^{-10}$ on the no-go family ($x^{-4.818\pm0.080}$)
against $0.2010$--$0.3282$ real, so the one number J1 asks for is exactly the number that
separates the families; and the $r$-ceiling tightness separates too ($12.5$--$24.6$
against $1.03$--$1.16$). The floor survives ($t=0.05$), so a floors-only probe would have
seen nothing. \textbf{And the stress kills J1's one measured step}: the domination of the
eight-dimensional defect by the $2\times2$ model holds on $16/16$ real windows and
\emph{fails} on $8/8$ no-go sizes (model $0.977$--$0.982$ against truth
$0.9990$--$0.9996$, a narrow undershoot of $1.7\times10^{-2}$--$2.2\times10^{-2}$ ---
which is the point): it is not a theorem and cannot become one by more measuring on the
real family. Controls exact: parity $4.8\times10^{-14}$; $\mu^P_9$ to
$2.3\times10^{-13}$; $\mu^P_1$ to $2.0\times10^{-11}$ in the \emph{worthless}
configuration $W=\mathrm{span}\{t_2..t_{13}\}$ (the certificate reports its own
worthlessness); the Dirichlet negative control hits its own $2/\sqrt N$ prediction to
$7.4\times10^{-5}$.

\begin{keybox}[After T156: both terms resist --- two angles remain]
\emph{(O1)} \textbf{R2$''$, one $m$-free lower bound on $p_1$}: the squared overlap of
the bottom parity sine with the bottom eigenvector of the section, measured
$0.2010$--$0.3282$ ($55.1$--$63.4^\circ$), flat. Everything above it is now a theorem: the
$2\times2$ reduction to $F(P,r)$ is an identity, $r\le1/(Ls)\le1/p_1$ is two lines, and
$F$ is explicit --- a bound $p_1\ge p^*$ would give the $m$-free loss $F(P,1/p^*)$
directly ($0.672$--$0.799$ at the measured $p_1$). Separate second debt: the step from
the two-dimensional model to the eight Ritz directions, which holds on $16/16$ real
windows and fails on $8/8$ no-go sizes --- a good separation instrument, not a theorem.
\emph{(O2)} \textbf{R1$''$, one $m$-free alignment statement}: a lower bound for the arch
Rayleigh quotient \emph{on the subspace where the atom form is large}, equivalently an
$m$-free angle between the two extremal vectors --- \emph{not} a mass bound of any kind
(refuted with numbers: symbol arguments, additive splits, $\ell^1$ budgets, diagonal
dominance); the arch half is ready for it (a one-variable grid infimum
$0.8226$--$1.3973$, non-decreasing, factor $3.29$--$5.59$ over $t$). The verdict was
evaluated from the numbers: $2$ open terms and $3$ measured rungs, hence
\textsc{terms-resist}. T155's $12\times12$ certificate is strengthened as an
\emph{instrument} (exactness controls to $2.0\times10^{-11}$, self-reported
worthlessness, the no-go breaking on three axes) and weakened as a \emph{uniformity
claim} (its value is governed by the single scalar $p_1$, and the load-bearing
inequality of the reduction step fails on the no-go family) --- the honest
recommendation: promote it as a fixed-size certified instrument with its per-window
numbers, and promote nothing about uniformity. The honest state, in one sentence: after
T156 both remaining terms are single scalars --- one angle each --- whose $m$-freeness is
not a matter of measuring more windows but of proving one inequality each.
T157 (\texttt{angle\_floor\_probe.py}) is running at exactly those two angles.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{Neither angle falls, both change shape: the $p_1$ floor becomes a theorem
times one number, the arch half is certified (T157)}
T157 (\texttt{angle\_floor\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{ANGLE.FLOOR}, $32/32$,
$3.9$\,s on $16$ prime-power windows $h=142\ldots1293$, the alignment surface on $12$
windows $h=50\ldots1077$, verdict \textsc{angles-resist}, the gates evaluated from the
numbers: $p_1$ $m$-free \textsc{false}, $p_1$ non-trivial \textsc{true}, arch half
certified \textsc{true}, alignment $m$-free \textsc{false} --- terms $=2$) attacks the
two angles T156 left, and neither falls --- but both change shape. The instrument cores
below are promoted as \veri{v552\_angle\_instruments.py}.

\emph{The best $p_1$ route is the resolvent, and it splits into a theorem times one
number.} Write $\gamma=Te_1(A)$ for the parity coordinates of the bottom eigenvector and
split the modes at $k_b=16$. The tail is a \emph{theorem}, one line from the certified
pencil floor $A\succeq tL_P$ and the certified ladder ceiling
$\lambda_1\le S\mu^P_1$ alone:
\[
\|\gamma_H\|^2 \;\le\; \frac{\lambda_1}{t\,\mu^P_{17}} \;\le\;
\frac{S/t}{\rho_{17}} \;=\; 0.0165\text{--}0.0293 ,
\qquad \rho_{17}=\frac{\mu^P_{17}}{\mu^P_1},
\]
so $e_1(A)$ lives $97.1$--$98.4\%$ inside the first sixteen parity sines,
\emph{$m$-freely in shape} --- T146's measured ``$98$ per cent in the sine block'' now
has a one-line proof, and the lesson is the ceiling: substituting the pencil ceiling
$\kappa$ ($3.1\times10^{3}$--$2.7\times10^{6}$, growing $x^{2.821\pm0.038}$) for the flat
ladder $S=1.1676$--$2.1178$ ($x^{0.010\pm0.092}$) would make the bound vacuous
($43.5$--$38632$). What remains measured is \emph{one} number: $\hat
g_1^2=0.2010$--$0.3282$ (flat, $x^{0.054\pm0.029}$), the first coordinate of the bottom
vector of a $16\times16$ Schur null problem (solved to a relative residual
$8.4\times10^{-15}$), and the resulting floor $p_1\ge\hat
g_1^2(1-\mathrm{tail})=0.1968$--$0.3228$ is $97.9\%$ of the measured $p_1$. Three other
routes are refuted with numbers: the classical Rayleigh angle bound
$p_1\ge(\lambda_2-\mathrm{RQ})/(\lambda_2-\lambda_1)$ is \emph{empty already in its
measured form} ($16/16$ negative --- $\mathrm{RQ}(t_1)$ exceeds $\lambda_2$ by
$818$--$519458$, and the bottom is nearly degenerate, $\lambda_2/\lambda_1=1.73$--$5.87$:
the shape fails, no certification can rescue it); its block version answers the T156
question --- the chain \emph{does} admit the block, and the block mass is spectacular,
$p_{\mathrm{blk}}(2)=0.9369$--$0.9993$ ($t_1$ lives almost entirely in the bottom
\emph{pair}) --- but the block Rayleigh bound stays empty at every $J$ of the ladder; and
the angle-free Cauchy--Schwarz route $Ls\ge L/\hat a$ is a theorem that loses exactly the
Kantorovich product $P=5.6\times10^{2}$--$1.0\times10^{6}$, beating the $p_1$ floor on
$0$ of $16$ windows.

\emph{The structural gem: the whole first term is one diagonal entry.} There is an
identity nobody had used: $s=\mu^P_1\,t_1^{\mathsf T}A^{-1}t_1=(B^{-1})_{11}$, hence
$1/s$ is carried by the $(1,1)$ entry of the \emph{same} fixed-size $16\times16$ Schur
complement $S_L=B_{LL}-B_{LH}B_{HH}^{-1}B_{HL}$ that the T152..T157 chain already forms

\subsection{The cancellation-seeing bound exists, and it is a theorem: the entry as a
Dirichlet maximum, the growth pointer refuted (T158)}
T158 (\texttt{schur\_entry\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{SCHUR.ENTRY}, $36/36$,
$8.2$\,s on $28$ prime-power windows $h=254\ldots1393$, the band surface on $21$
windows $h=254\ldots1031$, verdict \textsc{entry-resists}, the gates evaluated from the
numbers: entry ceiling $m$-free \textsc{false} --- the cancellation depth grows
$x^{2.135\pm0.021}$ where $m$-free needs non-growing; entry ceiling sharp-and-uniform
\textsc{true} --- tightness $\le1.2738$, flat; domination margin non-shrinking
\textsc{false} --- trend $x^{-1.649\pm0.643}$ --- terms $=2$) attacks exactly the
cancellation-seeing bound T157 demanded, and it exists --- as a theorem.

\emph{The entry as a Dirichlet maximum, and the ladder of positive terms.} The object
that makes trial spaces legitimate in the right direction is the dual (Thomson) form of
the entry (Maz'ya 1985; Miclo 1999 --- $s$ is a \emph{conductance} of mode~$1$ into the
bulk, and every admissible flow is a floor):
\[
s \;=\; (B^{-1})_{11} \;=\; \max_x\,\bigl(2x_1-x^{\mathsf T}Bx\bigr),
\]
so \emph{every} trial vector is a lower bound on $s$ and hence an upper bound on $1/s$
--- the entry R2$''$ must ceiling. This is exactly the variational structure
Cauchy--Schwarz lacks: CS evaluates $b^{\mathsf T}B_{HH}^{-1}b=\max_z(2b^{\mathsf
T}z-z^{\mathsf T}B_{HH}z)$ at the \emph{single} direction $z\parallel b$, and it missed
by $3.13\times10^{3}$--$5.18\times10^{5}$ (reproduced with its direction intact on
$28/28$: what fails is sharpness, not sign --- the cancellation is spread over the low
modes, and one direction cannot see it). The Cholesky ladder $g_K=\sum_{j\le K}y_j^2$
with $y=L_K^{-1}e_1$ (the nested-Schur identity) writes $s$ as a sum of \emph{strictly
positive} terms with monotone partial sums on $28/28$ windows, and $1/g_1=\hat a$ is
exactly T157's route: the ladder starts where T157 ended. At $K=16$ --- the same low
block the T152..T157 chain already forms --- the certified ceiling is
$1/g_{16}=2.9670$--$7.9664$ against the true $1/s=2.3359$--$6.3868$, \emph{tight to
$1.1323$--$1.2738$}, ceiling trend $x^{0.059\pm0.017}$ (at $K=8$ already inside a
factor $1.767$). Directions checked before use: (M1) $1/s\le(S_L)_{11}$ with slack
$8095$--$1.013\times10^{5}$ on $28/28$ (Schur 1917 / Haynsworth 1968 --- T157's entry
is a ceiling on $1/s$, an inequality and not an identity), and no trial ever overshot
$s$.

\emph{The entry is two-dimensional.} The Green-column trial space is not a bound at all
--- it is the identity: $\mathrm{span}\{t_1,A^{-1}L_Pt_1\}$ attains $s$ exactly ($g/s=1$
to $10^{-9}$ on $28/28$), for a theorem reason --- $L_Pt_1=\mu^P_1t_1$ (KMS 1953), so
$A^{-1}L_Pt_1$ \emph{is} the Dirichlet maximiser. This settles that the entry is a
\emph{two-dimensional} quantity the moment one Green column is granted; that column
costs an $m$-sized solve, and the fixed-size sine truncation pays exactly the factor
$1.1323$--$1.2738$ for not needing it. The object the chain actually wants:
$L\,g_{16}=0.2143$--$0.2724$ against the true $Ls=0.2521$--$0.3413$, and with the
certified pencil floor $t$ in place of $L$, $t\,g_{16}=0.0314$--$0.0826$ --- the
Dirichlet ladder lands in the band of T157's \emph{measured} $p_1=0.2010$--$0.3282$,
without an angle.

\emph{The growth pointer, refuted --- an honest negative.} The growth T157 pointed at
is real and sub-quadratic: $f^{\mathrm{arch}}/(4\sin^2(\theta/2))\sim\theta^{-q}$ with
$q=1.259$--$1.438$ ($q<2$ says $f^{\mathrm{arch}}$ itself decays like
$\theta^{0.56\text{--}0.74}$ --- a partial cancellation of numerator and denominator,
not a clean pole), and the binding vector of the domination pencil sits exactly where
T157 said: $0.6818$--$0.9988$ of its mass in the \emph{lowest} dyadic band (centroid
$\theta/\pi=0.0191$--$0.0845$ --- the localisation half of the pointer is confirmed).
What is refuted is that the growth can pay for it: the atom negative mass grows like
$\theta^{-1.546\ldots-1.744}$, \emph{faster} than the certified arch floor's
$\theta^{-1.203\ldots-1.458}$ --- the low-$\theta$ limit belongs to the atom, and the
growth is a liability, not a resource. In the lowest band the arch floor covers only
$0.4161$--$0.4507$ of the atom mass, band-local domination \emph{fails in every band}
on $21/21$ windows, and the off-band coupling (Frobenius $1.612$--$27.97$, the
conservative direction) exceeds the available margin by $660$--$7.71\times10^{5}$:
what carries the inequality is precisely the structure a dyadic argument throws away.
T157's adaptive Lipschitz ceiling, re-run band by band, certifies $7$ of $116$
(band, window) pairs --- exactly the large-$\theta$ bands where the growth is not the
resource. The margin is $3.57\times10^{-5}$--$2.86\times10^{-3}$ with trend
$x^{-1.649\pm0.643}$, shrinking: R1$''$ stays a per-window certificate, and the verdict
gate reads it numerically.

\emph{The debt relabelled, the balance, the stress.} The containment
$\mathrm{span}\{t_1,A^{-1}L_Pt_1\}\subset S_{16}$ is exact ($5.84\times10^{-16}$ on
every window) --- nothing in the T156 debt is about the spaces --- but it cannot be
cashed: Ritz defects are not monotone in the trial space (smallest principal angle to

pretend otherwise). End to end, priced like for like: the substitution is
direction-clean and conservative (the substituted complement floor
$4.3904$--$6.5357\,\mu^P_1$ never exceeds the measured $5.7763$--$8.6051$), the Temple

\textbf{theorem} / $3$ certified-uniform / $4$ certified-per-window / $\mathbf 1$
\textbf{measured} (T157 stood at $5/2/3/3$): $p_1$ is \emph{retired} --- the ladder

The obligatory stress breaks on \emph{five} axes: $p_1$ collapses
($x^{-4.818\pm0.080}$), the true entry $1/s$ explodes to $1185$--$2.547\times10^{5}$,

negative control hits its own $2/\sqrt N$ prediction to $7.4\times10^{-5}$.

\begin{keybox}[After T158: the entry ceiling is a theorem plus one Cholesky --- two rests remain]
\emph{(O1)} \textbf{an $m$-free upper bound on one quadratic form}: $x^{\mathsf
T}B_{LL}x=2.9670$--$7.9664$ for a nearly universal fixed sixteen-vector (pairwise
alignment $0.8599$--$0.9976$ across the windows, normalised to $x_1=1$) --- nothing

$+2.395\times10^{4}\ldots+9.323\times10^{5}$, both of one sign across the surface, so

\emph{(O2)} \textbf{an $m$-free lower bound on $\lambda_{\min}(B_{HH})$ that is not

\subsection{The cancellation executed algebraically: seven identities, the gauge
identity, and the form is the weight (T159)}
T159 (\texttt{exact\_form\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{EXACT.FORM}, $41/41$,
$2.9$\,s on $23$ of $24$ prime-power zones $h=142\ldots1293$ ($70$--$24574$ atoms;
the sign surface on $18$ windows $h=142\ldots963$), verdict \textsc{form-resists},
the gates evaluated from the numbers: R2$''$ $m$-free \textsc{false} --- every
pricing of the transformed sum grows, best rung $h^{+3.604}$, every closed vector
grows, frozen $h^{+3.510}$; R1$''$ $m$-free \textsc{false} --- the sign structure
sits entirely on the archimedean side --- terms $=2$) executes T158's rest O1
symbolically. The algebra is delivered; the bound is not: \emph{the cancellation
is localised, and it is the weight}.

\emph{The symbolic sixteen-form: seven machine-checked identities.} All seven hold
to $10^{-12}$ against the absolute scale $\sum_d|c_d\,w_d|$ --- the honest bar,
because relative to the cancelled total the same identities hold only to
$1.0\times10^{-12}$--$1.2\times10^{-8}$: the cancellation eats $4.0$--$8.1$ decimal
digits in double precision, and that measured loss \emph{is} the quantitative
reason no $m$-free bound can be read off numerically. (P1) $x^{\mathsf
T}B_{LL}x=y^{\mathsf T}Ay$ with $y=\sum_k(x_k/\sqrt{\mu^P_k})\,t_k$ --- the pencil
is gone ($2.8\times10^{-17}$--$1.4\times10^{-15}$). (P2) the \emph{exact lag sum}
$x^{\mathsf T}B_{LL}x=\sum_d c_d\,w_d$ with $w_d=T_d-H_d$ ($T$ the autocorrelation,
$H$ the convolution of $y$): one explicit arithmetic sum with arithmetic ($c$) and
geometry ($w$) separated. (P3) $w_d$ in \emph{closed form}: a $256$-term
Dirichlet-kernel expression (Dirichlet 1829, product-to-sum) reproduces the
assembled weights to $1.42\times10^{-15}$--$2.85\times10^{-15}$ of $\sup|w|$ at
every lag of every window --- $w_d$ is a fixed-size trigonometric function of
$(d,h)$, no $m$-dependence beyond $N=2h+1$. (P4) the \emph{gauge identity},
the content of the module:
\[
\sum_d w_d \;=\; 0 \qquad\text{exactly},
\]
because $A_{rs}=c_{|r-s|}-c_{M-1-r-s}$ annihilates constant lag vectors
identically ($0.0$--$9.4\times10^{-14}$ of $\sup|w|$): \emph{the form is blind to
the lag mass of $c$ and sees only its variation} --- and the lag mass is exactly
where the archimedean and atom halves are $h^2$-sized and cancel. (P5) the two
closed scalars $w_0=\sum_k x_k^2/\mu^P_k$ (the $N^2/4\pi^2$ factor itself,
$2.655\times10^{5}$ at $h=1119$, relative error $\le4\times10^{-16}$) and
$2w_0-w_1=\|x\|^2$ exactly --- because $L_P$ is the odd Toeplitz
$(2,-1,0,\ldots)$ and the $t_k$ are its exact eigenvectors (KMS 1953): the huge
and the $O(1)$ scale sit in the \emph{same two weights}. (P6) the $p$-fold Abel
identity exact at every rung $p=1..5$ ($2.6\times10^{-20}$--$3.3\times10^{-16}$).
(P7) the Toeplitz-minus-Hankel signature $A_{r,s}-A_{r+1,s+1}=f(r+s)$
($1.1\times10^{-16}$--$1.5\times10^{-16}$) --- the premise of P4. Reproduction:
$x^{\mathsf T}B_{LL}x=1.7648$--$4.9008$ flat ($h^{-0.130}$; same object as T158's
$2.967$--$7.966$ on a different surface), halves $-9.605\times10^{5}\ldots
-9.828\times10^{3}$ against $+9.831\times10^{3}\ldots+9.605\times10^{5}$,
cancellation depth $1.86\times10^{-6}$--$3.56\times10^{-4}$ falling $h^{-2.234}$;
the sixteenth Cholesky rung stays sharp, $(1/g_{16})/(1/s)=1.0694$--$1.2509$.

\emph{$m$-free not reached: four routes closed with exponents.} The core negative
first: \textbf{the $h^2$ does not telescope away} --- $|$arch$|$ and $|$atom$|$
both grow $h^{+2.104}$, i.e.\ like $w_0=1/\mu^P_1$ itself. The $h^2$ is the common
\emph{weight} of both halves, not an archimedean artefact algebra could clear, and
it cancels only in the sum --- the gauge identity says why: each half alone
carries the lag mass against an $h^2$-sized weight. The four routes: (R1)
\textbf{T158's fixed sixteen-vector, refuted} --- frozen at one window the form
grows $h^{+3.510}$ ($3.025$--$6.997\times10^{5}$), with the reason closed:
$\mathrm{cond}(B_{LL})=1.223\times10^{5}$--$1.386\times10^{8}\sim h^{+2.887}$, so
a direction error $\varepsilon$ costs $\varepsilon^2\lambda_{\max}\sim
\varepsilon^2h^2$; a closed direction would have to be accurate to
$\kappa^{-1/2}=8.5\times10^{-5}$--$2.9\times10^{-3}\sim h^{-3/2}$, while the true
optimiser drifts by $1-\cos=2.52\times10^{-2}$--$1.47\times10^{-1}$ between
neighbouring zones --- a refutation, not a difficulty. (R2) one sine refuted:
$B_{11}=1/g_1=1.9\times10^{4}$--$2.1\times10^{7}\sim h^{+3.066}$, the price of
collapsing sixteen rungs to one is $4224$--$1.3\times10^{7}$ --- the
sixteen-dimensional minimum is irreducible, the cancellation lies \emph{across}
the sixteen. (R3) the preregistered ansatz family ($4$ forms $\times$ $10$
exponents, no fitting): the best member grows $h^{+3.001}$ --- no closed power
direction is flat. (R4) $\ell^1\times\sup$ pricing of the Abel sum at every rung
refuted: best rung $p=1$ with bound $1.54\times10^{7}$--$3.95\times10^{10}\sim
h^{+3.604}$, missing the target $1.765$--$4.901$ by $5.63\times10^{6}$--$2.21
\times10^{10}$, higher rungs worse ($p=5$: $h^{+7.718}$) --- the transformation
removes the lag mass ($\ell^1$ masses fall) but the surviving weight tails grow
exactly as fast ($\sup|W^1|=3.45\times10^{5}$--$2.00\times10^{8}\sim h^{+2.906}$,
and $W^1_1=-w_0$ identically, so $\sup|W^1|\ge w_0\sim h^2$ is unavoidable: the
transformation \emph{moves} the cancellation from the lag mass into the weight
tail, it does not remove it). Two $m$-free-shaped new pieces survive:
\textbf{$\|\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}}\|_1=3.6487$--$5.3788$ flat ($h^{+0.165}$)} ---
the T115 kernel has uniformly bounded variation $\le6.00$ in the zone --- and the
atom budget is T150-Chebyshev-correct, $\|\Delta c^{\mathrm{atom}}\|_1=37.0$--$191.7
\sim h^{+0.727}$ inside $\sum\mu_j\le4B\sqrt X$ at the \emph{atom cutoff}
$X=e^{2\alpha}$ (a pedantic correction: not the window size $N=2h+1$ --- a
different integer), occupancy $0.8767$--$0.9602$.

\emph{The sign law: the archimedean block is a Z-matrix, exactly.} (S1) holds raw:
\textbf{$B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH}$ is a symmetric Z-matrix} --- $100\%$ of the
off-band archimedean entries nonpositive, without similarity, on $18/18$ windows;
(S2) the checkerboard sign pattern is refuted ($0.4890$--$0.4936$ mass fraction $=$
a coin flip). Collatz--Wielandt bites on the archimedean half: the \emph{closed
sign-based floor} $\min_k(B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH}\mathbf 1)_k=0.8194$--$1.1647$,
flat ($h^{+0.176}$), comfortably above the target $t=0.25$ --- row sums of a
Z-matrix, an $m$-free-shaped object (Gantmacher--Krein 1950; the Perron root of
the off-band part sits a factor $2.2740$--$2.7262$ below its row-sum norm: the
signs pay). And it is not enough: the atom block obeys \emph{no} sign law
($0.3067$--$0.4891$ nonpositive $=$ noise), its off-band mass exceeds the
archimedean floor by $32.44$--$4555$ growing $h^{+2.330}$, and on the full block
the M-matrix criterion is vacuous: best power test vector
$\min_k(B_{HH}v)_k/v_k=-9.324\ldots-0.6086$ against the exact
$\lambda_{\min}(B_{HH})=0.0742$--$0.1974$. The verdict without hedging: the
archimedean sign structure is real, exact and usable, and it does not suffice,
because the object it would have to dominate has no sign structure.

\emph{Assembly, stress, and the numerical horizon.} End to end the chain still
certifies $\lambda_1(A)\ge t\,\mu^P_1$ per window with $t=0.0705$--$0.1583$,
recovery $0.0686$--$0.2164$ of the exact $\lambda_1(A)$ (a deeper zone surface
than T158's $0.287$--$1.0$ --- a surface difference, not a regression; and the
decisive reading: M1/M2 did \emph{not} move it --- the new theorems are
structural, not quantitative). The T145 no-go breaks $5/5$ (no Z-law, signature
defect $7.79\times10^{-2}$, M-matrix criterion vacuous despite positive
definiteness, the localisation referee $m/H_m$ diverges $h^{+0.821}$, diagonal
constancy violated); three directions re-verified before use (Thomson maximum
never overshot, Schur complement $\ge1/s$, Ritz ceiling); Dirichlet and parity
controls at $8\times10^{-15}$ with the $2/\sqrt N$ bound \emph{saturated} to
$0.999708$--$0.999995$. The balance moves $6/3/4/1\to\mathbf{13}$
\textbf{theorem} $/\,6$ certified-uniform $/\,4$ certified-per-window $/\,\mathbf 1$
\textbf{measured}: seven new theorems P1--P7 and three new certified-uniform rows
(U1 the Z-law, U2 the archimedean floor $\ge0.81$, U3 the bounded variation
$\le6$), zero new per-window rows, zero new measured rows. And a
\textbf{numerical horizon, declared as its own measurement}: one window dropped
because $\mathrm{cond}(B_{LL})>10^{12}$, the first at $h=1292$ --- beyond it the
sixteen-block is singular in double precision and the per-window optimiser does
not numerically exist. That is the same obstruction the cancellation depth
reports, seen from the other side. The theorem cores of T158\,+\,T159 are
ledger-carried as \vref{v553}
(\veri{v553\_exact\_form\_identities.py}): the dual form with the positive ladder,
the two-dimensional span, the gauge identity with the signature, the closed
scalars with the lag sum, and the Z-law with the Collatz--Wielandt floor ---
per instance, with the pairing bound and $m$-freeness explicitly typed open.

\begin{keybox}[After T159: one fully explicit pairing inequality remains]
\emph{(O1)} R2$''$ is now \textbf{one fully explicit inequality}: the form equals
$\sum_{d\ge1}(\Delta c)_d\,W^1_d$ with $\|\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}}\|_1\le6$ (U3,
$m$-free-shaped), $\|\Delta c^{\mathrm{atom}}\|_1=O(h^{0.73})$ inside the
Chebyshev budget, and $\sup|W^1|=53.88$--$504.72\times w_0$. What is missing is a
bound on the \emph{one pairing} that uses the \emph{correlation} between
$\Delta c$ and $W^1$ instead of their sizes: $\ell^1\times\sup$ is off by
$h^{3.7}$, and the cancellation to be recovered is exactly $h^2$. \emph{(O2)}
R1$''$ needs a third device for the atom off-band block that is neither a norm
(refuted in T158 by $660$--$7.7\times10^{5}$) nor a sign (refuted here, purity
$0.31$--$0.49$). \emph{(O3)} two cheap proofs would upgrade rows: U1 from the
Hankel half of the closed T115 kernel, U3 as a total-variation bound on the same
integral. Permanently off the list: the fixed sixteen-vector, the single sine,
power ans\"atze, Abel-$\ell^1$ at every rung, the checkerboard, the full-block
M-matrix. T160 (\texttt{pairing\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{PAIRING}) executed
exactly that attack --- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The pairing attacked through correlation: the sampling identity ---
the last term is a prime exponential sum (T160)}
T160 (\texttt{pairing\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{PAIRING}, $46/46$, $2.8$\,s on
$19$ of $20$ prime-power zones $h=199\ldots1256$ ($187$--$19593$ atoms per window;
the R1$''$ sub-surface on $8$ windows $h=199\ldots534$; one window dropped at the
declared T159 horizon $\mathrm{cond}(B_{LL})>10^{12}$, first at $h=1292$ --- not
fitted through), verdict \textsc{pairing-resists}, the gates evaluated from the
numbers: arch half inside the bar \textsc{true} (slack $1.95\times10^{-8}$ of the
$O(1)$ total); arch half non-growing at a fixed witness \textsc{false} ($0$ of
$120$ fixed pairs --- but floor-limited, see below); atom half inside the bar
\textsc{false} (best device $4.78\times10^{6}$); third R1$''$ device positive
\textsc{false} (floor $-7.93$) --- terms $=2$) attacks the one pairing
$\sum_{d\ge1}(\Delta c)_d\,W^1_d$ through its correlation structure. Two terms
remain open --- the same \emph{count} as T159, and that is the honest headline ---
but both are now \emph{located}, and one of them is no longer an algebra problem.

\emph{No oscillation: the sign-block count is closed, and the block device is
refuted by its own numbers.} $W^1$ has $J=3$ sign blocks on every window, flat
($h^{+0.000}$), with a \emph{closed} bound $J\le4(2\cdot16)+2=130$ from the
trigonometric zero count ($w_d$ is a piecewise trigonometric polynomial of degree
$\le32$; F\'ejer 1915): $W^1$ is one smooth \emph{three-lobe profile} with
quasi-period $0.332$--$0.333$ of the window, not an oscillation. The prefix ratio
$\sup|\Psi|/\sup|W^1|=83.5$--$569.8$ grows as $h^{+1.022}$ --- the quantitative
reason iterated Abel loses: each further summation by parts trades a factor $h$
of tail size for a factor $h$ of difference smallness, neutral in the exponent
and strictly worse in the constant. Consequently the Leibniz block device the
contract asked for is refuted \emph{quantitatively}: block-H\"older overshoots as
$h^{+4.115}$ and block-Abel as $h^{+4.131}$ --- $5.2$--$16.5$ times \emph{worse}
than the already-refuted $\ell^1\times\sup$ pricing at $h^{+3.595}$, because with
three blocks the block masses are of prefix size. The head peel is refuted too:
no proper split clears the bar on any window ($K^*=M$ on $19/19$), and the best
improper one ($K/M=0.97$) still overshoots the true pairing $Q=1.7527$--$6.0895$
by $60.3$--$4.80\times10^{3}$, growing as $h^{+2.428}$ --- the $h^2$ cancellation
itself, essentially undiminished.

\emph{The moment laws, and the second numerical horizon.} What carries on the
smooth half are three \emph{closed sign-definite moment laws}, new theorems,
machine-checked: $m_0=\sum_d w_d=0$ (the T159 gauge identity), $m_1=\sum_d
d\,w_d=-[S_0^2+2\sum_jP_j^2]\le0$ (the $\max(r,s)$ identity: minus a sum of
squares; $7.1\times10^{-16}$), and $m_2=\sum_d d^2w_d=-[2S_1-(M-1)S_0]^2\le0$ (a
\emph{perfect square}; $3.0\times10^{-16}$), with closure of $m_p$ in the moments
of $y$ for every even $p$ (verified at $p=2,4$): the pairing cannot see the lag
mass, and it sees a linear or quadratic trend only with a sign known in advance.
Against a \emph{fixed} polynomial witness (fraction $0.2$ of the lags, degree
$48$, the same pair on every window --- a device, not a fit) the smooth
archimedean half of the pairing is \emph{reproduced} to $0$--$2.44\times10^{-15}$
relative, worst slack $1.95\times10^{-8}$ of the $O(1)$ total on all $19$
windows. And a \textbf{second numerical horizon is declared} rather than hidden:
the measured residual is $4.12$--$428$ times the double-precision floor
$\varepsilon\,\sup|c^{\mathrm{arch}}|\,\|w\|_1$, so the surface reports the
arithmetic floor of the measurement and \emph{not} the witness error --- the arch
half is honestly reported as \emph{neither established nor refuted} on any
double-precision surface; only a symbolic Chebyshev bound on the T115 kernel
could decide it (rest item R-A below). Atom sparsity is refuted in one number:
the support is \emph{not} sparse --- it fills $0.3226$--$0.6377$ of the lag range,
because the prime-power gaps $\log(1+1/n)$ fall below the grid spacing $D$ as
soon as $n>1/D$; even the support-localised $\ell^1$ (exact position \emph{and}
exact local value of every atom, absolute values taken) misses by
$4.78\times10^{6}$--$2.64\times10^{9}$ growing as $h^{+3.505}$, while the required
relative precision on the atom half is the cancellation depth itself,
$|{\rm total}|/|{\rm atom}|=2.19\times10^{-6}$--$1.12\times10^{-4}\sim h^{-2}$.

\emph{The core of T160: the sampling identity.} The atom half of the pairing is a
\emph{weighted sampling} of the closed weight vector at the prime-power
positions --- a theorem, machine-checked to $1.0\times10^{-16}$--$2.9\times
10^{-15}$ of the absolute scale on every window:
\[
\sum_d c^{\mathrm{atom}}_d\,w_d
\;=\;-\frac12\sum_{n\le X}\frac{2\Lambda(n)}{\sqrt n}\;\widehat w(\log n)
\quad(\text{plus one reflected term below the grid}),
\]
with $\widehat w$ the linear interpolant of the closed weight vector --- and by
T159's Dirichlet-kernel form, $\widehat w(u)$ is a \emph{fixed} trigonometric
polynomial with frequencies $\pi(k\pm l)/\alpha+O(1/h)$, $k,l\le16$. So
\textbf{the atom half of R2$''$ is, identically, a finite combination of sums
$\sum_{n\le X}\Lambda(n)\,n^{-1/2}\cos(t\log n)$ at thirty-two explicit
frequencies $t$} --- needed to relative depth $2.19\times10^{-6}$--$1.12\times
10^{-4}=h^{-2}$, and measured to cancel only to $0.0000$--$0.3659$ of the trivial
mass bound. The consequence, stated with the fence in place: \emph{the $h^2$
cancellation is the intrinsic arithmetic hardness of the problem}, not an
artefact of the T115 assembly --- the geometric half is now evaluated down to the
arithmetic floor, so nothing geometric is left to trade against the prime sum.
$\sum_n\Lambda(n)\,n^{-1/2-it}$ is the \emph{shape} of a partial sum of a
Dirichlet series on the line $\operatorname{Re}s=\tfrac12$; that is reported as a
\emph{diagnosis} of where the $h^2$ lives, never as an input: the sums are
assembled from the finite von-Mangoldt table and nothing else, no zero of any
$L$-function is read, generated or approximated, no equivalence is claimed, and
Weil 1952 / Bombieri 2000 remains an address.

\emph{The third R1$''$ device: $\rho>1$, flat --- and its inequality form is
refuted.} On the sub-surface ($8$ windows, $\lambda_{\min}(B_{HH})=0.0748$--$0.2023$;
the Z-matrix and its Collatz--Wielandt floor $0.8811$--$1.0988$ reproduced
exactly): the rank/support route is refuted --- the effective negative rank of the
atom block is $0.455$--$0.634$ of the block dimension, so no fixed-size corner can
contain it; the corner device is refuted --- it prices the coupling by
$\|M_{12}\|_2=1.554$--$71.447$ and is T158's refuted norm route in disguise. The
surviving fact: $\rho=\min_{0\ne v\in V_-}(v^{\mathsf T}B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH}v)/
(-v^{\mathsf T}B^{\mathrm{atom}}_{HH}v)=\mathbf{1.0036}$--$\mathbf{1.0140}>1$ on
\emph{every} window, flat ($h^{-0.011}$) --- the archimedean block dominates the
atom block on every destructive direction, an \emph{angle} statement no norm can
see, and the first R1$''$ fact that is neither a norm nor a sign nor a rank
(\textsc{measured}: a generalised eigenvalue of two size-$h$ blocks). Its
inequality form $B_{HH}\succeq B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH}-(1/\rho)\,P_-
B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH}P_-$ is a theorem given $\rho$, with no arithmetic on the
right --- and as a device it is refuted: floor $-7.9261\ldots-1.0919<0$ on $8/8$,
because the margin $(1-1/\rho)\lambda_{\min}=3.76\times10^{-3}$--$1.24\times
10^{-2}$ loses to the archimedean cross-coupling $2.808$--$18.15$ between $V_-$
and its complement by a factor $10^{4}$. Any future device must use $\rho$
\emph{together with} the geometry of $V_-$ inside $B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH}$ ---
pricing that geometry by a norm is exactly what fails.

\emph{Two cheap theorems, the reassembly, the stress.} \textbf{U3 is upgraded
\textsc{cert-unif}${}\to{}$theorem}: $c^{\mathrm{arch}}$ is nonpositive and
monotone increasing on $d\ge1$ (both hypotheses machine-checked; fraction
$1.0000$ of $25458$ pairs), so the total variation equals the total rise and
$\|\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}}\|_1\le|c^{\mathrm{arch}}_0|+2\sup_{d\ge1}
|c^{\mathrm{arch}}_d|<6$ --- measured $3.9101$--$5.4153$ against the closed bound
$3.9105$--$5.4153$: \emph{four digits}, the constant closed and
window-independent. U1 is \emph{partially} upgraded, and the honest statement is
the interesting one: $K_{kl}(0)=0$ and $\sum_dK_{kl}(d)=0$ exactly, so
$R_{kl}(0)=R_{kl}(1)=0$ and the Abel step has no boundary term --- the Z-law of
$B^{\mathrm{arch}}_{HH}$ is \emph{equivalent} to one \emph{prime-free}
trigonometric inequality $\sum_{d\ge2}(\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}})_d\,R_{kl}(d)
\le0$ (the weight nonnegative by U3); it holds on every sampled pair, but the
pointwise strengthening $R_{kl}(d)\le0$ is refuted (it holds at only $0.4848$ of
the lags): the monotone weight is essential, and the statement is \emph{not} yet
a theorem and not reported as one. End to end, the number is the verdict: the
composite chain (arch half by the fixed witness, atom half by the
support-localised $\ell^1$) recovers $3.79\times10^{-10}$--$2.10\times10^{-7}$ of
the exact per-window value --- \emph{if the atom half were evaluated as exactly as
the arch half now is, the same chain would recover $1.0000$}: the whole deficit
of R2$''$ is carried by one term, of size $4.77\times10^{6}$--$2.64\times10^{9}$.
T159's certified per-window band $0.287$--$1.0$ is unchanged --- T160 moves the
