obstruction, it does not sharpen the number. The identities roll up worst-case at
$2.95\times10^{-12}$; the T145 no-go breaks on $\mathbf{6/6}$ axes including the
two new ones (A5 the gauge/moment structure --- the no-go form does not
annihilate constants, so the Abel step has no analogue on it; A6 the
complementarity --- $\rho$ is undefined on it); Dirichlet and parity eigenpair
controls at $8.2\times10^{-15}$ with the $2/\sqrt N$ bound saturated. The balance
moves $13/6/4/1\to\mathbf{14}$ \textbf{theorem} ($6$ new) $/\,4$
certified-uniform $/\,3$ certified-per-window $/\,3$ measured, with $8$ refuted
device families; the candidates T160-P1$\ldots$P7 (the moment laws; the sampling
identity; the block count with its refutation; the U3 upgrade; the U1 partial
upgrade; $\rho$; the second horizon) are all \textsc{pending} --- no promotion
here, and \vref{v553} is untouched.

\begin{keybox}[After T160: two classical rests, one arithmetic object, and the
circularity question]
\emph{(R-A)} one classical estimate: a symbolic Chebyshev bound for $s\mapsto
A(s,D)$ on $[0.2\cdot2\alpha,\,2\alpha]$ (the Bernstein ellipse of the T115
integral, whose only singularity is the $1/s$ head at the origin) --- it decides
the \emph{arch} half of R2$''$ $m$-freely, which no double-precision surface can
(T160-P7). \emph{(R-B)} one trigonometric inequality, prime-free:
$\sum_{d\ge2}(\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}})_d\,R_{kl}(d)\le0$ --- it turns the Z-law
(T159-U1) and with it the Collatz--Wielandt floor into a theorem. \emph{(R-C)}
the arithmetic term, and it is not an exercise: a bound on $\sum_{n\le X}
\Lambda(n)\,n^{-1/2}\cos(t\log n)$ at the thirty-two explicit frequencies
$t=\pi(k\pm l)/\alpha$, to relative depth $h^{-2}$ --- by the sampling identity
(T160-P2) this \emph{is} the atom half of R2$''$, and nothing geometric is left
to trade against it. \emph{(R-D)} a fifth device for R1$''$: $\rho$ together
with the geometry of $V_-$, without pricing that geometry by a norm.
\emph{(R-E)} optional: closed odd-$p$ moment functionals. T161
(\texttt{classical\_closure\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{CLASSICAL.CLOSURE})
executed exactly that programme --- the two classical rests R-A/R-B plus the
\emph{circularity triage} for R-C --- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The circularity triage: the hardness sits in the split, not in the
primes (T161)}
T161 (\texttt{classical\_closure\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{CLASSICAL.CLOSURE},
$35/35$, $1.2$\,s on $19$ log-spaced prime-power zones of $75$ admissible,
$h=50\ldots1445$ --- a $28\times$ lever arm --- with $\alpha=2.3979$--$6.4938$ and
atom cut-off $X=e^{2\alpha}=n_{\mathrm{zone}}^2$ exactly $=121$--$4.37\times10^{5}$;
$\psi(x)/x\le1.038830$ \emph{verified} at every jump point up to $n=400000$, the
unconditional input the triage prices; verdict \textsc{closure-resists}, triage
verdict \textsc{needs-beyond-rh-strength}) attacks R-A and R-B head-on and prices
R-C against the classical ladder.

\emph{R-A: the analytic half closes $m$-free, and the head needs no peeling.}
Two theorems anchor it: the T115 arch kernel is \emph{exactly}
$A(s,D)=D\,\widehat A(s,D)$ with $\widehat A$ the triangle smear of
$g(w)=e^{-w/2}/(1-e^{-2w})$ ($4.2\times10^{-16}$--$2.0\times10^{-13}$ against the
assembly on $19/19$), and the analyticity width is set by the $1/s$ head alone ---
the poles of $g$ sit exactly at $w=ik\pi$, and on $[0.4\alpha,2\alpha]$ the first
complex pole lands outside the Bernstein ellipse by margin $1.29$--$3.29$ on every
window. The Bernstein parameter is therefore \emph{closed and scale-free},
$\rho^*=(3+\sqrt5)/2=2.618034$ (it depends only on the interval ratio $5$; on the
surface $\rho(D)=2.5593$--$2.6160$), with the ellipse constant $M=3.06$--$5.93$
uniform in $h$ and the measured coefficients obeying the envelope at
$0.055$--$0.074\le1$ --- tight to $1.1$ orders. The new structure T161 contributes:
the smeared pole integrates in \emph{closed form}, so for every lag $d\ge1$
\[
c^{\mathrm{arch}}_d\;=\;\Psi_d+D\,\widehat G(dD,D),\qquad
\Psi_d\;=\;-\tfrac12\bigl[(d{+}1)\log(d{+}1)-2d\log d+(d{-}1)\log(d{-}1)\bigr],
\]
with $\Psi$ closed, $D$-free and $m$-free (the $\log D$ cancels identically;
agreement $1.7\times10^{-16}$--$4.8\times10^{-16}$ at \emph{every} lag of every
window) and $\widehat G$ the smear of the regularised $g-1/(2w)$ --- no head peel,
no fitted cut; on the full interval $[0,2\alpha]$ the closed rate
$\rho_{\mathrm{reg}}=2.05$--$3.38$ is \emph{not} scale-free
($\to1+\sqrt{\pi/\alpha}$). The ``fixed degree'' hope is refuted with a number:
both routes give a degree \emph{schedule} $K(h)=O(\log h)$ ($K=12$--$19$ peeled,
$9$--$25$ head-free; $dK/d\log h\approx2.0$ and $4.5$), because $\|w\|_1$ grows as
$h^{+2.85}$ (fit) against $D\sim h^{-1}$. The residual of R-A, named exactly: the
\emph{log-moment} $\sum_d\Psi_d\,w_d=2.15$--$3.14$ of the arch half
$=-\tfrac12\sum_d(d\log d)(\Delta^2w)_d$ --- prime-free, classical (a
Clausen/Lerch-type object), and \emph{not} in the polynomial moment ladder.

\emph{R-B: refuted in all four readings --- and the fraction bound survives.} The
contract's inequality $\sum_{d\ge2}(\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}})_d\,R_{kl}(d)\le0$ is
tested in all four of its readings before any proof is attempted, and all four
fail: per pair directly on $3168$ of $4320$ pairs (worst $+0.92$ of
$\|\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}}\|_1$), per pair in the Abel-tail reading on $1229$, the
\emph{aggregate} by \emph{sign} --- the arch half is negative on every window while
its off-diagonal block is positive, exactly the harmful direction for the needed
upper bound --- and the Abel route's sufficient condition on $3801$ of $4320$
(worst $+763$). The reason is structural: $R_{kl}$ is a difference of Dirichlet
kernels and changes sign in $d$, and the coefficients $a_ka_l$ change sign too ---
a one-sign statement was never the right object. The by-products are positive:
$(\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}})_d\ge4.5\times10^{-8}>0$ and decreasing, with a
total-positivity reason from the $\Psi$ split ($\Psi$ is minus the triangle smear
of the completely monotone $1/w$). What survives is weaker and usable:
$|\text{off-diagonal}|/|Q^{\mathrm{arch}}|=0.1035$--$0.1713$, flat in $h$ (exponent
$-0.116$, fit) over a factor $24$ --- a certified \emph{fraction} bound with the
constant $\tfrac14$, costing the chain a factor $1+\tfrac14$ in the constant and
nothing in the structure; its $m$-free version is a $16\times16$ Gram positivity
statement (Fej\'er 1915, Schur 1917), entirely prime-free.

\emph{The triage --- and the answer to the circularity question.} A new theorem
first: the thirty-two frequencies satisfy $t\,(2\alpha)=2\pi j$ \emph{exactly} for
$j=1\ldots32$ --- they are precisely the \emph{Fourier harmonics of the
log-window} $[0,2\alpha]$, so the atom half of the pairing is the vector of the
first $32$ Fourier coefficients of the measure
$\sum_n(2\Lambda(n)/\sqrt n)\,\delta_{\log n}$. The measured $0.00$--$0.37$
cancellation of T160 is then \emph{identified}: at the harmonics
$\theta=t\log X=2\pi j$ collapses the partial-summation main term to the closed,
parameter-free prediction $(\sqrt X-1)/(\tfrac14+t^2)$, which matches $S(t)$ to
$0.014$--$0.232$ of the trivial mass, improving as $X^{-0.39}$ (fit) --- the
$1/(\tfrac14+t^2)$ is the Mellin factor of $x^{-1/2}$, \emph{not} an arithmetic
saving; the genuinely arithmetic part is the residual against $d\psi(x)-dx$. The
$\delta$ arithmetic, compactly (the demand is $h^{-2}=X^{-\delta}$ with
$\delta=\log h/\alpha$ exactly, since $\log X=2\alpha$):

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}l l@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{strength} & \textbf{$\delta$ it buys}\\
\midrule
trivial / Chebyshev 1852 & $0$\\
zero-free region (de la Vall\'ee Poussin) & $c/\sqrt{\log X}\to0$ (no power saving)\\
van der Corput 1921 / Vinogradov 1937 & inapplicable ($t=0.5$--$42$ is $O(1)$; $j\le32$ turns)\\
harmonic-frequency geometry ($\sin\theta=0$) & $0.29$--$0.92$ (measured suppression $7.0$--$19.8$)\\
RH strength & $\tfrac12-o(1)$\\
\midrule
\textbf{needed (arch/atom split)} & $\boldsymbol{1.1482}$--$\boldsymbol{1.8809}$\\
\textbf{needed (arch+smooth / fluctuation re-split)} & $\boldsymbol{0.9839}$--$\boldsymbol{1.3767}$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\noindent The sharpest form of the same fact: the required \emph{absolute}
precision is $0.012$--$0.31$ of the \emph{last term} of the sum --- below the
boundary term $|\psi(X)-X|\,X^{-1/2}$ that every partial-summation bound carries,
so no strengthening of the $\psi(x)-x$ input (zero-free region, RH, or beyond)
lowers the floor of the method to it. And the re-split proves the demand is
\emph{split-dependent}: subtracting the smooth prime term
$-\int e^{u/2}\widehat w(u)\,du$ cancels the arch half to $0.50$--$0.76$ (the
explicit-formula pairing, confirmed), and the demand moves from
$\delta=1.148$--$1.881$ to $\delta_{\mathrm{eff}}=0.984$--$1.377$ --- it
\emph{moves} with the split, but stays above $\tfrac12$ on $18/18$.

\emph{The honest reading, stated prominently and soberly: the chain is not
circular.} It does not secretly need RH --- it needs \emph{more} than RH-strength
input would supply, and the demand is not even reachable by the partial-summation
framework at any input strength. The measured cancellation at the thirty-two
frequencies is fully the prime-number-theorem main term, with no arithmetic
surplus; the frequency geometry is genuinely special (worth $\delta=0.29$--$0.92$,
already inside the measured numbers) and does not close the gap. So the $h^2$ is
located in the \emph{split}, not in the primes: T161 refutes two splits with
numbers, and finding a third --- one with
$\delta_{\mathrm{eff}}<\tfrac12$ --- is the whole remaining R2$''$ task. The
controls are re-verified rather than inherited (Dirichlet kernel identity
$1.3\times10^{-15}$ including the degenerate branch, KMS eigenpairs
$7.1\times10^{-15}$, Chebyshev reconstruction $6.1\times10^{-15}$,
$\mathrm{odd\_toeplitz}(c^L)=L_P$ exact); the balance moves by
$+6$~theorem~$/+6$~certified-uniform~$/+1$~certified-per-window~$/+6$~measured~$/
+3$~refuted to $\mathbf{20}/10/4/9/3$. The closed cores of T160+T161 --- the
sampling identity, the moment laws with the TV theorem, the harmonic-frequency
theorem with the PNT prediction, the head split with $\rho^*$, and the fraction
bound with the sign refutation as its wired negative control --- are load-bearing
as \vref{v554} \veri{v554\_sampling\_harmonics\_identities.py}
(Section~\ref{sec:v554}); the $\delta$ triage itself is a comparison of strengths,
a documentation item, and is promoted nowhere.

\begin{keybox}[After T161: one moment, one matrix inequality, one split, one
device]
\emph{(R-A$'$)} one closed prime-free moment: the log-moment
$\sum_d\Psi_d\,w_d=-\tfrac12\sum_d(d\log d)(\Delta^2w)_d$, $2.15$--$3.14$ of the
arch half and outside the polynomial moment ladder (Clausen/Lerch address) ---
everything else in R-A is done, and a \emph{fixed} witness degree is provably not
available, only the schedule $K(h)=O(\log h)$. \emph{(R-B$'$)} one matrix
inequality, prime-free: the $m$-free version of the fraction bound
$|\text{off-diagonal}|\le\tfrac14|Q^{\mathrm{arch}}|$ --- a positivity/norm
statement for the $16\times16$ Gram form $(\Delta c^{\mathrm{arch}},R^1)_{kl}$
(Fej\'er 1915, Schur 1917), certified on every window today. \emph{(R-C$'$)} one
\emph{split}: not an exponential-sum bound --- the demand sits below the boundary
term of every partial summation --- but a split of the pairing with
$\delta_{\mathrm{eff}}<\tfrac12$; the arch/atom split gives $1.148$--$1.881$ and
the arch+smooth/fluctuation split $0.984$--$1.377$, both above $\tfrac12$, and
finding a third is the whole remaining R2$''$ problem. \emph{(R-D)} a fifth device
for R1$''$: $\rho=1.0036$--$1.0140>1$, flat, stays the surviving structure fact.
T162 (\texttt{third\_split\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{THIRD.SPLIT}) executed
exactly that search --- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The third split: the Mellin ladder saturates, and the Fej\'er split
goes sub-RH at a price (T162)}
T162 (\texttt{third\_split\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{THIRD.SPLIT}, $30/30$,
$5.2$\,s on the T161 surface rebuilt \emph{independently} from the declared
recipe: $19$ log-spaced prime-power zones of $75$ admissible, $h=50\ldots1445$,
of which $18$ windows sit inside the declared condition horizon
$\mathrm{cond}(B_{LL})\le10^{12}$, $h=50\ldots1218$; the pairing identity
re-checked to $9.98\times10^{-18}$--$3.01\times10^{-14}$ of the large scale and
the gauge identity to $2.5\times10^{-16}$; $\psi(x)/x\le1.038830$ verified at
every jump point up to $n=400000$, i.e.\ $\kappa=0.038821$ --- the \emph{one}
unconditional arithmetic input every number below is priced against; verdict
\textsc{delta-reduced}) searches for the third split, and the search returns
both the split and its limit.

\emph{The currency, declared before any candidate.} Two numbers are kept
strictly apart from here on, because T161 used only the first:
$\delta_{\mathrm{val}}=\log(|R|_{\mathrm{meas}}/|Q|)/\log X$ is the measured
residual \emph{value} --- a floor --- and
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}=\log(E_{\mathrm{triv}}\,C_w/|Q|)/\log X$ is what a
\emph{proof} must beat, with $E_{\mathrm{triv}}$ the Chebyshev-strength
(unconditional) size of the arithmetic factor. RH strength is $\tfrac12$ in both
currencies, as a comparison of strengths and never as a claim; always
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}\ge\delta_{\mathrm{val}}$. The taxonomy, in both
currencies (smooth part closed on every row):

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}l l l@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{split} & \textbf{$\delta_{\mathrm{val}}$ (floor)} & \textbf{$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}$ (demand)}\\
\midrule
C0 arch / atom & $1.1482$--$1.8809$ & --- (no factorisation)\\
C1 arch$+$smooth / fluctuation & $0.9839$--$1.3767$ & --- (no cell-level input)\\
C2 $=$ C1 $+$ Mellin ladder at $K^*$ & $0.6247$--$0.9307$ & --- (same)\\
C5 $=$ C2 $+$ one Abel step & $0.6247$--$0.9307$ & $1.3965$--$1.7867$\\
C3 spectral (ground pair, $\le16$ modes) & --- & $0.4602$--$1.3145$ (price $\sim h^{+2.93}$)\\
C4 Fej\'er taper (\texttt{fejer\_2}) & --- & $\boldsymbol{0.1332}$--$\boldsymbol{0.4169}$ (price $\sim h^{+2.86}$)\\
\midrule
frontier, price $\le2$ & & $1.319$--$1.650$\\
frontier, price $\le10^{2}$ & & $0.412$--$1.126$\\
frontier, price $\le10^{4}$ & & $-0.079$--$0.681$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

\emph{The Mellin ladder is the third genuine gain, and it is an asymptotic
series.} Past the PNT main term the smooth part of $d\psi$ is the derivative of
the \emph{elementary} closed function $-\tfrac12\log(1-x^{-2})$, so the $k$-th
rung pays $+\sum_dw_d\,C_d(-(2k+\tfrac12))$ in closed cell moments (Mellin
1896) --- no zero data anywhere. The residual is minimised at $K^*=2$ on all
$18$ windows (relative drop $0.9015$--$0.9256$ --- a genuine factor), and past
$K^*$ it \emph{rises} by $15.5$--$25.1$ up to $K=20$: the predicted
log-divergence of the formal sum $\sum_kx^{-2k-1}=1/(x(x^2-1))$, not a
numerical artefact. What it buys: $\delta_{\mathrm{val}}=0.6247$--$0.9307$
against C1's $0.9839$--$1.3767$, a forced (not fitted) gain of
$0.359$--$0.446$ --- and it \emph{cannot} be iterated to the missing
$X^{0.12}$--$X^{0.43}$, because the series diverges. C0 and C1 reproduce
T161's $1.148$--$1.881$ and $0.984$--$1.377$ to $0.01$ at both ends on the
independently rebuilt surface.

\emph{One Abel step, and R-C$'$ stops being an arithmetic problem.} Level $0$
admits no unconditional input at all (no cell-level Chebyshev bound --- T161's
granularity finding restated); one Abel step, licensed by the gauge identity,
gives $|V_d|\le2\kappa\sqrt X$ by two partial summations, and the ladder
identity $\sum_dv_dw_d=\sum_dV^{(k)}_d(\Delta^kw)_d$ is machine-checked at
every level $k=1\ldots4$ ($3.9\times10^{-15}$--$3.1\times10^{-14}$, boundary
free). The optimal level is \emph{exactly one} on $18/18$, for a closed reason:
each further step multiplies the envelope by ${\sim}2/D$ and divides
$\|\Delta^kw\|_1$ by ${\sim}\omega_{16}$, and the product is
$32\pi/\alpha=16.7$--$41.9>1$ --- partial summation is a single step, and it has
been taken. At that level the demand factorises \emph{exactly} as
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}\;=\;\tfrac12+\frac{\log\!\bigl(2\kappa\,\|\Delta
w\|_1/|Q|\bigr)}{\log X},
\]
so every arithmetic input sits in the single constant $\kappa$ and the
remaining question is the closed, \emph{prime-free} ratio
$\|\Delta w\|_1/|Q|=2.25\times10^{3}$--$1.15\times10^{6}$, growing as
$h^{+1.769}$ (fit); an RH-strength input misses the corresponding test
statistic by $4.8$--$8.2$ orders of magnitude.

\emph{The Fej\'er split, and the price of going below one half.} The Thomson
dual makes every trial vector $x$ with $x_1=1$, $Q(x)>0$ admissible at the
price $P(x)=Q(x)/Q(x^*)\ge1$ in the $1/s$ ceiling --- and the objective must be
priced, or it is gamed: an \emph{unpriced} search does find
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}<0$ here, by making $Q(x)$ huge and the bound vacuous.
Priced ($778$ trial vectors per window, the fast path re-assembled against a
literal double loop at $0.0$), the result is an exchange rate: a sub-$\tfrac12$
demand \emph{exists} on every window, at minimum price
$P_{\min}=7.2\times10^{1}$--$8.2\times10^{4}$ growing as $h^{+2.0}$ (fit), and
every unit of $\delta$ costs $1.17$--$3.31$ \emph{decades} of price. The
structured families beat the sweep: the spectral truncation C3 reaches
$0.4602$--$1.3145$ (below $\tfrac12$ on $5/18$), and the \textbf{Fej\'er taper
C4} --- $x_k$ weighted by $1-k/n_b$ (Fej\'er 1915), which by self-adjointness
of the smoothing \emph{is} the contract's ``pairing against Fej\'er-averaged
$\Lambda$-mass'' --- reaches
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}=\mathbf{0.1332}$--$\mathbf{0.4169}$, \emph{below
$\tfrac12$ on all $18$ windows}, lowering the demand by $1.15$--$1.51$ in
$\delta$ against the untapered optimiser. The catch, stated without hedging:
its price grows as $h^{+2.86}$ (fit), so the sub-RH demand is bought with an
asymptotically diverging loss in the $1/s$ bound, and a per-window certificate
at growing price is not a uniform statement --- R2$''$ is \emph{relocated} into
the price, not closed.

\emph{R-A$'$ closes, R-B$'$ is refuted.} The log-moment $L=\sum_d\Psi_dw_d$ ---
the one non-polynomial moment of the arch half --- agrees on three independent
routes: the direct sum; the double-Abel form \emph{with} its Wronskian boundary
term, $L=-\tfrac12\sum_d(d\log d)(\Delta^2w)_d-\tfrac12M\log M\,w_{M-1}$
exactly ($2.1\times10^{-15}$--$4.2\times10^{-14}$; the boundary term is
$3.2\times10^{-6}$--$3.5\times10^{-2}$ of $L$ and not optional --- T161's
identity is completed here, not quoted); and the Lerch/Frullani integral
\[
L\;=\;-\tfrac12\int_0^\infty\frac{(1-e^{-y})^2}{y^{2}}\,G(y)\,dy,\qquad
G(y)=\sum_{d\ge1}w_d\,e^{-(d-1)y}\ \text{closed},
\]
agreeing with the direct sum to $0.0$--$6.0\times10^{-16}$ --- machine
precision --- and converging at $y=0$ for exactly one reason, the gauge
identity; the $d=1$ term peels in closed form via
$\int_0^\infty((1-e^{-y})/y)^2dy=2\log2$, and the same constant reproduces
$\Psi_1=-\log2$ to $0.0$, an independent confirmation of the whole derivation
(Frullani 1828 / Lerch 1887 / Clausen 1832). R-A$'$ moves from open to
certified-per-window; it is $m$-indexed, and no $m$-freeness is claimed. R-B$'$
is \emph{refuted}, and the refutation is a result: the $16\times16$ Gram form
\emph{is} the arch half ($a^{\mathsf T}Ga=Q^{\mathrm{arch}}$ to
$0.0$--$1.9\times10^{-15}$, a theorem) and it is \emph{indefinite on every
window}, $\lambda_{\min}/|\lambda_{\max}|=-13.34\ldots-1.59$, zero of $18$
windows semidefinite in either sign; the mechanism is measured --- the diagonal
is strictly positive but small, the unweighted Gershgorin ratio is
$7.97$--$580.76$, so Gershgorin 1931 does not apply and no semidefiniteness
certificate exists. What survives is the $a$-weighted quarter bar: off-diagonal
mass against the arch half $=0.1435$--$0.2902$, flat (exponent $-0.102$, fit),
holding on $14$ of $18$ windows and exceeded by $16.1\%$ on four --- reported
honestly as $0.29$ and not as $\tfrac14$: a bound on a \emph{contribution}, not
a spectral property.

\emph{The assembly, the stress, and the anti-fitting refusal.} The full chain
$Q=(Q^{\mathrm{arch}}+Q^{\mathrm{smooth}}_K)+R$ closes end to end at
$6.1\times10^{-17}$--$1.8\times10^{-15}$ of the large scale
$\max(|\mathrm{arch}|,|\mathrm{atom}|)$ --- one unbroken chain of identities
followed by exactly one inequality, which holds with $2.0$--$3.2$ orders of
slack; the gap $\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}-\delta_{\mathrm{val}}=0.77$--$0.86$
\emph{is} the price of factorising, and it is bigger than the $0.12$--$0.43$
separating the residual value from RH strength: the factorisation, not the
arithmetic, now dominates the loss. The must-break controls break --- uniform
surrogate prime powers (same mass multiset) drive the total to
$5.2\times10^{2}$--$4.6\times10^{7}$ of $|Q|$, and violating the gauge breaks
the Abel identity by \emph{precisely} $c_0\sum_dw_d$ (reproduced to
$1.9\times10^{-14}$, a positive control on the mechanism) --- while a control
that did \emph{not} break is declared as information: $4\times$
under-resolution leaves the total $O(1)$ ($0.41$--$1.83$), so the cancellation
does not rest on resolving individual prime powers. And the anti-fitting
refusal, the most uncomfortable number of the probe, reported in full: the
exponent $\beta=\tfrac12$ in the smooth prime term is \emph{forced} by the
$n^{-1/2}$ weighting; the empirical minimiser over $[0.2,0.8]$ is
$\beta^*=0.600$--$0.800\ne\tfrac12$, where the residual would look up to a
hundred times better --- and it is \emph{refused}: the drift is a property of
the residual being large ($50$--$76\%$ of the object), not evidence about the
exponent. The verdict, in the two currencies: the $\delta$ trajectory
$1.88\to1.38\to0.93$ is real and monotone and does \emph{not} reach $\tfrac12$
(the best provable demand after the one Abel step is $X^{0.90}$--$X^{1.29}$
beyond RH strength), and the exhaustion \emph{saturates rather than
converges} --- three independent ladders all turn around at their first or
second step. The balance of T162: $10$~theorem~$/\,2$~certified-uniform~$/\,
3$~certified-per-window~$/\,9$~measured, zero fit rows (the only fitted numbers
are $h$-exponents, labelled in place); the candidates T162-P1$\ldots$P6 (the
closed log-moment; the Abel form with its boundary term; the quarter bar; the
Gram indefiniteness --- a negative result that closes a route; the Abel-level
theorem; the exchange rate) are all \textsc{pending} --- no promotion here, and
\vref{v554} is untouched.

\begin{keybox}[After T162: one front, one substitute, one device]
\emph{(R-C$''$)} the Pareto front, now prime-free: find an admissible trial
vector $x$ with $\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}(x)<\tfrac12$ at a price $Q(x)/Q(x^*)$
the T159/T160 chain can pay --- such $x$ exist at price
$\ge7.2\times10^{1}$ growing as $h^{+2.0}$, and both ways out are closed
questions: fix the affordable price from the chain and read the frontier, or
enlarge the search space beyond the $16$ low modes, where the total variation
may drop at constant price. \emph{(R-B$''$)} a substitute for the refuted Gram
positivity: the chain wanted a \emph{sign} and has a contribution bound (the
$a$-weighted quarter bar, certified-uniform via flatness). \emph{(R-D)} a
fifth device for R1$''$: $\rho=1.0036$--$1.0140>1$, flat, untouched by T162.
T163 (\texttt{pareto\_front\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{PARETO.FRONT}) executed
exactly that survey --- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The Pareto front: the front resists as a theorem, and the $h^2$ is
the parity spectral gap (T163)}
T163 (\texttt{pareto\_front\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{PARETO.FRONT}, $32/32$,
$1.9$\,s on a surface rebuilt with declared caps: $28$ log-spaced prime-power
zones of $70$ admissible, $h=142\ldots1445$ --- a $10\times$ lever arm, with
$H_{\min}=128$ declared as twice the largest mode block $K=64$ --- of which
$27$ windows sit inside the condition horizon
$\mathrm{cond}(B_{LL})\le10^{12}$; the closed weight vector re-derived as a
\emph{correlation form}, $w_0=A_0$, $w_d=2A_d-H_{M-1-d}$ with $A$ the
autocorrelation and $H$ the self-convolution of $v=T_K^{\mathsf T}a$, to
$1.6$--$2.0\times10^{-15}$ --- $O(h^2)$ and block-size-free, which is what
makes the sweeps affordable; pairing identity to
$5.9\times10^{-17}$--$9.5\times10^{-14}$ of the large scale, cancellation
headroom $\ge10$ decades over double precision, declared;
$\psi(x)/x\le1.038830$ verified at every jump point up to $n=400000$,
$\kappa=0.038821$; verdict \textsc{front-resists}) fixes the affordable price
\emph{from the chain} and reads the front --- and the answer arrives as a
theorem rather than as a search result. The theorem-shaped cores of T162 and
T163 are promoted as \vref{v555} \veri{v555\_pareto\_tv\_identities.py}
(Section~\ref{sec:v555}).

\emph{The price axis is chain-derived, not invented.} $Q(x^*)=1/g_{16}$
certifies that the T160 optimiser \emph{is} the top rung of the T158 Cholesky
ladder ($2.3\times10^{-13}$--$2.1\times10^{-8}$, below the conditioning bar
the solve carries); the rung prices $P_{\mathrm{rung}}(K)=g_{16}/g_K\ge1$ are
prices the chain has \emph{already paid}, since $1/g_K$ is an upper bound on
$1/s$ it already accepts; and the affordable price is preregistered as
$P_{\mathrm{aff}}=P_{\mathrm{rung}}(1)=g_{16}B_{11}=3.93\times10^{3}$--$1.01\times10^{7}$,
growing as $h^{+3.049}$ (fit) --- the T157 route-(0) certificate
$1/s\le B_{11}$, the loosest rung the chain has ever used. The Fej\'er knob
$t_k(\sigma)=\max(0,1-k/\sigma)$ (Fej\'er 1915; $50$ geometric grid points on
$[1,4096]$ plus $\infty$) has \emph{both endpoints in the chain}: $\sigma=1$
is exactly the $K=1$ rung ($0$--$3.9\times10^{-15}$) and $\sigma=\infty$ the
untapered optimiser, i.e.\ the $K=16$ rung. Price and demand are
\emph{measured} monotone in opposite directions along the knob at all
$27\times50$ grid points (every point admissible), so the knob curve \emph{is}
the Pareto front: there is no interior optimum to find, and the only question
is where the chain can afford to sit. Read at the declared prices, the flat
caps $1.25/2.00/10.00$ give $\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}=1.310$--$1.756$ /
$1.263$--$1.686$ / $1.102$--$1.375$, and the flat rung tiers the same ---
\textbf{$0/27$ windows below the yardstick $\tfrac12$ at any flat price};
only the full $P_{\mathrm{aff}}$ reaches
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}=-0.004$--$0.019$ on $27/27$. The crossing price is
$P_{\mathrm{cross}}=8.05\times10^{2}$--$1.01\times10^{5}\sim h^{+1.906}$
(fit), and $P_{\mathrm{cross}}/P_{\mathrm{aff}}=0.0066$--$0.2047$: the
crossing sits $5$--$152\times$ \emph{strictly inside} the certificate the
chain already accepts, with the margin \emph{widening} in $h$ --- the one
genuinely new positive of the part, stated without inflation, because a
per-window bound at a price growing like $h^2$ is not a uniform statement.

\emph{The price anatomy is an identity, not a fit.} Substituting
$P(x)=g_{16}|Q(x)|$ into the definition of the demand gives, for every
admissible trial vector and with no asymptotics,
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}(x)\;=\;\tfrac12+\frac{\log\!\bigl(2\kappa\,g_{16}\,
\mathrm{TV}(x)/P(x)\bigr)}{\log X},\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}(x)<\tfrac12\iff P(x)>2\kappa\,g_{16}\,\mathrm{TV}(x),
\]
machine-checked at all $27\times50$ grid points
($0.0$--$7.0\times10^{-14}$): \textbf{price and demand are two coordinates on
one object}, the trial vector enters only through the single ratio
$\mathrm{TV}(x)/|Q(x)|$, and the ``exchange rate'' T162 measured is a change
of variables, not a second lever. The crossing exponent \emph{decomposes
additively} --- TV at the crossing grows as $h^{+2.013}$, $g_{16}$ as
$h^{-0.061}$, sum $+1.952$ against the directly fitted $+1.906$ --- so the
$h^2$ sits in the total variation and nowhere else. The taper's structural
gain in TV is real and \emph{bounded}: a factor $2.75$--$4.64$, $h$-flat,
worth at most $0.276$ of $\delta$ and decaying like $1/\log X$; where the
price moves, $\tau_{\mathrm{TV}}=-0.0191$ (median) says every remaining unit
of $\delta$ is paid one-for-one out of the price. And the second half of the
anatomy identifies the object: the cancellation quality
$\mathrm{CANC}(x^*)=|Q|/\max(|Q^{\mathrm{arch}}|,|Q^{\mathrm{atom}}|)
=2.2\times10^{-6}$--$3.6\times10^{-4}$ ($h^{-2.039}$) jumps to
$0.449$--$0.934$ at $\sigma=2$ --- \emph{the taper destroys the arch/atom
cancellation}, and the price is the cancellation depth read backwards.

\emph{The search space, and then the theorem that makes the sweeps
unnecessary.} Enlarging the block, $K=16\to32\to64$, lowers TV only by
$0.868$--$0.958$ at a price \emph{dividend} ($0.81$--$0.94$) and makes the
demand \emph{worse} (up to $+0.0135$); the TV exponent is unmoved
($+1.832/+1.820/+1.810$); the best closed candidate --- the Fej\'er-weighted
$64$-mode sum --- gives a TV factor $0.843$--$0.931$ and no crossing; and the
pooled flat-price best over everything built is
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}=1.331$--$1.788$. Then the sweeps can be put aside,
because the question they were probing has an exact answer:

\begin{keyeq}
\textbf{(T1)}\ $w_0(x)=\|a(x)\|^2$\quad\textbf{(T2)}\
$\mathrm{TV}(x)\ge|w_0(x)|$\quad\textbf{(T3)}\ $x_1=1\Rightarrow
\|a\|^2\ge1/\mu^P_1$\quad$\Longrightarrow$\quad
$\displaystyle\mathrm{TV}(x)\ \ge\ \frac1{4\sin^2(\pi/N)}\ \sim\ h^2$
\end{keyeq}

\noindent for \emph{every} admissible trial vector in the parity sector ---
(T1) because the parity rows are orthonormal ($0$--$5\times10^{-16}$), (T2) by
telescoping with $w_M=0$, (T3) because the Thomson normalisation is not free.
Verified on all $1674$ trial vectors built anywhere in the probe ($50$ taper
widths $\times$ $4$ weightings $\times$ $3$ block sizes), with slack
$\mu^P_1\mathrm{TV}=5.00$--$23.20$ --- the floor is tight to a factor of
order ten --- and the floor itself
$2.06\times10^{3}$--$1.77\times10^{5}\sim h^{+1.997}$ (fit; exactly $h^2$ in
closed form since $N=2h+1$). \textbf{(T4)} Combined with the crossing
criterion: every $x$ with $\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}<\tfrac12$ must pay
$P>2\kappa g_{16}/\mu^P_1=5.46\times10^{1}$--$5.87\times10^{3}\sim
h^{+1.937}$, already $5.5$--$590\times$ above the largest declared flat cap
--- \emph{a flat-price sub-$\tfrac12$ demand is provably impossible on this
surface}, for every admissible trial vector and not merely for the families
swept. R-C$'''$ (``bounded total variation at bounded price'') is thereby
\textbf{closed negatively}, by an inequality.

\emph{Never in the primes --- the sober reading.} The relocation T162
suspected is exact, and its $h^2$ is now identified: the $h^{2.86}$ of T162's
Fej\'er price, the $h^{1.91}$ of the crossing price and T161's granularity
are \emph{all} the reciprocal smallest parity eigenvalue --- the spectral gap
of the parity Laplacian (Kac--Murdock--Szeg\H{o} 1953) meeting the entry
normalisation $x_1=1$. Sub-$\tfrac12$ demand at flat price is impossible in
the parity sector as long as $1/s$ must stay $O(1)$, which is the whole point
of the T152--T160 chain; the statement involves no prime, no taper and no
truncation --- and the mode sweep confirms it from the other side, since
$16\to64$ modes buys a price dividend, a worse demand, and leaves the TV
exponent at $h^{+1.81}$, a bounded factor above the theoretical floor.

\emph{R-B$''$, R-D, the stress and the anti-fitting control.} The chain never
needed the sign: in the upper direction $1/s\le Q(x)$ is Legendre duality
plus an \emph{evaluated} positive number, with headroom $\ge10^{14.9}$ over
the rounding floor on every window; T162's indefiniteness is reproduced
($a^{\mathsf T}Ga=Q^{\mathrm{arch}}$ to $9.3\times10^{-13}$,
$\lambda_{\min}/|\lambda_{\max}|=-14.6\ldots-2.2$); what the sign would have
bought is \emph{uniformity} --- the certified cancellation quality at the
operating point drifts ($h^{-0.172}$) --- so R-B$''$ reduces to R-B$'''$:
make the positivity margin $h$-uniform (T162's $a$-weighted quarter bar is
the right shape of object). R-D is a type mismatch: the taper acts on the
trial vector while the block floor $1/g_K$ is a property of the
\emph{operator}; smoothing the operator instead (a Fej\'er $3$-tap average of
the lag coefficients) degrades the floor by
$2.3\times10^{3}$--$2.7\times10^{5}\sim h^{+2.036}$ --- the same $h^2$ again,
for the same reason --- and bounds a different number: a measured negative,
not a device. The must-break controls break: the uniform surrogate drives the
total to $7.7\times10^{2}$--$4.7\times10^{7}$ of $|Q|$, the gauge violation
to $3.4\times10^{-2}$ of $\|w\|_1$, and the T145 resolution no-go breaks
\emph{monotonically} over $\nu=4\to2\to1\to0.5\to0.25$ with damage
$1.0\to9.1\to25.4\to129\to434$ (maxima; the $\nu=4$ column an exact null
control) --- monotone in the collision rate, which is what makes it the T145
mechanism rather than a generic loss of accuracy. And the anti-fitting
control is enforced rather than promised: a single globally fixed knob
setting $\sigma=3$, calibrated on the smallest window alone, delivers
$\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}=0.176$--$0.380$ out of sample on all $26$ remaining
windows at $0.14$--$0.23$ of $P_{\mathrm{aff}}$ --- no per-window tuning
anywhere. The balance of T163: $11$~theorem~$/\,1$~certified-uniform~$/\,
4$~certified-per-window~$/\,10$~measured, zero fit rows (the only fitted
numbers are $h$-exponents, labelled in place).

\begin{keybox}[After T163: one successor with two prime-free arms]
\emph{(R-C$'''$)} \textbf{closed, negatively, on this construction}: bounded
total variation at bounded price is impossible in the parity sector ---
$\mathrm{TV}(x)\ge1/\mu^P_1\sim h^2$ for every $x$ with $x_1=1$, an
inequality over the whole admissible set. \emph{(R-E)} the successor the
theorem points at, both arms prime-free: \emph{arm A} --- show that the
downstream T159/T160 chain tolerates a \emph{growing} $1/s$ ceiling (a
question about the chain, not about the pairing); \emph{arm B} --- represent
the entry functional in a sector whose lowest eigenvalue does \emph{not}
vanish like $h^{-2}$. \emph{(R-B$'''$)} make the positivity margin
$h$-uniform (the certified $\mathrm{CANC}$ at the operating point drifts,
exponent $-0.172$; the $a$-weighted quarter bar is the right object).
\emph{(R-D)} a fifth device for R1$''$: $\rho=1.0036$--$1.0140>1$, flat,
untouched by the Fej\'er perspective for the type reason above. T164
(\texttt{sector\_change\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{SECTOR.CHANGE}) decided
both arms of exactly that successor --- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The sector change: the $O(1)$ gate discharges to a quantifier, and
sectors are a gauge (T164)}
T164 (\texttt{sector\_change\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{SECTOR.CHANGE},
$28/28$, $31.7$\,s, the T163 surface rebuilt and re-verified: $28$ log-spaced
prime-power zones of $70$ admissible, $h=142\ldots1445$ inside the declared
caps, $27$ windows inside the condition horizon
$\mathrm{cond}(B_{LL})\le10^{12}$; pairing identity to
$2.2\times10^{-16}$--$1.0\times10^{-13}$ of the large scale, T163's TV floor
reproduced at the untapered optimiser ($\mu^P_1\mathrm{TV}=13.77$--$23.20$);
$|\psi(x)-x|\le\kappa x$ with $\kappa=0.038821$ verified at every jump point in
$[100,4\times10^{5}]$; verdict \textsc{tolerance-carries} (arm A) /
\textsc{sector-resists} (arm B)) decides both arms of the successor R-E, and
the two answers reshape the map rather than merely extending it.

\emph{Arm A --- the tolerance analysis, and the power is exactly one.} The
chain does not use $1/s$; it uses a ceiling $U$ with $1/s\le U$, and T164
instruments every downstream station with the direction of its arrow. ST1, the
direction check: $s\ge g_{16}\ge g_1$ window by window, i.e.\
$1/s\le1/g_{16}\le1/g_1=B_{11}$ --- the T158 ladder really is a chain of
\emph{upper} bounds on the entry ceiling and the T157 route-(0) rung really is
the loosest; $P_K=\hat a\,s\ge1$ is the Kantorovich admissibility the T156
kernel needs. ST3, the heart: at $U=1/g_{16}$,
\[
\frac{d\log(1-F)}{d\log U}=-1.0005\ldots-1.0000,\qquad
\frac{d\log r}{d\log U}=+1.0000\ \text{exactly},
\]
so inflating the ceiling by $\lambda$ shrinks the T156 loss margin by
$\lambda^{-1.00}$: \textbf{the kernel spends the ceiling at power exactly one},
and a ceiling growing like $h^{\varepsilon}$ costs a margin decaying like
$h^{-\varepsilon}$, algebraically, for every $\varepsilon>0$ (measured for the
power, theorem for the monotonicity). The end-to-end $\varepsilon$-scan
confirms it --- the exponent of the declared proxy
$T_{\mathrm{marg}}=(1-F)\,L$ falls by exactly one unit per unit of
$\varepsilon$ ($+0.391$ at $\varepsilon=0$ down to $-1.609$ at $\varepsilon=2$)
--- and the declared one-sided rule returns $\varepsilon^*=0.50$, which the
probe \emph{disowns} at once: the $\varepsilon=0$ baseline already carries a
tailwind of $h^{+0.391}$, bought entirely from the measured drift of
$L=\lambda_1(A)/\mu^P_1$ ($h^{+0.196}$) on this surface, and $\varepsilon^*$ is
nothing but that tailwind divided by power one. No structural slack; the
$O(1)$ requirement was real.

\emph{The quantifier collapse --- the key result of arm A.} But who asked for
a growing ceiling? T163's price grows because it was buying a
\emph{sub-yardstick demand}; the ceiling the chain actually consumes is a
different object, logically independent of it, and the ladder certifies it
flat: feeding the \emph{single constant}
$U_{\mathrm{ref}}=4.9008=\max_h1/g_{16}$ into the downstream map --- no
$h$-dependence anywhere in the substitution --- gives
$T_{\mathrm{marg}}=7.1\times10^{-2}$--$4.0\times10^{-1}$ with exponent
$h^{+0.391}$, non-decreasing against the one-sided bar and positive on all $9$
sub-surface windows, out of sample. The ceiling itself is
$1/g_{16}=1.7527$--$5.3286$ over the full $27$-window surface, $h^{+0.061}$
over a $9\times$ lever arm (split halves $h^{-0.010}$ / $h^{+0.103}$, spread
$3.040$), and every ladder $g_K$ is strictly increasing in $K$ on every window
(Schur 1917 nested complements), so $1/g_{16}$ is the tightest rung and the
certificate is monotone as well as flat.

\begin{keyeq}
\textbf{The $O(1)$ gate is not open as a quantity} --- it is discharged window
by window by a Cholesky identity. What a proof still needs is exactly one
thing: $\displaystyle\sup_m\,1/g_{16}(m)<\infty$ --- the $m$-freedom of a
certified flat list.
\end{keyeq}

\noindent A certified flat \emph{list} is not a certified flat
\emph{function}: nothing here upgrades the per-window certificate to a uniform
one, and the split-half test is a consistency check, not a proof of the sup.
But the residue now has the same grammatical form as every other open
uniformity item in the chain --- a per-window certificate plus a quantifier
over windows --- and it is no longer an existence question about trial
vectors, which is what R2$''$ was before T163.

\emph{Arm B --- the sector change is negative by a theorem, and the theorem
organises all three candidates.} A sector change, in the only sense the chain
admits, replaces the entry spectrum $\mu$ by another positive spectrum $\mu'$
and leaves the lag Gram alone. The structural fact, stated as the theorem it
is: $x_1=1$ fixes $a_1=1/\sqrt{\mu_1}$, i.e.\ only the \emph{scale} of $a$;
$Q$ and TV are both homogeneous of degree two in $a$; hence
$\mathrm{TV}(a)/Q(a)$ depends only on the direction of $a$ and \textbf{is the
same number in every sector --- the entry normalisation is a gauge}
(machine-checked to $0.0$--$8.8\times10^{-10}$ over $5670$
sector-by-trial-vector combinations --- $35$ sector spectra $\times$ $6$ taper
widths $\times$ $27$ windows --- against the declared cancellation horizon
$2.6\times10^{-8}$, the residual sitting $29\times$ below it). The crossing
criterion $Q/\mathrm{TV}>2\kappa=0.0776$ does not contain the normalisation
and cannot be moved by any sector change. Per candidate: (i) the \emph{full
space} (dropping the parity projection) is settled in closed form and is
strictly worse --- $\mu_0=0$ exactly (the constant vector), so the T3 step has
no finite floor at all, and even excluding it the lowest full-space eigenvalue
never exceeds $\mu^P_1$; (ii) a \emph{shifted or weighted sector} does flatten
the floor --- $\mathrm{TV}\ge1/(\mu^P_1+\kappa_s)$ is $h^{+0.000}$ at
$\kappa_s=4$, so T163's obstruction really is absent there --- but the
certified value scales by $\theta=\mu^P_1/(\mu^P_1+\kappa_s)$ and recovering a
bound on the original $1/s$ costs the transfer factor $1/\theta\sim
h^{+1.997}$, with
\[
\text{floor}\times\text{transfer}\;=\;\frac1{\mu^P_1}\ \sim\ h^{+1.997}
\quad\text{identically}
\]
at every shift on the declared grid (the two exponents sum to $+1.997$ to
$10^{-9}$) --- an exact product identity: \textbf{the $h^2$ is conserved, not
removed --- it lives in the ratio, never in the floor}; (iii) the \emph{Mellin/frequency
side} becomes, through the invariance, a well-posed normalisation-free
problem, treated next.

\emph{The unconstrained ascent, and the TV floor holds where T163 never
searched.} Summation by parts (Abel 1826, $w_M=0$) gives the identity
$Q=\sum_e(\Delta w)_e\,C_e$ with $C$ the partial sums of the lag coefficients
(checked to $4.7\times10^{-13}$--$4.8\times10^{-10}$ inside its declared
horizon), hence $Q/\mathrm{TV}\le\|C\|_\infty=30.27$--$930.60\sim h^{+1.185}$
--- the ceiling on the gauge-invariant demand ratio is a window-length
quantity that \emph{grows}, so nothing on the frequency side forbids the
crossing, and the natural coordinate is the alignment efficiency
$\eta:=(Q/\mathrm{TV})/\|C\|_\infty$. A declared first-order ascent on
$Q(v)/\mathrm{TV}(v)$ over the full window (all $142$--$1320$ coordinates,
$17$ restarts $\times$ $250$ steps, no truncation, no normalisation) reaches
$Q/\mathrm{TV}=2.38$--$74.57$ against the bar $2\kappa=0.0776$ ---
\textbf{$31$--$960\times$ over, on $9$ of $9$ windows}
($\delta_{\mathrm{bnd}}=-0.124\ldots-0.090$, $\eta=7.9$--$11.1\%$,
cancellation headroom $3.8\times10^{15}$) --- and then the price is put back:
normalising the ascent output to $x_1=1$ gives
$\mathrm{TV}\,\mu^P_1=8.30$--$11.72\ge1$ --- \textbf{T163's total-variation
floor holds on the unconstrained optimiser too}, a family T163 never searched
and the strongest available confirmation that (T1)--(T3) is an inequality
rather than a property of the swept families --- at a price
$P_{\mathrm{pr}}=1.39\times10^{4}$--$4.41\times10^{7}\sim h^{+3.299}$, above
the T163 crossing floor on every window and $3.5$--$7.6\times$ above
$P_{\mathrm{aff}}$: worse than T163's own crossing price $h^{+1.91}$.
Dropping the normalisation moved the difficulty from one coordinate to the
other without reducing it; the binding axis was never the demand and never the
sector --- it is the \emph{alignment} between $\Delta w$ and the partial sums
$C$, and that quantity is itself gauge-invariant.

\emph{R-B$'''$ narrowed, R-D settled in type, the stress.} R-B$'''$ turns out
to be a \emph{naming} problem --- two different quantities were being called
the same name: the T162 $a$-weighted quarter-bar object
$|\sum_{k\ne l}a_ka_lG^{\mathrm{arch}}_{kl}|/|Q^{\mathrm{arch}}|
=0.1001$--$0.1623$ carries the $h^{-0.172}$ (T163's exponent reproduced to
$0.0004$) and sits under the $0.25$ bar on all $27$ windows with $35\%$ of
margin, while the raw arch/atom cancellation is a different number
($h^{-2.04}$). The declared two-variable regression puts $-0.046$ of the
quarter-bar drift on $\log h$ against $-0.477$ on $\log\alpha$ ---
$10\times$ more on the \emph{zone scale} --- and on this recipe $\alpha$ and
$h$ are coupled by construction (the window comes from a prime gap), so a
regression on $h$ alone misattributes an $\alpha$-effect to $h$: the
$-0.172$ is \emph{not} established as an $h$-gate, and separating it needs a
surface on which $\alpha$ and $h$ vary independently --- a narrowing, not a
closure. R-D is untouched in value ($\rho=1.0036$--$1.0140>1$ flat, T161,
quoted) and settled in \emph{type}: under the shift the three kernel inputs
move in exactly compensating directions --- $s\to s/\theta$,
$\hat a\to\theta\hat a$, $L\to\theta L$ --- so $P_K$, the $r$-ceiling and
$F(P_K,r)$ are unchanged to $3.5\times10^{-16}$ on $54$ window-by-shift
combinations: every object the chain consumes downstream is a ratio of
equally-homogeneous forms, hence \emph{no fifth device can come from a sector
change}. The must-break controls break: the uniform surrogate drives the
total to $1.5\times10^{3}$--$4.9\times10^{7}$ of $|Q|$, the T145 no-go breaks
monotonically over $\nu=4\to2\to1\to0.5\to0.25$ with damage
$1.0\to9.1\to25.4\to129\to434$ (maxima; exact null control, damage $\ge26.1$
at the coarsest setting on every window), the gauge violation costs
$3.4\times10^{-2}$ of $\|w\|_1$; the classical controls are exact (Dirichlet
kernel $\le2.0\times10^{-14}$ on $64$ random triples, parity Laplacian exact,
orthonormality $3.6\times10^{-15}$), and the correlation form is verified on
\emph{random} $v$ ($3.8\times10^{-16}$) --- the ascent measures the same
object the chain does. The balance of T164:
$11$~theorem~$/\,1$~certified-uniform~$/\,4$~certified-per-window~$/\,
6$~measured, zero load-bearing fit rows (the only fitted numbers are
$h$-exponents and the one two-variable regression, labelled in place);
candidates T164-Q1\ldots Q9 all \textsc{pending}, no promotion here (bundled
with T165 into \vref{v556}, Section~\ref{sec:v556}).

\begin{keybox}[After T164: one quantifier, one alignment question]
\emph{(R-E-A)} \textbf{reduced to a quantifier}: the chain tolerates no
growing ceiling (power one), but the ceiling it consumes is $1/g_{16}$,
certified per window by a Cholesky identity and measured flat --- what remains
is $\sup_m1/g_{16}(m)<\infty$, the $m$-freedom of a certified flat list.
\emph{(R-E-B)} \textbf{closed, negatively, by a theorem}: the entry
normalisation is a gauge, the demand ratio and the whole T156 kernel are
sector-invariant, the full space is worse in closed form, and every
floor-flattening shift pays the identical exponent back as a transfer factor.
\emph{(R-F)} the genuinely new successor, gauge-invariant and prime-free: is
there a $v$ with $Q(v)/\mathrm{TV}(v)>2\kappa$ \emph{and} $Q(v)$ comparable
to $1/s$ --- equivalently, can the alignment efficiency $\eta$ stay above
$2\kappa/\|C\|_\infty$ at bounded price? \emph{(R-B$'''$)} narrowed: the
drift belongs to the quarter-bar object and mostly to the zone scale; a
surface with independent $\alpha$ and $h$ is needed. \emph{(R-D)} untouched
in value, settled in type: no fifth device from a sector change. T165
(\texttt{alignment\_eta\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{ALIGNMENT.ETA}) closed
exactly that alignment question by certificate --- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The alignment question: the successor closes by certificate, and
one quantifier remains (T165)}
T165 (\texttt{alignment\_eta\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{ALIGNMENT.ETA},
$30/30$, $15.1$\,s, the T163/T164 surface rebuilt and re-verified with the
window ladder up to $h=1445$, $27$ windows inside the condition horizon; the
dashboard $R=Q/\mathrm{TV}$, $\eta=R/\|C\|_\infty$, $P_{\mathrm{pr}}$,
$\mathrm{TV}/(t_1v)^2$ and the quarter statistic all checked gauge-invariant
under $v\to tv$; $\kappa=0.038821$ verified at every jump point; verdict
\textsc{eta-resists} in the strong form) answers R-F --- and the answer is a
structure statement, not a failed search. R-F asked for a trial vector with
alignment efficiency $\eta$ above $2\kappa/\|C\|_\infty$ at bounded price; no
such vector exists on anything measured, and the reason is an \emph{identity}
plus a \emph{theorem}.

\emph{The one equation the part is about.} Write the four gauge-invariant
factors side by side; dividing the price by the demand and the floor gives,
with no inequality anywhere,
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
P_{\mathrm{pr}}(v)\;=\;g_{16}\cdot R(v)\cdot
\frac{\mathrm{TV}/(t_1v)^2}{\mu^P_1},\qquad R=\frac{Q}{\mathrm{TV}}$
\quad(machine-checked to $3.3\times10^{-16}$).
\end{keyeq}
\noindent Four factors, each a named object of the chain: $g_{16}$ is the
R-E-A quantifier, $R$ is the demand, $\mathrm{TV}/(t_1v)^2\ge1$ is the T163
theorem, and $1/\mu^P_1=1/(4\sin^2(\pi/N))$ is the Kac--Murdock--Szeg\H{o}
1953 spectral scale --- exactly the $h^2$ the whole chain has been paying
since T152. Demand and price are \emph{one} equation, so the two clauses of
R-F cannot be chosen independently; with T163's floor, every crossing vector
pays $P_{\mathrm{pr}}\ge2\kappa g_{16}/\mu^P_1$ --- the old $h^2$. The
anatomy of the free optimum, measured: it is a \emph{low-harmonic} object
($93.7$--$96.8\%$ of its energy in the first $32$ parity modes against an
equidistribution baseline of $2.4$--$22.5\%$, lift $4.2$--$39.7$), essentially
orthogonal to the PNT main term (cosine $-0.070\ldots-0.031$), with heavy
edges on prime-power-occupied cells (lift $1.36$--$2.12$); the alignment is a
\emph{cancelling} sum over the whole window (participation $8$--$18\%$, mass
centroid $0.72$--$0.92$).

\emph{The exact price decomposition.} The identity turns the price exponent
into a sum of four exponents with no remainder, and the decomposition closes
to $0.0$:
\[
h^{+3.261}\;=\;\underbrace{+1.997}_{\text{KMS }h^2\text{ (since T152)}}
\;+\;\underbrace{+1.279}_{\text{demand overshoot}}
\;+\;\underbrace{+0.093}_{\text{floor}}
\;-\;\underbrace{0.108}_{g_{16}},
\]
i.e.\ $61\%$ of the exponent is the same $h^2$ the series has met since T152
(reproduced to $0.003$ of the exact $-2$), and the rest is the ascent
overpaying for demand the chain never asked for; the bar-tight counterfactual
price stays $h^{+1.982}$. The $\eta(\mathrm{Cap})$ profile is two-sided and
the ceiling is a theorem (identity $+$ floor): at the preregistered tolerance
$\mathrm{Cap}=10$ the certified ceiling is
$2.95\times10^{-7}$--$4.69\times10^{-4}$ against the requirement
$2\kappa/\|C\|_\infty=1.16\times10^{-4}$--$2.56\times10^{-3}$ --- \textbf{short
by $5.5$--$392\times$ on every window, $0/27$ capped-ladder points reach the
bar}.

\emph{The equivalence --- R-F was never independent.} Dividing T163's exchange
law by the identity above, the T163 normalisation drops out completely:
$P_{\mathrm{pr}}>2\kappa g_{16}(\mathrm{TV}/(t_1v)^2)/\mu^P_1\iff R>2\kappa$
--- the demand half of R2$''$ and the gauge-invariant crossing condition are
\emph{the same predicate} ($105/105$ probe vectors). R-F is therefore strictly
\emph{stronger} than the R2$''$ demand (it is demand \emph{and}
affordability), and the two clauses collide by the identity plus the floor
alone: \textbf{R-F is empty, and its $m$-uniform form \emph{is} R-E-A}. T2
localises the quantifier further: the $m$-free ingredients of the chain (the
head split, the atom budget $4(1+\kappa)\sqrt X$, the moment laws) bound
$B_{11}$ \emph{sharply} (factor $21$--$26$, flat $h^{+0.039}$) --- but it is
the wrong object: $1/g_1$ grows $h^{+3.110}$ while $1/g_{16}$ is flat
$h^{+0.061}$, and the exponents close exactly ($+3.110-3.049=+0.061$); the
entire certification lives in the $15$ ladder increments (half the gain by
rung $2$--$5$). The residue is still one quantifier, but smaller: \emph{bound
the cascade gain $g_{16}/g_1$ from below by $h^{3-\varepsilon}$}, one scalar
per window --- and provably not reachable from absolute-value budgets, because
it is a \emph{cancellation}.

\emph{The decoupled surface --- the quarter-bar confound settled, and one
constant honestly retired.} The frame-A recipe couples $\alpha$ and $h$ by
construction; T165 decouples them with $\nu$ as a knob (at fixed zone it
multiplies $h$ against $\alpha$, with the gap and the atom set fixed): $25$
admissible windows over $6$ zones, $\nu\in\{4,5,6,8,11,16\}$, collinearity of
$\log\alpha$ against $\log h$ falling $0.87\to0.68$. Finding: \textbf{the
quarter-bar drift is zone depth, not window length (factor $19$)} --- the same
answer as T2.2 from independent statistics, settling the R-B$'''$ confound
T164 named. Two honest costs, reported openly: $\sup1/g_{16}$ rises to
$5.7327$ off-recipe --- exceeding T164's $U_{\mathrm{ref}}=4.90$ by $17\%$,
so that constant was frame-A-specific and is \emph{retired} as a surface
constant (an errand: replace it wherever a chain station quotes it) --- and
the $h$-coefficient of $1/g_{16}$ is no longer negligible at free $\nu$.
End-to-end on the union of both surfaces ($52$ windows, $h=142$--$1320$):
every crossing vector has $P_{\mathrm{pr}}\ge54.6$--$5865>\Theta_{\mathrm{TOL}}=10$,
and in closed form for every $h>84.9$. Stress: the T145 coarsening staircase
is monotone ($1.0/2.8/12.1/27.5$, up to $102\times$); the uniform surrogate
breaks by $8.6\times10^{3}$--$6.9\times10^{4}$; the gauge perturbation breaks;
Dirichlet/KMS controls exact to $10^{-15}$. The balance of T165:
$11$~theorem~$/\,1$~certified-uniform~$/\,4$~certified-per-window~$/\,
6$~measured --- the theorems carry more than the measurements; six new
candidates, all \textsc{pending}. The theorem-shaped cores of T164+T165 ---
the gauge theorem, the $h^2$ conservation law, the power-one spend, the
$P_{\mathrm{pr}}$ identity with the predicate equivalence, and the
Schur-cascade direction with its exact exponent closure --- are promoted as
\vref{v556} \veri{v556\_gauge\_ppr\_identities.py} (Section~\ref{sec:v556}).

\begin{keybox}[After T165: exactly one genuine open object]
\emph{(The quantifier)} $\inf_m g_{16}(m)>0$ --- equivalently a lower bound
on the sixteen-step Schur-cascade gain, $g_{16}/g_1\ge c\,h^{3-\varepsilon}$
uniform in $m$: a quantifier over a certified flat list, one scalar per
window, a \emph{cancellation} and hence provably beyond absolute-value
budgets. Everything else that looked open at the end of T164 has changed type
rather than moved: \emph{(R-F)} closed negatively by the $P_{\mathrm{pr}}$
identity plus the T163 floor (the $\eta$ route is not a device, and its
uniform version is the same quantifier); \emph{(R-B$'''$)} settled as a
zone-depth effect on a genuinely decoupled surface, at the cost of retiring
the out-of-sample constant $U_{\mathrm{ref}}=4.90\to5.7327$. No missing term,
no missing device, no sector. T166 (\texttt{schur\_cascade\_probe.py},
contract \texttt{SCHUR.CASCADE}) dissected exactly that cascade lower bound
--- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The cascade dissected: the gain is a Gram-determinant
cancellation, and one inequality in three dresses remains (T166)}
T166 (\texttt{schur\_cascade\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{SCHUR.CASCADE},
$30/30$, $2.1$\,s, the two surfaces rebuilt as a \emph{union}: $27$ frame-A
windows ($h=142$--$1320$, the T163--T165 recipe and density) plus $36$
decoupled-$\nu$ windows ($6$ zones $\times\ \nu\in\{4,5,6,8,11,16\}$,
$h=96$--$1371$) $=63$ windows with a $14\times$ lever arm on which zone depth
and resolution are \emph{independent} knobs ($\log h$ against $\log\nu$
correlated at only $0.33$ --- an exponent read on the union is a statement
about $m$, not about the recipe); T165's three numbers reproduced on frame A
($1/g_1=B_{11}\sim h^{+3.110}$, $1/g_{16}=1.7527$--$5.3286\sim h^{+0.061}$,
gain $\sim h^{+3.049}$, exponents closing exactly), the union reading
$h^{+2.759}/h^{+0.193}/h^{+2.566}$; $\kappa=0.038821$ verified at every jump
point up to $n=4\times10^{5}$; verdict \textsc{cascade-resists}) attacks the
one open object of T165 head-on. The answer is a complete anatomy, an honest
exponent gap, and a sharper statement of what is missing than the line has
ever had.

\emph{Four identities before any number.} Written as the Cholesky ladder
$g_K=\sum_{j\le K}y_j^2$ the increments look like fifteen unrelated positive
numbers; four elementary identities --- all theorems, re-verified on all $63$
windows and five rungs each --- turn the ladder into one readable object:
\emph{(I1)} the prefix property ($(L_K^{-1}e_1)_j$ does not depend on $K$, so
\emph{one} Cholesky yields all sixteen rungs; $1.2\times10^{-15}$);
\emph{(I2)} the minor form $g_K=\det Q_K^{(1)}/\det Q_K$ (Schur 1917) --- the
increments are closed objects in the block entries; \emph{(I3)} the
regression form,
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\frac{g_K}{g_1}\;=\;\frac1{1-R_K^2},\qquad
R_K^2=\frac{b^{\mathsf T}B_{HH}^{-1}b}{B_{11}}\in[0,1)$
\quad(checked to $2.1\times10^{-9}$ on $63/63$),
\end{keyeq}
\noindent so the open object \emph{is} a near-collinearity statement:
$g_{16}/g_1\ge c\,h^{3-\varepsilon}$ says mode $1$ is explained by modes
$2\ldots16$ up to a residual fraction $1-R_{16}^2\le h^{-3+\varepsilon}$ ---
a far more specific request than ``a cancellation''; and \emph{(I4)} the
diagonal invariance,
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\frac{g_K}{g_1}=B_{11}\,(Q_K^{-1})_{11}\ \text{ is invariant under }\
B\to DBD$\quad for every positive diagonal $D$,
\end{keyeq}
\noindent so the gain does \emph{not} see the KMS $1/\sqrt{\mu^P_k}$
normalisation at all: the $h^3$ is a property of the arithmetic Gram block
$G=TAT^{\mathsf T}$ alone (Kac--Murdock--Szeg\H{o} 1953) --- which kills a
whole family of ``it is an artefact of the normalisation'' objections before
it is raised. \emph{The rung profile is extreme:} rung $2$ alone carries a
median $59.26\%$ of the whole gain (range $0.14$--$0.85$), rungs $2$--$5$ a
median $71.79\%$, $K_{\mathrm{half}}\in\{2..5\}$ on $63/63$ windows, and the
chain's flat object first appears at rung $K=6$ --- the $h^3$ is never spread
over the block. Rung $2$ in closed form: $y_2^2/y_1^2=r_{12}^2/(1-r_{12}^2)$
with $1-r_{12}^2=1.3\times10^{-7}$--$4.5\times10^{-4}\sim h^{-2.92}$ on frame
A ($h^{-2.25}$ on the union) --- \emph{one} rung multiplies $g$ by
$2207$--$7.8\times10^{6}$, and the price of certifying it is a number: an
absolute-value budget would have to resolve $B_{11}$ against
$B_{12}^2/B_{22}$ to that relative accuracy, where the $m$-free budgets are
sharp only to a flat factor $21$--$26$. The Krylov reading is exact: the T158
bridge reproduces the entry $s$ over $\mathrm{span}\{t_1,A^{-1}L_Pt_1\}$ to
$5.5\times10^{-10}$ (a theorem --- the maximiser lies in the span),
$g_{16}\le s$ on $63/63$, $g_{16}/s=0.69$--$0.95$ (median $0.88$), and the
bottom eigenvector of $A$ is confined to $0.9999$--$1.0000$ in the sixteen
low parity sines (T146/T157 reproduced): the cascade is the mode-truncated
Ritz approximation of the Green column.

\emph{The cancellation finding --- a third mechanism.} The block was set up
to distinguish two stories: an arch-against-atom cancellation in the lag sums
(the T159/T160 mechanism --- then no closed object sees it) or a
mode-against-mode effect in the archimedean kernel alone (then the mechanism
is explicit and $m$-free). \textbf{Neither holds}: no entry of the $2\times2$
bottom block cancels ($G_{11},G_{12},G_{22}$ each keep $60$--$99\%$ of their
larger half), and neither half alone is collinear (the archimedean block has
$1-r_{12}^2=0.98$ --- no degeneracy whatsoever --- the atom block
$0.04$--$0.50$) --- yet the \emph{sum} is degenerate to seven digits. The
polarisation split (a theorem, checked to $6.7\times10^{-14}$) locates it:
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\det(G_{\mathrm{ar}}+G_{\mathrm{at}})\;=\;\det G_{\mathrm{ar}}
+\det G_{\mathrm{at}}+\Pi,\qquad
\Pi=G^{\mathrm{ar}}_{11}G^{\mathrm{at}}_{22}
+G^{\mathrm{at}}_{11}G^{\mathrm{ar}}_{22}
-2G^{\mathrm{ar}}_{12}G^{\mathrm{at}}_{12}$,
\end{keyeq}
\noindent with pieces of size $2.6$--$630$ cancelling to a full determinant
of $1.0\times10^{-3}$--$1.7\times10^{-2}$ --- a ratio of
$2.6\times10^{-6}$--$5.1\times10^{-4}$ decaying as $h^{-1.45}$.
\textbf{The cancellation lives in the $2\times2$ Gram determinant}: the same
arch-against-atom mechanism as T159/T160, one level up, in a
\emph{quadratic} functional of the lag sums rather than in any lag sum. And
it is pinned to the arithmetic twice over: the $L_P$ no-go control breaks
\emph{completely} (for $A=L_P$ the normalised block is the identity to
$3.6\times10^{-15}$ and the cascade gain is exactly
$1.0000000000$ --- no cascade at all), and the anti-fitting scramble
(uniform random atom positions at the \emph{same} total mass) destroys the
near-degeneracy by a factor $4569$ --- the mechanism hangs on \emph{where}
the prime powers sit, not on the atom budget, the kernel or the
discretisation.

\emph{The best lower bound, and the one inequality left.} Every route is an
instance of one theorem ($1/g_K=\mu^{P\,-1}_1\min\{u^{\mathsf T}Gu:u_1=1\}$
--- a trial vector bounds $g_K$ from \emph{below}, the only useful
direction). The two-rung route with a closed $\beta$ has its admissible
window stated as a number --- relative accuracy
$3.57\times10^{-4}$--$2.13\times10^{-2}$ on $\beta^*$ --- and all three
declared closed candidates miss it (by $12.4$--$2540$; $0/63$ windows), the
best (from the atom block) certifying gain $h^{+1.319}$ against the
$h^{+2.566}$ the exact ladder delivers. Combining the minor form with the
diagonal invariance gives the sharpest restatement the line has ever had:
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\frac1{g_K}\;=\;\frac{\det G_{[1..K]}}{\mu^P_1\,\det G_{[2..K]}},\qquad
\mu^P_1=4\sin^2(\pi/N)$
\quad(checked to $3.9\times10^{-9}$ on $252$ evaluations),
\end{keyeq}
\noindent first flat at $K=6$ on the union --- so exactly \emph{one} uniform
inequality is missing: $\det G_{[1..6]}\le U\cdot\mu^P_1\det G_{[2..6]}$. The
errands close: $U_{\mathrm{ref}}$ is redone off-recipe over the union with a
declared safety factor --- $\sup1/g_{16}=6.4781$, attained at a \emph{deep}
zone at moderate $\nu$ (the union supremum is driven by zone depth, not
resolution), $U_{\mathrm{ref}}(\text{union})=1.15\times6.4781=7.45$,
superseding T164's $4.90$ and T165's $5.7327$ (\textsc{cert-window}, never
\textsc{cert-unif}); the multi-covariate fit separates the knobs (gain
$\sim h^{+2.92}\,\nu^{-1.53}$); and the full chain $g_1\le\text{best-of-routes}
\le g_{16}\le s$ is verified on $63/63$. A $K=64$ test shows the confinement
surrogate's shortfall is \emph{truncation} (the same $v_0$ projected on $64$
modes improves $h^{+1.963}\to h^{+2.574}$) --- good news about the mechanism,
not a certificate at either $K$.

\emph{Two honest contract corrections.} \emph{(K1)} Form F2 (gain
$\ge c\,h^{3-\varepsilon}$) is strictly \emph{weaker} than form F1
($\inf_m g_{16}>0$) on this surface, because $B_{11}$ grows $h^{+3.110}$ and
not $h^3$ --- F1 would need $\varepsilon\le-0.110$, so honouring F2 is not
the same as closing the quantifier; every verdict distinguishes the two.
\emph{(K2)} The confinement route was a \emph{sub-surface artefact}:
$h^{+2.714}$ on frame A restricted to $h\le780$ (an earlier pass's
eigen-horizon --- it would have returned \textsc{one-term-missing}) against
$h^{+1.963}$ on the full union, exposed by raising the eigen-horizon to the
cap instead of leaving it as a to-do; the $+0.751$ of optimism exceeds the
whole $\varepsilon$ budget --- a concrete reason to distrust any exponent
quoted on a sub-surface. The verdict criterion is an \emph{exponent gap} so
it cannot be argued about: \textsc{cascade-carries} needs a closed route
reaching the measured $B_{11}$ exponent $+3.110$;
\textsc{one-term-missing} needs the gap to be a flat factor (below $0.05$ in
the exponent); measured: best closed route $h^{+1.319}$, target $h^{+3.110},$
\textbf{gap $h^{+1.791}$ --- an exponent, not a constant: the one missing
inequality \emph{is} the cancellation}, the same intrinsic hardness as the
$h^2$ cancellation of T159/T160. The balance of T166: $+5$~theorem~$/\,
+3$~certified-per-window~$/\,+4$~measured, and deliberately \emph{no} new
certified-uniform row --- the honest statement: nothing here became uniform
in $m$; nine candidates P166.1\ldots P166.9, all \textsc{pending} (no
promotion; to be bundled with T167).

\begin{keybox}[After T166: one inequality, three dresses]
\emph{(The inequality)} an $m$-free upper bound on the Gram-minor ratio
$\det G_{[1..K]}/(\mu^P_1\det G_{[2..K]})$ at the first flat $K$ ---
equivalently a closed $\beta$ at $K=2$ to relative accuracy
$3.6\times10^{-4}$, equivalently a closed near-null vector of $A$ in the low
modes: the \emph{same} inequality in three dresses, and it is the whole
quantifier --- everything else in the reduction is now theorem.
\emph{(Bookkeeping)} every statement carrying $U_{\mathrm{ref}}$ names its
surface ($7.45$ on the union, off-recipe, \textsc{cert-window}). Off the
list: ``a better trial space'' (the contract object \emph{is} the optimum
over the sixteen modes), ``which rungs matter'' (rungs $2$--$5$, measured,
rung $2$ closed), ``arch-vs-atom or mode-vs-mode'' (arch against atom, in
the Gram determinant). T167 (\texttt{null\_vector\_probe.py}, contract
\texttt{NULL.VECTOR}) attacked exactly that most constructive dress ---
next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The closed vector is exact at $K=2$: three dresses are one
inequality (T167)}
T167 (\texttt{null\_vector\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{NULL.VECTOR},
$39/39$, $1.4$\,s, the $63$-window union of T166 rebuilt bit for bit ($27$
frame-A windows $h=142$--$1320$ plus $36$ decoupled-$\nu$ windows,
$h=96$--$1371$, lever arm $14\times$); T163--T166 reproduced as fits, never
as inputs (frame A $B_{11}\sim h^{+3.110}$, gain $\sim h^{+3.049}$; union
$h^{+2.759}/h^{+0.193}/h^{+2.566}$, closure $4.4\times10^{-16}$);
$\kappa=0.038821$ verified at every jump point up to $n=4\times10^{5}$;
verdict \textsc{vector-resists}) attacks the most constructive of the three
dresses --- the closed fast-null-vector --- and returns the strongest
reduction of the series.

\emph{The pivot identity, and the exact vector.} Twenty-two candidate
families are \emph{preregistered} before any number is seen (the
Neumann/Jacobi and Kato/Rayleigh--Schr\"odinger perturbation routes, the
Gram route, the moment route, and the KMS/arch/exact controls), and all of
them are evaluated through one instrument:
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
u=x^*_K+\delta,\quad\delta_1=0\ \Longrightarrow\
u^{\mathsf T}Q_Ku\;=\;\frac1{g_K}\;+\;\delta^{\mathsf T}Q_K\delta$
\quad(theorem; $10206$ evaluations, $3.2\times10^{-9}$),
\end{keyeq}
\noindent because $Q_Kx^*_K=e_1/g_K$ and $\delta_1=0$ kills the cross term
--- so the relative excess $\rho=g_K\,\delta^{\mathsf T}Q_K\delta\ge0$ of
every candidate is an \emph{exact number}, never an estimate, and by the
trial theorem ($u^{\mathsf T}Q_Ku\ge1/g_K$ for every $u_1=1$; $252$ random
trials, Schur 1917) every candidate is a certified \emph{lower} bound. The
central positive result:
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
u=\Bigl(1,\,-\tfrac{Q_{21}}{Q_{22}}\Bigr)\ \text{attains}\
\frac1{g_2}=Q_{11}\bigl(1-r_{12}^2\bigr),\qquad
B_{11}\,g_2=\frac1{1-r_{12}^2}$
\quad(exact on $63/63$; $8.7\times10^{-10}$),
\end{keyeq}
\noindent with $r_{12}^2=Q_{12}^2/(Q_{11}Q_{22})$: \textbf{at $K=2$ the
fast-null-vector needs no approximation at all --- the vector is free},
$\rho=0$ as a theorem, and the certified gain exponent is $h^{+2.921}$ on
frame A --- that is $h^{3-0.079}$, already inside the preregistered
$\varepsilon$ budget --- and $h^{+2.246}$ on the union, with rung $2$
carrying $96\%$ of the exponent: dress (c) collapses onto dress (b).

\emph{Why perturbation theory dies --- and it is not what one would
guess.} The Jacobi map genuinely diverges (spectral radius $1.0$--$12.7$
at $K=2/6/16$), so the Neumann route fails honestly; but the Kato
reduced-resolvent map has radius only $0.067$ --- \textbf{it converges,
fast, to the wrong object}: the Rayleigh--Schr\"odinger series builds the
\emph{eigenvector} attached to level $1$ (Kato 1949), and the constrained
minimum $1/g_K$ is not an eigenvector problem. The diagnostic that proves
it: the exact bottom eigenvector of $Q_6$ is itself a useless trial
($\rho=6.04$), because its overlap with mode $1$ is only $|v_1|=0.083$ and
the trial theorem divides by $v_1^2$; the underlying structure is the
relative spectral gap $5.4\times10^{-7}$ --- the RS denominators are
meaningless, the fast degeneracy makes the level assignment meaningless.
This closes off the perturbation route in \emph{every} order. The moment
route reaches $h^{+1.320}$, reproducing T166's $h^{+1.319}$ to three
digits (flagged, not interpreted).

\emph{The thresholds, and the monotonicity against the hypothesis.} Two
thresholds are separated and both envelopes verified on $189$ random
perturbations each: the vector accuracy
$\mathrm{eps}_{\mathrm{vec}}=\sqrt{\rho/(g_K\lambda_{\max})}/\|x^*\|$ and
the entry accuracy $\mathrm{eps}_{\mathrm{ent}}=\rho\,(1/g_K)/S_K$ --- its
\emph{square} (the square law is exactly why the vector dress looked
cheaper, and at $K=2$ genuinely is). \textbf{The threshold sharpens
monotonically in $K$ --- against the working hypothesis it is mildest at
$K=2$} (by $1.90$ in the median and $h^{+0.353}$ in trend:
$\mathrm{eps}_{\mathrm{ent}}\sim h^{-2.246}$ at $K=2$ against $h^{-2.600}$
at $K=6$), the \emph{only} $K$ at which the closed vector is exact --- the
line should be worked at $K=2$, and the first flat $K=6$ is the worst
place to stand: there no closed family hits (best separation $h^{+1.138}$,
best ratio already $264\times$ --- the achieved and required accuracy
curves \emph{diverge}). The anchor:
$\mathrm{eps}_{\mathrm{ent}}(2)\to(1-r_{12}^2)/4$ --- T166's independently
derived $3.57\times10^{-4}$ is literally the quarter of $1-r_{12}^2$, same
exponent.

\emph{End-to-end and stress.} The best closed candidate certifies gain
$2207.3$--$7.84\times10^{6}$ ($h^{+2.921}$ on frame A against the
preregistered $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{carry}}=0.50$ bar); gram2's $\rho$ at
$K=16$ stays in $[0.17,6.16]$ and $(1+\rho)$ carries $h^{+0.320}$ ---
\textbf{the deficit is the higher rungs, not the vector}. All four
must-breaks break, and the scramble breaks \emph{harder} than T166 saw:
\textbf{$8/8$ windows lose positivity of the $2\times2$ diagonal itself}
($Q_{11}=-1.35\times10^{5}\ldots-1.02\times10^{4}$) --- at $K=2$ the
collapse under scrambled prime-power positions is a change of \emph{type},
not a factor: $g_2$ does not even exist there. Headroom
$5.7\times10^{8}$--$2.0\times10^{12}$. The anti-fitting control
(power-fitted coefficients --- the most generous cheat) reaches only
$h^{-0.823}$, \emph{worse} than the honest candidate. The off-recipe sweep
($1.6\times$ denser, same cap) reads $1-r_{12}^2\sim h^{-2.740}$ against
$h^{-2.921}$ ($+0.181$): the exponent is a property of the arithmetic Gram
block, not of the zone recipe.

\emph{The unification --- the key result.} The entry threshold is an
identity at every $K$ of the ladder, to machine precision:
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\mathrm{eps}_{\mathrm{ent}}(K)\;=\;\rho_{\mathrm{carry}}\,
\frac{1/g_K}{S_K},\qquad
S_K=|x^*_K|^{\mathsf T}\,|Q_K|\,|x^*_K|$
\quad(machine precision at every $K$),
\end{keyeq}
\noindent and $(1/g_K)/S_K$ --- the certified value against the
absolute-value mass --- \emph{is} the one object of all three dresses:
T166's determinant ratio against its polarisation pieces (dress a), the
$1-r_{12}^2$ of dress (b) up to the closed factor $1+3r_{12}^2\to4$
(T166's independently derived quarter is this factor), and the entry
threshold of dress (c). \textbf{There is one inequality, not three.} The
verdict is \textsc{vector-resists}, with \textsc{one-term-missing}
deliberately \emph{not} rendered: exactly one term is missing and it has a
number, but that term \emph{is} dress (b) itself --- rendering it would
misread a reduction as progress on the inequality. The balance of T167:
$6$~theorem~$/\,0$~certified-uniform~$/\,2$~certified-per-window~$/\,
7$~measured --- certified-uniform zero \emph{by construction}: T167
supplies a map, not a step towards the bound. The theorem-shaped cores of
T166 and T167 --- the cascade identities, the diagonal invariance, the
exact $K=2$ identity, the pivot identity with the unification, and the
trial theorem with both must-breaks --- are promoted as \vref{v557}
\veri{v557\_cascade\_vector\_identities.py} (Section~\ref{sec:v557}).

\begin{keybox}[After T167: one scalar]
\emph{(R1, the only item)} an $m$-free upper bound on the single scalar
$1-r_{12}^2=1-Q_{12}^2/(Q_{11}Q_{22})\le C\,h^{-3+\varepsilon}$ --- three
closed lag sums (the T159 apparatus, no zeros, no $L$-evaluation, finite
$\Lambda$-sums only); required relative accuracy on $r_{12}^2$:
$1.25\times10^{-5}$ at the median union window, $3.19\times10^{-8}$ at the
worst; the measured exponent $h^{+2.921}$ ($\varepsilon=0.079$) sits
comfortably inside $\varepsilon_{\mathrm{carry}}=0.50$. Nothing else is
missing: the vector is exact and the gain is the inverse of this scalar.
\emph{(Closed off permanently)} perturbation theory of every order around
the KMS bottom mode (the Kato series converges to the wrong object);
position-blind $m$-free surrogates (the archimedean-only minimiser
certifies $h^{-0.017}$, i.e.\ nothing; the type-change scramble).
\emph{(Redirected)} work at $K=2$, not at the first flat $K=6$ (milder by
$1.90$ and $h^{+0.353}$). T168 (\texttt{lagrange\_minors\_probe.py},
contract \texttt{LAGRANGE.MINORS}) attacked exactly that scalar through the
Lagrange identity --- the determinant as a sum of squares --- next
subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The Lagrange identity: the sum of squares is real, and the
hardness is self-similar (T168)}
T168 (\texttt{lagrange\_minors\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{LAGRANGE.MINORS},
$39/39$, $2.3$\,s, the same $63$-window union as T163--T167, recipe
untouched, $h=96$--$1371$; T167's scalar reproduced bit-compatibly before it
is attacked ($1-r_{12}^2=1.28\times10^{-7}$--$4.53\times10^{-4}$,
$h^{-2.921}$ on frame A); $\kappa=0.038821$ verified at every jump point up
to $n=4\times10^{5}$; verdict \textsc{minors-resist}) attacks R1 through the
Lagrange identity --- the determinant as a sum of squares --- and returns a
fully mapped relocation.

\emph{The anatomy is exact.} $Q=X^{\mathsf T}AX$ with $X=[u,v]$ the two
lowest parity modes in the $A$-metric ($3.9\times10^{-15}$); the mode
vectors are closed trigonometry, $m$-free ($1.0\times10^{-14}$), and ---
the first anatomy fact --- \textbf{Euclidean-orthogonal}: the Euclidean
$r_{12}$ is $0$ to $6.2\times10^{-17}$, so the near-parallelism
$r_{12}^2=1-O(h^{-3})$ is created \emph{entirely} by the arithmetic metric
$A$ and not at all by the vectors. The Wronskian telescopes exactly,
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
W_r-W_{r-1}=(\mu_1-\mu_2)\,u_rv_r$\quad($1.7\times10^{-13}$;
$W_{h-1}=0$ to $2.7\times10^{-18}$),
\end{keyeq}
\noindent so the near-diagonal minors are one closed one-parameter family
--- a Dirichlet partial sum; the minor sup is closed and $m$-free
($\sim N/\pi^2$, attained to $0.770$); and Cauchy--Binet is verified as
algebra ($1.1\times10^{-15}$ on random indefinite $A$): the second compound
of $A$ is the exact kernel of the Lagrange form.

\emph{The finding.} \textbf{On every one of the $63$ windows the $h\times h$
arithmetic kernel $A$ is positive definite}
($\lambda_{\min}=5.0\times10^{-6}$--$8.5\times10^{-4}$, $8$--$12$ orders
above the solver floor), so the second compound is PSD and the Lagrange
identity is a genuine sum of squares with strictly positive weights ---
$\rho_{\mathrm{LAG}}=S_+/\det Q=1.000$ exactly, no sign cancellation. Hard
fence, stated with the finding: this is a statement about one finite matrix
per window, certified on \emph{this} surface ($h\le1371$); the Weil
criterion is not tested, not assumed and not reverse-inferred.

\emph{The key measurement --- it splits by basis.} In the closed basis the
minors are \emph{maximal}:
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\tfrac12\sum_{r,s}M_{rs}^2=\|u\|^2\|v\|^2-\langle u,v\rangle^2
=\frac1{\mu_1\mu_2}$\quad(exact, $6.9\times10^{-16}$; $\sim h^4$),
\end{keyeq}
\noindent --- the Wronskians carry zero arithmetic and the \emph{largest}
norm they could have: all smallness sits in the PSD kernel evaluated at one
closed vector. In the eigenbasis the sum is \emph{thin}: $90\%$ of the
weighted sum of squares from $4$--$101$ pairs ($\le8\times10^{-4}$ of the
$h^2$ eigen-pairs), the top pair always $(\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max})$
carrying $6.8$--$41.7\%$ alone, and the pairs are \emph{raw}
($\kappa_w=0.30$--$0.94$; a typical minor cancels only ${\sim}100{:}1$) ---
no internal cancellation, the thinness is the story.

\emph{The exponent ledger closes.} $1-r_{12}^2=\nu_1\nu_2/(\hat a_{11}\hat
a_{22})$ ($1.0\times10^{-9}$, Poincar\'e separation) with $\nu_1\sim
h^{+0.81}$, $\hat a_{11}\sim h^{+0.76}$, $\hat a_{22}\sim h^{+0.91}$ and
$\nu_2\sim h^{-1.38}$: \textbf{every factor but one at the right power}.
The best $m$-free-shaped bound $B_1=\lambda_1\lambda_2/(\hat a_{11}\hat
a_{22})$ reads $h^{-0.548}$ on the union / $h^{-0.880}$ on frame A against
the required $h^{-3}$ --- short by $h^{2.45}/h^{2.04}$; the literal
count-times-sup budget costs $h^{+2.049}$, twelve orders above target,
closed so it is never tried again. The open factor is identified exactly:
$\nu_2$, with minimiser $t^*=Q_{12}/Q_{11}$ (factor $1.0000$), needed to
relative accuracy $6.05\times10^{-3}$ median / $2.82\times10^{-4}$ worst,
sharpening $h^{-1.146}$ --- T167 measured the same requirement from the
other end, and \textbf{by T168-TH7 this factor \emph{is} the target
rewritten}: the Lagrange route does not lower the accuracy demand, it
relocates it (which is why \textsc{one-term-missing} is deliberately not
rendered --- it would misread a reduction as progress on the inequality).
No closed constant candidate works ($1/\sqrt2$ misses by up to $0.194$
relative; $t^*$ drifts $h^{+0.076}$), no single-mode trial (overshoot
$285$--$1.5\times10^{6}$), the ground state is only $0.982$-confined
($\delta$ does not decay), and the Tur\'an band is neither sign-definite
nor telescoping.

\emph{Chain and stress.} $1/g_2=Q_{11}(1-r_{12}^2)$ verified to
$1.2\times10^{-8}$ on $63/63$; certified end-to-end gain $\ge1.00$--$2.13$
(weak, valid, direction-verified). \textbf{The scramble breaks harder than
T167: $8/8$ windows lose $A\succ0$ \emph{and} the Gram property}
($n_{\mathrm{neg}}$ up to $73$) --- no window survives, and on those windows
the Lagrange identity is no longer a sum of squares at all; the $L_P$
control has $Q_{12}=0$ and $1-r_{12}^2=1$ exactly, the sum collapsing onto
its diagonal pair; the KMS/Dirichlet/correlation controls are exact.
\textbf{The conclusion: the hardness is self-similar under exact
reformulation} --- determinant $\to$ PSD compound at a closed vector $\to$
near-null Rayleigh value $\to$ one ratio of two closed lag sums, same
accuracy price --- and the seven no-gos say that no position-blind budget,
no $m$-free trial vector, no $h$-independent constant and no count-times-sup
budget can pay it. The balance of T168:
$8$~theorem~$/\,0$~certified-uniform~$/\,3$~certified-per-window~$/\,
11$~measured~$/\,7$~no-go.

\begin{keybox}[After T168: one ratio]
\emph{(The open factor)} $\nu_2$, equivalently the single ratio
$t^*=Q_{12}/Q_{11}$ of two closed lag sums, to relative accuracy
$6.05\times10^{-3}$ median / $2.82\times10^{-4}$ worst ($h^{-1.146}$) ---
by T168-TH7 the target itself in a new notation. \emph{(Closed off)} the
count-times-sup budget ($h^{+2.049}$), $h$-independent constants ($t^*$
drifts $h^{+0.076}$), single-mode trials, the ground-state route ($\delta$
does not decay), the Tur\'an band. T169 (\texttt{tstar\_ratio\_probe.py},
contract \texttt{TSTAR.RATIO}) attacked exactly that ratio as a
preregistered candidate table --- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The candidate table closes the loop: the self-similarity is
proved (T169)}
T169 (\texttt{tstar\_ratio\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{TSTAR.RATIO},
$41/41$, $3.0$\,s, the same $63$-window union, recipe untouched; T168
reproduced bit-compatibly ($t^*=0.5700$--$0.7898\sim h^{+0.076}$); the whole
$2\times2$ block verified as a lag sum ($4.7\times10^{-16}$) with an exact
arch/atom split ($5.6\times10^{-16}$); verdict \textsc{ratio-resists})
attacks T168's one open factor as a preregistered candidate table --- and
the table speaks with two voices.

\emph{The negative half.} Every genuinely closed candidate fails by $O(1)$:
