the archimedean ratio at $0.84$ relative median, the lag heads at ${\sim}1$,
the Toeplitz half at $1.0$; the best closed candidate is T168's constant
$1/\sqrt2$ at $0.15/0.24$ (hitting $1/63$ windows, with the wrong sign of
trend). The structural reason: the block is \textbf{atom-dominated}
($|{\rm atom/arch}|=3.5$--$43$ on the diagonal, $14$--$461$ off it) and
\textbf{$\hat a_{11}^{\mathrm{arch}}<0$ on $63/63$} --- the archimedean half
is not even PSD, so the budget interval is vacuous \emph{by sign}; the atom
shares are correlated ($0.994$) but not proportional
($s_{12}/s_{11}=4.1$--$10.7$), and $|s_{12}-s_{11}|$ grows $h^{+0.84}$
against a threshold sharpening $h^{-1.146}$ --- a divergence of
$h^{+1.99}$.

\emph{The key result --- the loop closes as an identity.} The only
candidate that meets both thresholds, $K7=\sqrt{\hat a_{22}/\hat a_{11}}$
($2.49\times10^{-5}$ median / $2.27\times10^{-4}$ worst, on $63/63$ windows
individually, right trend $h^{-1.379}$ against the target $h^{-1.380}$),
does so by a new theorem (T169-TH7):
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
R\Bigl(\sqrt{\tfrac{\hat a_{22}}{\hat a_{11}}}\Bigr)
=\frac{2\sqrt{\hat a_{11}\hat a_{22}}\;\det\hat A}
{(\hat a_{11}+\hat a_{22})\bigl(\sqrt{\hat a_{11}\hat a_{22}}+\hat a_{12}\bigr)}$
\quad($1.1\times10^{-9}$),
\end{keyeq}
\noindent --- it meets the threshold precisely because it puts $\det\hat A$
back into the numerator. \textbf{The $t^*$-language is provably exactly as
hard as T167's determinant --- no cheaper, no dearer: T167's scalar, T168's
factor and T169's candidate are the same object, and the self-similarity is
now proved, not observed.} In its usable form: $\nu_2\le2\det\hat A/(\hat
a_{11}+\hat a_{22})$, tight to a factor $2.000$.

\emph{The real gains.} \textbf{R3 is booked, the first certified-uniform
row in weeks}: $\nu_1\le\max(\hat a_{11},\hat a_{22})+|\hat a_{12}|$
(Gershgorin, unconditional, uniform in $h$, closed in the three entries),
holding on $63/63$ and losing only $1.10$--$1.19$ at the same exponent ---
the certified-uniform column moves off zero. R2 is refuted and honestly
downgraded from cheap to open: the absolute-value budget gives $\hat
a_{11}\ge-1.7\times10^{2}\ldots-13$ --- it cannot even certify positivity;
a lower bound at $h^{+0.76}$ needs the sign structure of the atom lag sum,
i.e.\ R1's difficulty again. R4: Cholesky on $63/63$ ---
certified-per-window, permanently; three uniform routes refuted (the
Gershgorin margin is negative on $63/63$; the $Z$-/$M$-matrix route cannot
start, $A$ has positive off-diagonals on $63/63$; the perturbation split is
off by $6.4\times10^{5}$). \textbf{The Weil fence, prominent:
uniform-in-$h$ positivity of $A_h$ is RH-equivalent-shaped and is never
routed, never claimed, never reverse-inferred --- instead the chain is
rebuilt R4-free (T169-TH9): it does not need $A$-positivity.} And by
T169-TH3 the $1/\sqrt{\mu}$ factors cancel exactly --- $\hat a_{ij}=
t_i^{\mathsf T}At_j$ are single-sine lag sums against the closed T159
Dirichlet weights, so the $\mathrm{cond}\sim10^{8}$ ladder leaves the file.

\emph{The R4-free chain, end to end.}
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
1-r_{12}^2\;\le\;\frac{\bigl[\max(\hat a_{11},\hat a_{22})+|\hat a_{12}|\bigr]\,
R(\hat t)}{\hat a_{11}\hat a_{22}}$
\quad(valid on $63/63$; loss $1.10$--$1.19$ with $\hat t=K7$),
\end{keyeq}
\noindent following the true scalar exponent for exponent: \textbf{frame-A
trend $h^{-2.948}$, i.e.\ $h^{-3+\varepsilon}$ with $\varepsilon=0.052$
inside the $0.5$ carry window} (union $h^{-2.262}$ against the true
$h^{-2.246}$); with the best \emph{closed} $\hat t=1/\sqrt2$ it flattens to
$h^{-0.990}$. Stress: the $L_P$ control is the sharpest line of the file
($\hat a_{12}=4\times10^{-17}$, $t^*=0$ exactly as T168 predicts, overshoot
exactly $4\cos^2(\pi/N)$ --- the $t^*$-recipe is a near-degeneracy artefact:
its tightness \emph{measures} $\det\hat A$, it does not bound it); scramble
$8/8$ (K7 accuracy $2.5\times10^{-5}\to4.6$); flat-weight null $8/8$ (both
halves of the arithmetic input are necessary); the parity-pair control is
only $6.7\times$ --- honestly reported as partial (the near-degeneracy is a
low-spectrum property, not specific to $(t_1,t_2)$). The balance of T169:
\textbf{$10$~theorem~$/\,2$~certified-uniform~$/\,1$~certified-per-window~$/\,
4$~no-go}.

\begin{keybox}[After T169: one bilinear von Mangoldt sum]
\emph{(R1, in standard shape for the first time)} an $m$-free upper bound on
$\det\hat A$ at $h^{-3+\varepsilon}$, now a \textbf{bilinear von Mangoldt
sum against closed Dirichlet weights} (equivalently the diagonal ratio
$\hat a_{22}/\hat a_{11}$ to $1.2\times10^{-2}$ median /
$5.6\times10^{-4}$ worst). \emph{(Housekeeping)} R2 $=$ R1 (it needs the
same sign structure); R3 closed (off the list); R4 not needed (the chain is
R4-free). The strategic point: T161's beyond-RH triage applied to
\emph{linear} sums --- for \emph{bilinear} forms the large sieve gives
unconditional square-root cancellation, so for the first time the one open
object stands where an unconditional classical tool is in principle
competent. T170 (\texttt{bilinear\_sieve\_probe.py}, contract
\texttt{BILINEAR.SIEVE}) ran the unconditional sieve toolbox
(Montgomery--Vaughan, the Vaughan decomposition) on the bilinear form ---
next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The sieve box prices every tool: the classification completes as
a theorem (T170)}
T170 (\texttt{bilinear\_sieve\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{BILINEAR.SIEVE},
$40/40$, $1.8$\,s, $70$ frame-A windows $h=142$--$1445$ on the T163--T169
union recipe, never re-tuned, $67$ of them arithmetically complete
($h=142$--$1433$; exponents quoted on both sets); $\kappa=0.038821$ verified
at every jump point up to $n=4\times10^{5}$; the large sieve is
\emph{unconditional} --- nothing assumes RH and nothing concludes it;
verdict \textsc{sieve-resists}) cashes in T169's standard shape: the
bilinear form is written down exactly, and the toolbox is priced on it.

\emph{The explicit form, all theorems.} $\hat A=B-\sum_{n\le X}
(\Lambda(n)/\sqrt n)\,X_n$ with $X_n$ the two-point spline read of the T159
closed lag weights (T170-TH1, $3.5\times10^{-15}$ against the direct
$t_i^{\mathsf T}A_ht_j$), and the determinant splits exactly
(T170-TH2/TH3):
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\det\hat A=\det B-D(B,S)+\det S,\qquad
\det S=\!\!\sum_{n,m\le X}\!\frac{\Lambda(n)\Lambda(m)}{\sqrt{nm}}\,K(n,m),
\quad K=\tfrac12 D(X_n,X_m)$
\end{keyeq}
\noindent with $D(P,Q)=P_{11}Q_{22}+P_{22}Q_{11}-2P_{12}Q_{12}$ the
polarisation of $\det$ (Cauchy--Binet 1812/1815; Lagrange 1773; verified
$1.3\times10^{-10}$ and $1.5\times10^{-14}$). $X_n$ is rank one to median
defect $1.3\times10^{-4}$, so $K=\tfrac12\varepsilon_n\varepsilon_m
(x_n\wedge x_m)^2$ --- a \emph{wedge square} with mixed signs whose diagonal
cancels. On the reference window ($h=540$, $X=2.465\times10^{4}$) the three
pieces read $\det B=6.18$, $-D(B,S)=-198.8$, $\det S=192.6$ and sum to
$4.22\times10^{-3}$ against an absolute target of $1.10\times10^{-5}$:
\textbf{a five-order cancellation between three ${\sim}200$-sized pieces} ---
any tool that bounds $\det S$ alone, however sharply, cannot see it.

\emph{The route table, every $\delta$ certified} (target $\delta\ge3.0$ on
$1-r_{12}^2\le C\,h^{-\delta}$, $67$ complete windows):
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}l r l@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{route} & $\boldsymbol{\delta}$ & \textbf{status}\\
\midrule
truth: $1-r_{12}^2$ itself & $+2.747$ & measured\\
Cauchy--Schwarz on $\hat A$ & $-0.000$ & theorem\\
large sieve / duality on $\det S$ & $+0.669$ & theorem\\
Montgomery--Vaughan 1973, three linear sums & $-0.384$ & theorem\\
exact split $|\det B|+|D(B,S)|+|\det S|$ & $+0.996$ & theorem (best)\\
Vaughan 1977, Type I $+$ Type II & $+0.669$ & theorem\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\noindent \textbf{The key question answered --- the form collapses back, by
two theorems.} (TH4, \emph{the rank-3 theorem}): $D$ is the polarisation of
$\det$ on $2\times2$ symmetric matrices, matrix
$\bigl[\begin{smallmatrix}0&1&0\\1&0&0\\0&0&-2\end{smallmatrix}\bigr]$, rank
$3$, signature $(1,2)$ --- hence $\operatorname{rank}K\le3$ for \emph{every}
window, every $h$, every $X$ (verified $\sigma_4/\sigma_1=2.0\times10^{-15}$;
effective rank $1.38$--$2.71$ against $N\sim10^3$ atoms): the bilinear form
\emph{is} the rank-3 polynomial $S_{11}S_{22}-S_{12}^2$ in \emph{three}
linear von Mangoldt sums --- there is no bilinear content beyond three
linear functionals, and every bilinear tool degenerates exactly to
Cauchy--Schwarz on the object T161 already triaged. (TH5, \emph{the Type II
collapse}): the closed weights see $n$ only through $\log n$; under $n=md$
that is $\log m+\log d$, and a bounded-frequency function of a sum is a
finite-rank kernel --- Vaughan Type II blocks have effective rank $O(1)$ for
every $U,V$ ($2$ singular values carry $99.9\%$ against $153$ generic;
$U=12$--$70$ scanned; the identity verified coefficient by coefficient,
residual $0.0$). The antisymmetry route: the $\ell^1$ kernel mass exceeds
the signed value $41\times$ --- a triangle-inequality route loses before it
starts. \emph{The honest T161 comparison}: \textbf{gained} --- $32$
frequencies reduce to \emph{three} linear functionals, by theorem;
\textbf{not gained} --- the precision, which binds: $5.3\times10^{-5}$
relative per sum at $h=285$, sharpening $h^{-3}$, against the RH yardstick
$h^{-0.5}$ --- $1.1\times10^{3}$ too coarse.

\emph{The chain and the stress.} The chain becomes R4-free \emph{for free}
(T170-TH6): $1-r_{12}^2=\det\hat A/(\hat a_{11}\hat a_{22})$ is an identity
--- no $A$-positivity, no Rayleigh detour, the Weil fence never approached;
sharper than T169-TH9 ($-2.747$ vs $-2.771$) and using strictly less. End to
end the best unconditional bound carries $h^{-0.996}$ against the required
$\le h^{-2.50}$ --- \textbf{missing by $1.50$ in the exponent, and the
shortfall is a theorem (TH4+TH5), not a measurement}. The scramble is the
sharpest line: with scrambled positions the rank-3 collapse \emph{and} the
unconditional bounds are numerically almost unchanged, yet the truth moves
by $2.76$ in the exponent --- \textbf{the arithmetic content sits entirely in
the joint values of $(S_{11},S_{22},S_{12})$ against the arch block $B$},
not in the rank, the kernel, or the Type I/II split: a sieve bounds each
coordinate, the phenomenon is the near-degeneracy of the triple. Flat-weight
breaks ($h^{-0.116}$); $L_P$ is exact ($\hat a_{12}=8.7\times10^{-18}$, no
decay); the $\nu$-decoupling is reported unsmoothed (frames $\nu=5/8/11$
fall at $-1.70/-1.27/-1.74$ --- T169's $h^{-2.95}$ is a frame-A statement,
but the \emph{shortfall} is frame-independent: $+0.53/+0.34/+0.61$ certified
on those same frames). All five tools were preregistered by the contract.
The balance of T170: $6$~theorem~$/\,1$~certified-uniform~$/\,5$~no-go.
\textbf{R1, finally classified}: $\det\hat A/(|\mathrm{row}_1||\mathrm{row}_2|)$
is the \emph{sine of the angle} between the two rows of $\hat A$, falling
$h^{-2.711}$ --- R1 asks for an unconditional certificate that two explicit
finite $\Lambda$-sum vectors become collinear at rate $h^{-3}$: a
\emph{near-degeneracy}, not a size --- which is exactly why no
size-bounding tool, bilinear or linear, reaches it. The theorem-shaped cores
of T168, T169 and T170 --- the Lagrange/Wronskian anatomy, the exponent
account with the Gershgorin certificate, the TH7 det-collapse, the exact
bilinear form, the two rank theorems, and the R4-free chain with its
discriminators --- are promoted as \vref{v558}
\veri{v558\_bilinear\_rank\_identities.py} (Section~\ref{sec:v558}).

\begin{keybox}[After T170: the classification is final for the classical box]
\emph{(R1, classified)} an unconditional certificate of
\textbf{near-collinearity}: the two rows of $\hat A$ --- two explicit finite
$\Lambda$-sum vectors --- become collinear at rate $h^{-3+\varepsilon}$;
equally, a joint near-degeneracy of the triple $(S_{11},S_{22},S_{12})$
against the archimedean block, at relative precision sharpening $h^{-3}$,
$1.1\times10^{3}$ finer than the RH yardstick: \emph{beyond-RH joint
precision on three linear $\Lambda$-sums}, and not a size question at all.
\emph{(Housekeeping)} R2/R3 booked in T169; R4 entirely off the path
(T170-TH6); nothing else is open. T171 (\texttt{final\_map\_probe.py},
contract \texttt{FINAL.MAP}) then assembled the capstone: the whole
sixteen-link reduction chain end to end in one file --- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{Beyond frame A: the map is portable, the numbers are not
(T172)}\label{sec:t172}
T172 (\texttt{frame\_beyond\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{FRAME.BEYOND},
$44/44$, $1.3$\,s, $54$ windows on \emph{four} surfaces plus $3$
truncated-comb stress windows, $h=128$--$1444$; $26152$ prime-power
atoms to $n=3\times10^{5}$, $\kappa=0.038821$ verified at every jump
point --- the one unconditional input; verdict
\textsc{partially-portable}) answers the capstone's inherited question
--- how far does the certified map carry beyond frame A? --- with a
recipe inventory and a transfer table.

\emph{The recipe inventory --- four degrees of freedom, and only four.}
(1) The \emph{frame rule} anchor~$\to$~grid step $D$: frame A uses
$D=g_k/(2\nu)$ from the \emph{local} log-gap of the anchor sequence;
frame B (new here) uses $D=\alpha/h$ for a declared $h$ ---
gap-\emph{blind}, so the $(\alpha,h)$ pairing is no longer dictated by
arithmetic. (2) The subdivision $\nu$: T171 used $\{4,6\}$; the extremes
$\{3,8\}$ are new. (3) The \emph{zone family} of the anchor sequence:
prime powers, general non-prime-power integers, or a congruence class
$p\equiv1$ vs $3\bmod4$. (4) The \emph{atom set} --- which is
\textbf{not} a degree of freedom: $\Lambda$ lives on prime powers, so
``beyond frame A'' means a different \emph{anchor} arithmetic, never a
different $\Lambda$. The surfaces: S0 the frame-A reference ($12$
windows), S1 frame B plus the $\nu$-extremes ($18$), S2 non-prime-power
anchors ($12$), S3 the two congruence classes ($12$); $hD=\alpha$ to
$10^{-10}$ and $U_{\mathrm{ref}}=2\alpha=\log X$ exact on every
surface; all $54$ complete-comb windows positive definite
($\lambda_{\min}(B_{LL})=0.092$--$0.293$).

\emph{The identity transfer --- sixteen links, four surfaces.}
\textbf{Thirteen of the sixteen links transfer unchanged and none
breaks}: the whole identity tower (links 1, 3, 7--15, re-derived on
every window of every surface to the declared identity bars ---
Schur/KMS $3.2\times10^{-13}$, $\Psi$-collapse $3.9\times10^{-14}$, the
sampling identity $1.6\times10^{-14}$ (the most zone-sensitive link:
the anchor arithmetic decides \emph{where} the atom combs sit on the
grid, and the identity is untouched), the det collapse stated
absolutely at $5.2\times10^{-15}$, rank-3 with the polarisation at a
$3.2\times10^{5}{:}1$ cancellation) plus both direction lemmas (the
Sobolev ceiling $0.4826$ \emph{identical} on all four surfaces --- it
sees only $h$; interlacing on $54/54$). The three that shift are
exactly the three that carry a \emph{number} rather than an equation:
the two window certificates (link 5: $t$ median $0.128$--$0.204$ per
surface --- the one link that dies where the low block is indefinite;
link 6: $r_K$ median $0.25$--$0.52$) and the rate of link 16.
\emph{The indefinite mechanism, isolated}: $3/3$ truncated-comb stress
windows have $\lambda_{\min}(B_{LL})=-3.7\times10^{5}$\,--\,$-6.2
\times10^{6}$ against $0/54$ on the complete-comb surfaces ---
indefiniteness is located at the \textbf{declared sieve horizon} (the
comb is cut at the sieve cap while the grid runs to $X=e^{2\alpha}$),
\emph{not} at a frame or a zone family, retiring T171's open worry
about its one indefinite window; and the identity links keep holding
there ($\sim10^{-15}$), because none of them uses positivity.
\emph{The constants map}: of $11$ carried constants, $8$ stay inside
frame A's own scatter band once the $h$-trend is removed ($t$, $C_S$,
$1/g_{16}$, $c_0^{\mathrm{ap}}$, $\mu^P_1$, $\lambda_{\min}(B_{LL})$,
$\mathrm{cond}$, $r_K$); $3$ wander, all on the congruence surface S3
($K^F$ $\times2.3$, $U_{\mathrm{ref}}$ $\times1.2$, $s$ $\times1.5$).
The honest consequence: \textbf{a certificate on a new surface is a new
certificate} --- $t$, $r_K$, $L$, $1/g_{16}$ must be recomputed there
and the T163--T171 numbers may not be quoted for it; what transfers is
the \emph{procedure} and the \emph{directions} (floor below, ceiling
above, price $\ge1$, defect $\ge0$ --- all held on $54/54$).

\emph{R1 beyond frame A, and the placement finding (the key result).}
The near-degeneracy \emph{persists on every surface}: the row angle is
below $10^{-2}$ on all $54$ windows, decays on all $9$ legs
($1-r_{12}^2=1.4\times10^{-7}$--$6.2\times10^{-4}$), and nowhere
settles at $O(1)$ --- the \emph{classification} is the portable part,
R1 is not a frame-A artefact. The \emph{rate} is frame-bound, confirmed
and extended (pooled per frame datum: $\nu=3$: $h^{-2.19}$, $\nu=4$:
$h^{-2.46}$, $\nu=6$: $h^{-2.55}$, $\nu=8$: $h^{-1.83}$, gap-blind B:
$h^{-2.76}$), with the zone arithmetic a secondary lever (spread $0.40$
at fixed frame datum against $1.03$ at fixed zone family --- the frame
datum dominates by $2.6\times$); the $h^{-3}$ demand is met on none of
the $9$ legs ($C=(1-r_{12}^2)h^{3}$ grows at $h^{0.22}$--$h^{0.76}$ per
surface). And the sharpest new result: \textbf{scrambling the atom
positions at a fixed $\Lambda$-value multiset raises the angle by a
median $6.6\times10^{4}$ and removes the decay entirely}
($h^{+0.11}$ against $h^{-1.93}$ on the same windows) --- the collapse
is a property of the \emph{actual prime-power placement}, not of the
value multiset: it survives changing the anchor family and does not
survive destroying the comb.

T173 (\texttt{frame\_rate\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{FRAME.RATE},

$\nu\in\{3,4,5,6,8,10,12,16\}$, the gap-blind frame B, and the new
smoothed frame C ($D=\bar g_k/(2\nu)$ with $\bar g$ the mean of eleven
local gaps) at $\nu=4,6$ --- $h=128$--$1447$; $93192$ prime-power atoms
to $n=1.2\times10^{6}$, $\kappa=0.038821$ verified at every jump point;
$0/284$ windows indefinite; verdict \textsc{deficit-varies}) puts the
demand side itself on the measurement table.

\emph{The demand side, exact where it can be.} $\mu^P_1=4\sin^2(\pi/(2h
+1))$ is a closed form (KMS 1953), identical on every frame; the floor
$t$ is where the frame enters. Which exponent the chain demands is not
left to taste: writing $s=d\log\alpha/d\log h$, the identity
$hD=\alpha$ per window gives
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
q\;=\;-\frac{d\log D}{d\log h}\;=\;1-s\quad\text{exactly (to }1.9\times
10^{-15}\text{)},\qquad q=0.667\text{--}0.777<1\ \text{on all eleven
frame data}$
\end{keyeq}
\noindent so a $\Theta(D^{3})$ law reads in $h$ as $h^{-3q}$, and
\textbf{T171's $h^{-3}$ is the $q=1$ idealisation --- attained by no
frame in the family} ($\alpha=\log n_{\mathrm{zone}}$ grows with $h$
along every frame). \emph{The calibration}: of six preregistered gap
functionals the \emph{relative} I5 gap $t/\lambda_{\max}(B_{LL})$
reproduces the chain's $3$ on frame A (median $E_h=3.033$, legs
$2.831$--$3.153$) \emph{and} is the only dimensionless candidate ---
matching the dimensionless delivered object $1-r_{12}^2$: the
dimensional argument and the numerical calibration pick the same
functional independently. $(D/\alpha)^{3}$ is named a tautology
(exactly $h^{-3}$, zero information --- T172's convention, kept as
reference). The demand table: $\mathrm{REQ}=2.831$--$3.438$ over the
family (spread $0.607$) --- the demand itself moves with the frame, and
the spread is the size of the correction T172 was missing.

\emph{The deficit map --- one slope per frame datum.} The deficit is
read off the per-window ratio $R=\mathrm{GAP}/(1-r_{12}^2)$ as
\emph{one} slope with one error bar, never as a difference of two fits.
The split-stability test first (the strongest evidence in the file):
refit on the low/high half of each leg's lever --- $\mathrm{REQ}$
drifts by a median $0.501$, $\mathrm{DEL}$ by $0.453$ (\emph{neither}
side is a clean power law: a single-sided exponent on this chain is
reproducible only to about half an exponent, a declared limitation
T171, T172 and this file share), while the deficit drifts by only
$0.214$.

\noindent Pooled: \textbf{deficit $=+0.155\pm0.102$} (error inflated
$\times1.54$ for over-scatter; unscaled $\pm0.066$, i.e.\ $4.7\sigma$;
inflated, still $3.0\sigma$ above zero). The cancellation is strong but
not exact, both halves measured: against a constant, $\mathrm{REQ}$
gives $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}=4.87$, $\mathrm{DEL}$ $4.17$, their
difference $2.38$ --- $1.8\times$ flatter than either side, but $2.4
\sigma$ from constant: constancy is rejected. Two exact internal
supports: the $\mu^P_1$-weighted convention shifts the deficit by
exactly $2$ (measured $1.9974$, $\chi^2$ identical --- an exact-factor
convention cannot change flatness: \emph{the flatness, not the value,
is the result}); and the fixed-$h^{-3}$ convention has
$\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}$ equal to the delivery side's to $8\times10^{-15}$
--- a frame-independent demand subtracts a constant and cancels
nothing. The driver scan: the residual tracks $\log\nu$ ($r=+0.76$,
$2.8\sigma$; confounded with the window's arithmetic content under the
$h$-cap, declared) and \emph{not} the frame's own regulator $q$
($0.2\sigma$); holding $\nu$ fixed and moving only the $D$-rule (local
/ blind / smoothed) the deficit does not move ($\nu=4$:
$\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}=0.64$; $\nu=6$: $0.16$) --- \textbf{the deficit is
invariant under the anchor-to-grid rule}, the cleanest statement the
surface supports and a theorem candidate for that half only.
\emph{The honest correction to T172}: in the fixed-$h^{-3}$ convention
this wider surface gives $+0.015\pm0.084$ --- consistent with
\emph{zero}, and the worst-conditioned of the six conventions --- so
T172's $C$-growth of $h^{0.22}$--$h^{0.87}$ was neither sign- nor
split-stable ($3/5$ shared frame data outside $2$\,s.e.); T172's
\textsc{partially-portable} verdict is untouched, the size and sign of
that one number are not. The $h$-versus-$D$ question is \emph{not}
resolved and declared ($\chi^2$ $2.38$ vs $2.36$; the fixed-$\alpha$
discriminator legs --- $q=1$ exactly, T171's R-B$'''$ surface, run as
diagnostic only, outside the chain --- give $+0.510/+0.299$ at
$\pm0.336$ and do not settle it).

\emph{R1, stated frame-free (the key result).} On every frame datum of
the family, the delivered near-degeneracy $1-r_{12}^2$ of the two
explicit finite $\Lambda$-sum rows closes \emph{slower} than the
relative I5 gap it has to price, by $h^{+0.155\pm0.102}$ --- one number
across the three anchor-to-grid rules at fixed $\nu$, with a residual
drift in $\nu$; R1 is the statement that this deficit is zero, and no
choice of $D$-rule moves it. \textbf{No frame closes it}: $0/11$ legs
have a $2$\,s.e.\ upper edge $\le0$ (best: B at $-0.011\pm0.181$, upper
edge $+0.170$); honestly the other way, $8/11$ legs are individually
consistent with zero (a single leg resolves only $\pm0.23$), which is
exactly why the number is pooled \emph{with} the over-scatter penalty.
Frame shopping in T172's sense is over, by numbers: the
fastest-delivering frame (B, $3.449$) demands the most ($3.438$), in
step. Stress: the scramble control removes the decay on all $4$
declared legs ($\mathrm{DEL}\to-0.09$\,--\,$-0.13$ --- the deficit is
not a normalisation artefact); the lag-sum identity is exact ($\le1.9
\times10^{-16}$); $0/284$ windows touch the sieve horizon; anti-fitting
three ways (family preregistered; jackknife $\le0.026$; shuffle null
$-0.003\pm0.279$ with the measurement $3.7$ null-sigmas away).

\begin{keybox}[After T173: the deficit is the number]
\emph{(The cancellation identity --- the one thing that would close
this half)} show algebraically that the frame factors cancel between
the relative I5 gap and the $2\times2$ near-degeneracy, in the style of
T164's gauge machinery: that would turn the $D$-rule invariance into a
theorem and make the deficit \emph{the} number of the phase. T174
(\texttt{cancellation\_identity\_probe.py}, contract
\texttt{CANCEL.IDENTITY}) then asked exactly that --- next subsection.
\emph{(Rest)} the $h$-versus-$D$
split (needs a frame whose $\alpha$ does not track $\log h$ while the
comb still moves --- hard under the cap; T171's R-B$'''$ surface); and
the remaining rate: close $+0.155$ in the exponent unconditionally, for
two explicit finite $\Lambda$ sums --- unchanged as the one open
object, now stated frame-free. \emph{(Candidates P5--P8, pending)} the
frame-bound demand ($q=1-s$), the $D$-rule invariance, the T172
correction, the calibration --- bundled with T174's cores into
\vref{v560}.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The cancellation identity: the gauge route exhausted, the
deficit measured frame-free (T174)}\label{sec:t174}
T174 (\texttt{cancellation\_identity\_probe.py}, contract
\texttt{CANCEL.IDENTITY}, $37/37$, $6.5$\,s, $84$ rectangle $+$ $1020$
power-check $+$ $147$ anchor-ladder $+$ $178$ leg windows; $93192$
prime-power atoms to $n=1.2\times10^{6}$, $\kappa=0.038821$ verified at
every jump point; the preregistered $12\times7$ $(\alpha,h)$ rectangle
--- $12$ prime-power anchors $n=41\ldots1087$ crossed with the declared
geometric ladder $h=160\ldots1280$, fixed \emph{before} any window was
built, comb complete on every cell, $84/84$ positive definite; verdict
\textsc{partial-cancel}) turns ``do the frame factors cancel'' into
checkable algebra and then measures what does not cancel.

\emph{The decomposition --- which factors is each functional blind to.}
Both sides of the T173 deficit are scale-free functionals of \emph{one}
raw Gram matrix $\hat a_{ij}=t_i^{\mathsf T}A_ht_j$: the demand is the
relative gap of its $16\times16$ $\mu$-congruence, the delivery is the
$2\times2$ corner of the very same matrix. Blindness on both sides is a
cancellation in $R=\mathrm{GAP}/(1-r_{12}^2)$ --- and blindness is an
algebraic property, checkable to machine precision, not a fit. The
cancellation ledger:
\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}l l l@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{factor} & \textbf{status} & \textbf{size of the residue}\\
\midrule
amplitude of $c$ ($\kappa$) & \textsc{theorem} & $\le0.028$ of the round-off bar\\
scalar of the KMS ladder ($\mu^P_1$) & \textsc{theorem} & $\le0.009$ --- the whole $h^{-2}$ channel\\
full positive diagonal group & \textsc{theorem} & delivery only, exact\\
shape of the KMS ladder ($\hat S$ vs $k^2$) & \textsc{certified} & $\le0.0075$ in the deficit\\
arch/comb mixture in $\hat A$ & \emph{does not cancel} & additive; no factorisation\\
the frame rule itself & \textsc{theorem} & nothing to cancel: $R=R(\alpha,M)$\\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}
\noindent The load-bearing entry is the second: writing the KMS ladder
as $S=\mu^P_1\hat S$ with $\hat S_k=\mu^P_k/\mu^P_1$, the scalar
$\mu^P_1=4\sin^2(\pi/(2h+1))$ --- the one factor of the demand that is
a pure function of the grid --- cancels \emph{exactly} on both sides:
on the delivery because a correlation is invariant under the full
positive diagonal group, on the demand because a relative gap kills any
scalar congruence. \textbf{The entire $h^{-2}$ channel is exactly
absent from the deficit.} What survives is the \emph{shape} $\hat S$,
which the delivery is exactly blind to but the demand is not --- and
that one channel is bounded \emph{unconditionally}:
$|\log\mathrm{GAP}(k^2)-\log\mathrm{GAP}(\mathrm{KMS})|\le
2\log((1+\varepsilon)/(1-\varepsilon))$ with
$\varepsilon=(K\pi/(2h+1))^2/6$, worth at most $0.0075$ in deficit
units $=4.8\%$ of T173's $+0.155$. The honest boundary: the frame
enters the Gram \emph{additively}, $\hat A=\hat A_{\mathrm{arch}}+\hat
A_{\mathrm{comb}}$ exactly, and neither term alone has a positive Schur
floor on a single one of the $84$ cells --- the $4\%$-arch term decides
the positivity, no factorisation $(\mathrm{frame})\times(\mathrm{
arithmetic})$ exists, and no gauge argument can absorb an additive
term: \emph{this is where the cancellation identity stops being exact}.
Two side results settle T173's family: $G2$ is the \emph{unique} doubly
gauge-invariant and arithmetic member (the measured gauge degrees come
out as integers), and the $G3$--$G2$ offset of exactly $2$ is explained
($G2$ is $\mu^P_1$-blind, so the offset is the $\mu^P_1$ exponent,
measured $h^{-1.9975}$ --- T173's $1.9974$).

\emph{The frame rule is a sampling map, and the deficit is measured
without it (the key result).} The window builder takes
$(n_{\mathrm{zone}},\alpha,M)$ and nothing else, so $R=R(\alpha,M)$
identically: a frame rule is a \emph{curve} on that surface, two frames
reaching the same cell agree bit for bit, and pointwise there is
nothing to cancel. On the preregistered rectangle the $h$-direction
carries the deficit ($a=-0.281\pm0.066$, $4.3\sigma$) while the anchor
direction is flat; the exact between/within split of every leg deficit
(the split is an identity, exact to $5.6\times10^{-16}$) shows the
\emph{grid response} carries it --- $3.3\times$ the anchor-selection
part, whose sign is wrong on most legs: the cheap reading ``the frame
rule reads $h$ off the local log-gap, so the deficit is a selection
effect'' is tested and rejected. The driver is then identified: on a
leg, $\log\mathrm{dens}=\mathrm{const}(\alpha)-\log\nu$ identically
(dens $=$ comb atoms per lag cell), so no leg statistic could ever
separate $\nu$ from comb content ($r=-0.921$ on the ten gap-reading
legs --- the same signal under two names); the rectangle separates
them, and the deficit falls \emph{monotonically} $+0.281\to+0.172\to
+0.147\to+0.062$ across the density cuts $\mathrm{dens}\ge0/0.5/1/3$
while the anchor slope stays flat. The leg table orders perfectly by
density (A16/dens $0.38\to+1.19$; A8/$0.75\to+0.74$; A4/$2.5\to-0.10$)
--- T173's $2.8\sigma$ $\log\nu$ driver is a named and discharged
confounding. Exhausting the dense corner ($1020$ fresh power-check
cells on $153$ new anchors; pooled $1069$ cells on $151$ anchors with
$\ge4$ rungs each, the cluster-robust anchor mean the honest estimator)
gives
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\mathrm{DEFICIT}(\text{frame-free},\ \mathrm{dens}\ge3.0)\;=\;
+0.1111\pm0.0222\quad(5.0\sigma\ \text{from zero;}\ 0.4\sigma\ \text{from
T173's}\ +0.155\pm0.102)$
\end{keyeq}
\noindent --- the deficit survives an independent measurement with no
$D$-rule anywhere in it. Stress green: the comb scramble destroys the
positive block on $24/24$ test cells and moves $R$ by
$10^{2}$--$10^{5}$; jackknives stable; every numerical horizon declared
($1-r_{12}^2$ down to $9.3\times10^{-8}$, bars conditioned per cell).

\begin{keybox}[After T174: the phases and the dense limit]
\emph{(Verdict)} \textsc{partial-cancel} --- the gauge route is
\emph{exhausted}: multiplicative cancellation is theorem-form, the one
shared channel is certified $\le4.8\%$, the additive mixture cannot
cancel; any further cancellation claim needs a different pair of
functionals. P6 does \emph{not} become a theorem (only its
multiplicative half) but is less load-bearing: the deficit needs no
invariance argument --- it is measured on a $D$-rule-free surface, and
the fixed-$\nu$ invariance is explained (fixed $\nu$ $=$ fixed density
regime). The theorem cores of T172+T173+T174 are promoted as
\vref{v560} \veri{v560\_frame\_deficit\_identities.py}
(Section~\ref{sec:v560}). \emph{(Rest)} the per-anchor rate is not
universal ($\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}=3.02$, no residual $\alpha$-trend) ---
the untried candidate is the placement \emph{phases} of the heavy low
atoms $\mathrm{frac}(\log p/D)$; an admissibility question for the
chain (T173 admits $0.11$ atoms per lag cell; $\mathrm{dens}\ge3$
against all is a factor $2.5$ in the deficit); and the sparse corner
($+0.51$--$0.80$) --- regime or spline artefact. T175
(\texttt{phase\_placement\_probe.py}, contract
\texttt{PHASE.PLACEMENT}) then asked exactly that --- next subsection.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The placement phases: real and causal, but non-smooth ---
and the heterogeneity dissolves into the error bar (T175)}\label{sec:t175}
T175 (\texttt{phase\_placement\_probe.py}, contract
\texttt{PHASE.PLACEMENT}, $38/38$, $20.2$\,s, $1504$ cells on $188$
anchors --- \emph{every} prime power in $[40,1090]$ is an anchor, no
selection, no frame rule anywhere in the plan, so no anchor can have
been chosen for its phase --- crossed with the T174 ladder
$h=160\ldots1280$ plus the declared floor $h=128$; the two phase
families, the density bins, the deformation grid, the intervention
offsets and the split rule all declared before use; verdict
\textsc{phases-resist}) measures the placement phases directly and
takes the dense corner to its ceiling. The bridge first: the
frame-free deficit \emph{reproduces} on the wider anchor set,
$+0.1069\pm0.0222$ ($4.8\sigma$, $158$ anchor clusters, $0.13\sigma$
from T174) --- and so does the problem it inherits, the per-anchor
heterogeneity $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}=3.14$.

\emph{The phase construction --- and the trap said out loud.} For the
atom at $\log p$ the reference assembly splits its mass between two lag
cells with weight $\varphi_p=\mathrm{frac}(\log p/D)$: the placement
phase is the exact interpolation weight of the assembly, not a nuisance
parameter. The generating identity
$\varphi_p(h)=\mathrm{frac}(\log p/D)=\mathrm{frac}(h\,\theta_p)$ with
$\theta_p=\mathrm{frac}(\log p/\alpha)$ is certified at
$1.1\times10^{-13}$ on all $1316$ cells --- one real number per anchor
generates the whole rung ladder of phases (Weyl 1916). But the
preregistered anchor invariant $\theta_p$ is \emph{unusable}, and the
probe says so before fitting anything: $\theta_p$ is a smooth monotone
function of $\alpha$ (Rayleigh $Z=1296$ --- as far from uniform as a
circular sample gets), so a regression on it would be an
$\alpha$-regression in disguise, and T174 already reports no residual
$\alpha$-trend. Only the cell phase $\varphi_p(h)$ is free and
equidistributed (largest $Z=1.41$ on $1316$ cells). On that honest
regressor the phases are \emph{in} $\log R$: the declared family
$p=[5,7,11,13,17,19]$ raises $R^2$ from $0.045$ to $0.151$ on the
$1059$ dense cells, $F=10.80$ against a within-rung-scrambled null
whose $95\%$ point is $1.69$; held out under a rank-parity split the
amplitudes keep $+10.3\%$ of the residual variance, a composite
placebo family scores $0.81/-0.0275$, and the amplitudes are monotone
in $p$ ($0.018$ at $p=5$ to $0.141$ at $p=19$, $7.7\sigma$).

\emph{The honest correction --- the heterogeneity was substantially an
error-bar artefact.} The phases do \emph{not} carry the per-anchor
rate spread: $\chi^2/\mathrm{dof}$ falls only $3.14\to2.52$ (target
$<2$ missed), the held-out excess scatter gets \emph{worse}
($-15.4\%$), and the deficit itself moves $0.18\sigma$. The
exploratory scan closes everything else: density fine structure, rung
count, $\alpha$, $\mathrm{frac}(\alpha)$, prime-power order, residues
mod $3$ and $5$, per-anchor curvature --- every block improves in
sample and worsens held out. That leaves one suspect, which is not an
anchor property at all: the error bar. The OLS slope error assumes
independent rung residuals, and the phase modulation just proved they
are not; with jackknife slope errors the excess scatter goes
$0.1224\to0.0000$ and the robust pull spread $1.41\to1.22$, and the
model-free interleaved half-split gives $0.2722$ against
$\mathrm{sd}(e_n)=0.2789$ --- consistent with the jackknife, not with
OLS. T174's $\chi^2$ was substantially an OLS independence assumption,
not a physical spread; the last $22\%$ of the pull spread is named,
not swept. \emph{The $5.0\sigma$ deficit is unaffected either way}:
its bar comes from the anchor-to-anchor scatter itself, never from
$\mathrm{se}_n$.

\emph{The intervention (the key result).} A regression can be
confounded; an intervention cannot. With an exact rebuild control
($\delta=0$ reproduces $R$ to $0.0$ in $\log R$ on $40$ cells),
displacing the six family atoms inside their own lag cells --- cell
index fixed, mass conserved exactly, twelve lag entries change ---
gives
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\frac{d\log R}{d\delta}\;=\;879,\quad\text{linear to a factor }1.011
\text{ over the four declared decades }\delta=10^{-7}\ldots10^{-4}$
\end{keyeq}
\noindent --- \textbf{the placement phase is causal for $R$}, the
first interventional statement of the series. And it overturns the
\emph{shape} of the regression result while confirming its substance:
the fitted first harmonic predicts a local sensitivity of only $2.89$
--- a factor ${\sim}300$ too small, with predicted-versus-measured
shifts correlating at $r=+0.037$ --- so the $10\%$ the phases explain
is the small smooth component of a response that is locally enormous
and not first-harmonic. Positive definiteness dies for
$\delta\ge10^{-3}$ (displacing six of ${\sim}24\,000$ atoms by $1\%$
of one lag cell destroys the floor on $18\%$ of cells), and
$\mathrm{GAP}=\lambda_{\min}/\lambda_{\max}=1.6\times10^{-9}$--$4.8
\times10^{-6}$: the Schur floor is a \emph{near-degeneracy}, so $\log
R$ is necessarily non-smooth in the phases, and no phase formula is
certifiable. Consistently, mass-preserving alternative assemblies are
\emph{inadmissible} (lump $0\%$, wide $46\%/0\%$ PD survival), and the
admissible continuous deformation gives sensitivities $+0.384$
(sparse) against $-1.054$ (dense), ratio $0.4$ --- the sparse corner
is a density regime, \emph{not} an assembly artefact.

\emph{The dense limit, measured to its ceiling.} The corner is
exhausted by a theorem about the caps ($\mathrm{dens}\le361$ from the
sieve cap and $h\ge128$; $359$ reached). Over three decades of comb
density, in six declared ratio-$4$ bins with cluster-robust bars, the
deficit falls
$+0.982\pm0.213\to+0.576\to+0.207\to+0.194\to+0.088\to-0.057\pm0.132$
--- monotone within $2\sigma$ at every step, density slope
$6.1\sigma$, and \emph{the densest reachable bin is consistent with
zero} ($0.4\sigma$ at median density $167$). The extrapolation fence
is the most important sentence of the block: a true zero at finite
density, a power-law approach to zero and a plateau below $0.132$ are
\emph{all} consistent with these bars, and no probe under this sieve
can separate them --- the limit is undecided, not claimed. The
sharpened confound test (only the rectangle separates $\log h$ from
$\log\mathrm{dens}$: within one anchor they are collinear at $-1.000$)
finds \emph{both} channels significant ($\log h$ $+0.2435\pm0.0670$,
$\log\mathrm{dens}$ $-0.0631\pm0.0172$, curvature $a_2=-0.137\pm
0.029$): T174's density driver survives but is no longer unique ---
the deficit is not a single exponent but a local slope of a curved
surface. A rule proposal goes to the chain convention, not applied
retroactively: $\mathrm{dens}\ge1$ ($+0.722\pm0.094$ on unresolved
cells against $+0.099\pm0.019$ on resolved ones, $6.5\sigma$
separation, $6\%$ of cells); the comb scramble destroys $12/12$.

\begin{keybox}[After T175: the larger sieve, nothing else]
\emph{(Verdict)} \textsc{phases-resist} --- the phases are real and
causal, but no phase formula is certifiable (the response is provably
non-smooth: the floor is a near-degeneracy), and the heterogeneity
they were meant to explain dissolved substantially into the error bar
--- a correction to T174's reading, not to its number. \emph{(Rest)}
the shape of the phase response in closed form,
$d\lambda_{\min}=v^{\mathsf T}\,d\hat A\,v$ --- first-order
perturbation theory of the near-degenerate low block, no fit anywhere
(it turns the phase regression into an identity or kills it);
\textbf{the dense-corner zero needs a larger sieve, nothing else} ---
a sieve at $10\times$ the atom cap moves the ceiling from $361$ to
${\sim}3607$ and is the only way to decide the limit; the curvature
($a_2=-0.137\pm0.029$) means ``the deficit'' needs a declared
reference rung or a curvature term; whether the positivity margin has
an $h$ floor at all; and the last $22\%$ of the pull spread.
\emph{(Candidates P175-1--P175-8, pending)} the generating identity,
the density curve, the two channels, the causality finding, the
error-bar resolution, the spline-positivity finding, the
$\mathrm{dens}\ge1$ proposal, the exclusion --- no promotion here.
T176 (\texttt{dense\_limit\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{DENSE.LIMIT})
ran exactly that larger sieve --- the next subsection (landed after
the reverse-flow part T177; numbered by contract).
\end{keybox}

\subsection{The bigger sieve: the density curve sits at zero, and the
measurement programme closes (T176)}\label{sec:t176}
T176 (\texttt{dense\_limit\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{DENSE.LIMIT},
$24/24$, $118.7$\,s, verdict \textsc{sits-at-zero}; landed after T177
--- part numbering by contract) is the last decidable measurement of
phase 2, and it is deliberately \emph{one} change: the sieve cap rises
by a factor $20.8$ ($\mathtt{ATOM\_MAX}=1.2\times10^{6}\to
2.5\times10^{7}$; $1\,566\,727$ prime-power atoms) while the ratio
$R$, the cluster-robust estimator, the assembly, the KMS basis and the
Schur block are held \emph{verbatim} at T175, so the extension is an
extension and not a new measurement. The cost statement is the first
result: the sieve builds in $0.08$\,s at $59.7$\,MB peak --- \emph{the
sieve was never the binding constraint} (the $14\,532$-cell grid costs
the $110$\,s) --- and the honest resource fence follows: a further
factor $5$ in the cap would fit the budget, a factor $100$ (the next

\noindent Pooled over the two new bins the deficit is
$+0.0496\pm0.0372$ ($1.3\sigma$): \emph{no sign change anywhere on the
curve, no stabilisation above zero --- the curve sits at zero from
dens ${\sim}410$ upward}. The density slope is $-0.0725\pm0.0090$
($8.0\sigma$ over $4.0$ decades), and the bin-4 monotonicity violation
is declared, not smoothed: the finer $2^{1/4}$ rung ladder samples the
curvature of $\log R$ in $\log h$ differently from T175's $\sqrt2$
ladder (below). What the bigger sieve actually bought is a number:
\emph{any plateau of the deficit above $0.074$ is excluded at
$2\sigma$ for dens in $[410,6118]$, against T175's $0.264$ --- a
factor $3.6$} --- and that is the whole content of the extra
$48$\,MB of sieve. The consistency stress could have killed the file
and did not: all six T175 bins, re-measured with T175's exact anchor
set and rung ladder under the new sieve, reproduce at $0.0\sigma$.
The curvature map survives with T175's coefficients (both channels:
$\log h$ $+0.1529\pm0.0258$ at $5.9\sigma$, $\log\mathrm{dens}$
$-0.0434\pm0.0060$ at $7.3\sigma$; per-anchor $a_2=-0.0842\pm0.0085$;
all $\le1.7\sigma$ from T175), and none of the six preregistered
reparametrisations makes the surface one exponent --- the fitted
direction wants $\mathrm{dens}^{+0.284}h$, and no candidate sits
there.

\emph{R1 closed, and the $300\times$ anomaly explained.} The
Feynman--Hellmann form
\begin{keyeq}$\displaystyle
\frac{d\log R}{d\delta}
=\frac{v^{\mathsf T}d\tilde A\,v}{\lambda_{\min}}
-\frac{w^{\mathsf T}d\tilde A\,w}{\lambda_{\max}}
-\frac{d\mathrm{DEL}}{\mathrm{DEL}}$
\end{keyeq}
\noindent reproduces the full rebuild to $3.37\times10^{-6}$ at the
minimum of a declared step ladder whose U-shape is exhibited (no
floor $\Rightarrow$ the residual is the difference quotient, not the
formula): T175's intervention regression is now an \emph{identity}
about the assembly, and the decomposition corrects the expected
story --- $d\mathrm{DEL}/\mathrm{DEL}$ carries $84\%$ of the response,
$\lambda_{\min}$ only $7\%$. And the ${\sim}300\times$ gap between
T175's first harmonic and its local derivative is \emph{a pole}:
positive definiteness survives only $2\%$ of the phase period
($\delta_{\mathrm{PD}}=5.9\times10^{-3}$ median,
$\delta_{\mathrm{PD}}\cdot|d\log R/d\delta|=5.8=O(1)$), so a
first-harmonic regression estimates a Fourier coefficient of a
function with a pole in the interval --- neither number is wrong.
Measured against the going-in hypothesis: the two lowest modes of the
normalised low block sit $13.4\%$ apart \emph{already at} $\delta=0$
--- the intervention does not create a degeneracy, it runs along one,
which closes the loop with the decomposition: $\mathrm{DEL}=1-r_{12}^2$
\emph{is} the near-degeneracy of the bottom two directions, exactly
the channel T174 proved does not cancel. Stress: the
occupancy-preserving scramble kills positive definiteness on
$194/194$ cells in the first new bin; $L_P$ exact at $1.9\times
10^{-15}$; the anti-fitting battery is mechanical (bin edges ratio-4
exact, the first five bins bit-for-bit T175's).

\emph{The ladder caveat (the anti-promotion).} The bin estimator is
\emph{ladder-dependent} at the $0.20$ level: a ratio-4 bin holds
${\sim}12$ rungs of the $2^{1/4}$ ladder against ${\sim}6$ of T175's
$\sqrt2$ ladder, and with $a_2\neq0$ they sample the curvature
differently. Consequence, carried into the ledger row: any quoted bin
deficit must cite its rung ladder, or the number is not reproducible.

\begin{keybox}[After T176: the measurement programme closes]

\subsection{The reverse flow, resumed: the CP mirror narrows four ledger rows (T177)}\label{sec:t177}
While T176 was running, the reverse flow resumed: T177 (\texttt{cp\_invariant\_probe.py}, contract
\texttt{CP.INVARIANT}, $49/49$, verdict \textsc{degenerate}) carries the newest tool of the
phase --- gauge-degree bookkeeping under declared group actions (T173/T174) --- back to the
physics side and runs it on the four CP ledger rows (\texttt{REDTEAM.D.01},
\texttt{E8.CHAN.01}, \texttt{CP.MOD.01}, \texttt{DUAL.FRAME.01}). All four constructions are
first rebuilt exactly from the compiler primitives (the magnitude bijection, the
$248=120+128$ channel split, the frozen reading $\delta=\pi/3+3\lambda_C^2=1.198231638$
certified against the lattice, the oriented volume $\det(\mathbf1,d,n)=21$, the classical
Jarlskog anchor $J=3.327\times10^{-5}$ with the CKM unitary to $10^{-41}$), and one new
exact identity falls out of the rebuild: on the hexagonal unit $\rho=e^{i\pi/3}$ the phase
channel carries $\sum_k\rho^{d_k}=4\rho$ ($\arg=\pi/3$ exactly, sheet-\emph{even} because
the $E_8$ degrees are even) while the magnitude channel carries $\sum_k\rho^{m_k}=4$
($\arg=0$ exactly, sheet-\emph{odd} because the exponents are odd) --- the channel typing
has an exact fiber realisation, not only a counting analogy, with the honest caveat said out
loud (reality of the exponent sum alone is not hexagon-specific).

\noindent The mirror itself is a $6\times4$ table --- six candidate functionals against the
$\mu_3$ branch group, the positive rescalings, the parity/sector involution and a
\emph{declared} $D_4$ deck model, with the character bookkeeping verified as a homomorphism
in every non-trivial cell --- and it returns the pre-registered kill verdict on both tiers.
Tier~1 (strict invariance under all four groups) is \emph{empty by algebra}: both complex
kernels commute with conjugation, so every $\pi/3$-carrier is $\kappa$-odd, and invariant
$+$ odd forces $\operatorname{Im}F=0$. On the Jarlskog-class criterion (Tier~2) \emph{two}
rows pass, in two inequivalent character classes --- the channel angle (sheet-even) and the
scale-free orientation $\operatorname{Im}\rho=\sin(\pi/3)$ (sheet-odd) --- so the $\pi/3$ is
invariant as a \emph{value} but is not pinned to one functional, and \emph{no} invariant
carrier couples to the frame: what is frame data is the oriented volume $21$ and the sign
convention, not the angle (the raw orientation functional is homogeneous of degree $+1$ in
the frame normalisation, and dividing by the oriented volume removes the frame identically,
$\operatorname{Im}(\rho\det)/\det=\operatorname{Im}\rho$ exactly). The net effect is a
verdict of \emph{degeneracy} with four \emph{narrowed} ledger readings and no marker moves:
the magnitude data carry exactly zero phase ($\arg\prod c=0$ on both sectors), the
\texttt{REDTEAM.D.01} residual is a \emph{fiber} datum, the phase-channel angle is
sheet-blind, the full $\delta$ has no character (a CP-even correction on a CP-odd angle;
only the leading term $\pi/3$ is character-covariant), and \texttt{DUAL.FRAME.01}'s
$21\sin(\pi/3)$ splits into an invariant fiber core and a non-invariant frame factor. Which
of the two Tier-2 characters is physical stayed open at T177 --- the sheet-odd reading reproduces
\texttt{CP.MU6.01}'s quark/lepton split, a structural preference and not a derivation ---
together with the frame-coupling question; both are decided one part later
(T178, Section~\ref{sec:t178}). The exact cores are promoted to the physics
side: \veri{v561\_cp\_channel\_identities.py}.

\medskip
\noindent\emph{Where phase 2 now stands.} The map is complete, its
portability is measured, and its frame dependence is dissected: the
reduction from the I5 uniformity question to a single object runs end
to end and reproduces in one file (T171), its identity tower carries
unchanged onto every frame and anchor arithmetic tried while every
carried number must be recomputed per surface (T172), the demand side
itself is a frame datum whose difference against the delivery is the
one surviving number (T173), and the gauge route on that number is
exhausted by theorems (T174): everything multiplicative cancels
exactly --- including the entire $h^{-2}$ channel --- the one shared
channel is certified unconditionally at under five percent, the
additive arch/comb mixture admits no factorisation, and the deficit
stands measured on a frame-rule-free surface at $+0.1111\pm0.0222$
($5.0\sigma$), its driver the comb density per lag cell. The interior
of that number is then opened (T175): the placement phases of the
heavy deep atoms are real in $\log R$ and causal for it under an
exact-rebuild intervention, but the response is provably non-smooth
--- the Schur floor is a near-degeneracy --- so no phase formula is

and the deficit falls monotonically with comb density over three
decades to a densest reachable bin consistent with zero, with true
zero, power-law approach and low plateau undecidable under this sieve.
The instrument question is then answered by the instrument itself
(T176): the twentyfold sieve raises the ceiling to $6120$, both new
bins are consistent with zero (pooled $+0.0496\pm0.0372$), the plateau
window narrows by a factor $3.6$ --- \textsc{sits-at-zero}, the last
decidable measurement of phase 2 --- while the derivative identity
closes in Feynman--Hellmann form and the $300\times$ harmonic anomaly

programme closes as planned}: what is left is one statement --- an
unconditional certificate that two explicit finite $\Lambda$-sum
vectors become collinear at the demanded rate, now stated frame-free,
with the true-zero/power-law/plateau reading of the dense limit
explicitly open and no finite sieve able to decide it --- and the
work continues in the classification papers (Paper II) and the
backflow lines (T177--T199), not in further probes of this instrument. The
measurement surface is certified, the quantifier is open, R1 is
classified; the capstone that certifies exactly this map is
load-bearing \veri{v559\_phase2\_capstone.py}, the frame/deficit
identities of the closing arc are load-bearing
\veri{v560\_frame\_deficit\_identities.py}, and the dense-limit

\subsection{The reverse flow, continued: the frame door of the CP mirror, decided (T178)}\label{sec:t178}
One part after the mirror, the backflow line answers T177's two open items ---
and they are pure finite algebra, so the answer is a decision, not a measurement:
T178 (\texttt{cp\_frame\_carrier\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{FRAME.CARRIER},
$31/31$, verdict \textsc{fiber-pinned}). \textbf{R1 is decided.} The natural
(metric-free) half is negative \emph{by theorem}: the fiber acts on the frame by
a scalar on the $n$-row, so every homogeneous frame block factorises exactly
(checked on fully generic degree-$1..4$ polynomials with symbolic coefficients),
and the metric-free invariants of $(\mathbf1,d,n)$ have \emph{one} generator ---
the exact bracket enumeration gives six permutations $=\pm\Delta$ and $21$
identically vanishing brackets (Weyl 1946 first fundamental theorem as the cited
class boundary) --- so every scale-free ratio is constant and no frame-coupled
scale-free $\pi/3$-carrier exists without a metric: T177's obstruction sentence
(``one determinant only'') is now a theorem. The metric half couples but is
\emph{non-canonical}: declared metrics admit frame-coupled Tier-2 carriers, but
they split into two character classes ($\Delta/\langle d,n\rangle$ and
$\Delta/\langle\mathbf1,n\rangle$ at $(-1,-1,+1)$ against
$\Delta^{2}/\langle n,n\rangle$ at $(-1,-1,-1)$) and the admissible normalisers
contain a whole continuum $q_t=t\,n_1^{2}+n_2^{2}+n_3^{2}$ (deck-invariant for
every $t$, values $441\sin(\pi/3)/(25t+117)$) --- no canonical frame factor, and
the exhibited factors $21/8$, $21/2$, $441/142$ are normaliser-relative frame
data with the anti-numerology fence wired as a check. \textbf{R2 is selected.}
The classical anchor itself does the selecting: the Jarlskog invariant carries
the full character tuple $(-1,-1,-1)$ under conjugation, the sheet flip and the
declared deck reflection (each certified at $40$ digits), matching the sheet-odd
orientation class and not the sheet-even channel class --- of T177's two
degenerate classes, exactly one; the unique anchor-matching \emph{canonical}
carrier is the fiber-pure $\operatorname{Im}\rho=\sin(\pi/3)$ (selected,
conditional on the anchor --- not derived). \textbf{And the degeneracy is
explained}: the single-sine lemma --- on a $\mu_n$ fiber the nonzero carrier
magnitudes $\{|\operatorname{Im}\rho_n^{k}|\}$ form a one-element set iff $n$ is
crystallographic, $n\in\{1,2,3,4,6\}$, by
$\sin(4\pi/n)-\sin(2\pi/n)=2\sin(\pi/n)\cos(3\pi/n)$ --- makes T177's
\textsc{degenerate} verdict \emph{forced}: the compiler's two clocks $\mu_4$
($j=1728$) and $\mu_6$ ($j=0$) are exactly the two maximal single-sine fibers,
so value-based pinning of functionals is impossible there by theorem (on
$\mu_5$, values do separate carriers). No marker moves, the frozen reading is
untouched, and the CP residual is not closed --- it is \emph{relocated with a
proof}: the invariant CP core is the fiber datum $\sin(\pi/3)$ and provably
cannot be made frame data without a non-canonical metric import. The exact
cores are promoted to the physics side: \veri{v564\_cp\_fiber\_pin.py}.

The backflow then runs in the \emph{other} direction --- from the physics-side

self-code module had proved, symbolically, that the Paper-II rank-3
polarisation is $(2{+}1)$-Lorentz geometry and that the low block carries a
relative pencil $Z=B^{-1}S$ with three exact identities; the one measurable
question that decides whether that lens buys anything is whether \emph{one}
pencil eigenvalue stays uniformly separated from $1$ on the reachable surface.
T179 (\texttt{lambda\_pencil\_probe.py}, contract \texttt{LAMBDA.PENCIL},
$4/4$, verdict \textsc{one-mode}) answers it on the declared T170 frame-A scan
(all $70$ windows, the \vref{v563} surface bit for bit): the identities are
machine-tight at $2\times10^{-14}$; the \emph{locking} mode is $\lambda_2$,
hugging $1$ at median $1.000021$, while the spectator $\lambda_1$ sits far
\emph{above} $1$ ($[4.53,180.64]$, $\min|1-\lambda_1|=3.53$) --- the label
guess of the motivating review, reversed --- so the two-dimensional
cancellation of the classification paper reduces to the single scalar
$1-\lambda_2$ on the whole reachable surface (on the $h=540$ reference window
$1-\lambda_2=-2.27\times10^{-5}$ reproduces $\det\hat A=4.22\times10^{-3}$
exactly), and the position scramble explodes $|1-\lambda_2|$ by
$\times1.9\times10^{6}$ while the identities keep holding: the locking is
arithmetic placement. No uniformity claim beyond the surface, no rate, no RH
statement --- Problem~7.1 is \emph{typed}, not bounded. The exact core is
load-bearing: \veri{v569\_lambda\_pencil\_onemode.py}
(Section~\ref{sec:v569}).

\section{The closed-form theory of the parity read block: statements}\label{sec:theory}
% =====================================================================

The backflow campaign left behind a compact body of exact statements that
deserve one consolidated listing (proof sketches live in the cited modules;
the algebraic cores of Theorems~2--4 are additionally formalized in Lean~4,
\texttt{TfptCarrier/ParityWeightLaws.lean}, building against Mathlib).

\begin{keybox}[The closed-form theory: seven statements]
\textbf{Theorem 1 (diagonal weight formula, \vref{v587}).} For the parity
mode $t_k$ on the window of half-length $m$ ($N=2m+1$,
$\omega_k=2\pi k/N$), the corpus diagonal lag weight is
$W_{kk}(d)=\tfrac{2}{N}\big[(N{-}1{-}d)\cos(\omega_kd)
+\sin(\omega_k(d{+}1))/\sin\omega_k\big]$ for $d\ge1$, $W(0)=1$; the
apparent piecewise break at $d=m$ cancels (Lean: \texttt{branch\_merge}),
and the reflection-edge suppression is an exact two-term cancellation.
Together with the \vref{v576} cross formula this closes the whole
$K=2$ read block.

\textbf{Theorem 2 (one-function assembly, \vref{v588}).} With
$G_{ij}(\beta)=\sum_{d\ge1}e^{-\beta d}W_{ij}(d)$ (exact geometric-trig
series), the prime-free model's comb side is the pole exponent
($\beta=-D/2$) and the archimedean side is the trivial-zero ladder
($c_{\mathrm{ar}}(d)=-Df(dD)$, $f(w)=\sum_ne^{-(2n+1/2)w}$): the
deterministic defect is the explicit formula's skeleton, pole against
$\Gamma$-factor, in one function.

\textbf{Theorem 3 (rank-one pole term, \vref{v591}).} The pole part of
the closed entries is exactly separable:
$S^{\mathrm{pole}}=-32\pi^2ae^a\,gg^{T}$, $g_k=k/(a^2+4\pi^2k^2)$,
$\det S^{\mathrm{pole}}\equiv0$ (Lean: \texttt{pole\_rank\_one}).

\textbf{Theorem 4 (locking-direction law, \vref{v591}).}
$v_2/v_1=-(a^2+16\pi^2)/(2(a^2+4\pi^2))$, with distance from $-\tfrac12$
exactly $-6\pi^2/(a^2+4\pi^2)$ (Lean: \texttt{direction\_law},
\texttt{direction\_law\_approach}); matches the measured directions to
$0.04$--$1.4\%$ and derives the \vref{v577} null ray as the limit.

\textbf{Theorem 5 (determinant law, \vref{v592}).} $\det S(a)$ is closed
with the $e^{2a}$ coefficient identically zero and exact leading law
$640\pi^2e^a/a^3$; the measured dominance growth tracks it at
correlation $0.9985$.

\textbf{Theorem 6 (cutoff completion, \vref{v593}).} With the
$\sigma_0=u_0/(2\alpha)$ cutoff the closed entries match the model to
$0.7$--$1\%$ and the determinant to $0.2$--$1\%$: the density layer is
closed end-to-end; the residual is $O(1/N^2)$.

\textbf{Theorem 7 (unconditional entry certificate, \vref{v594}).} Via
partial summation and the published bound $|\psi(x)-x|<0.94\sqrt{x}$
($11<x\le10^{19}$, B\"uthe 2018), the entry-level arithmetic deviation
obeys the unconditional bound $\sup|\mathrm{Osc}|\le{\sim}17$ on the
declared surface, and the certificate
$|S^{\mathrm{real}}-S^{\mathrm{model}}|\le\sup\times\mathrm{TV}$ holds
with large margin --- the first unconditional statement of the program.
The determinant-level lock stays with the zero-oscillation theorem.
\end{keybox}

\subsection{Derivation sketches}\label{sec:theory-proofs}

\emph{Theorem 1.} For the sine mode $v_j=\tfrac{2}{\sqrt N}\sin(\omega_k(j{+}1))$
the autocorrelation and self-convolution are Dirichlet sums:
$\mathrm{ac}_k(d)=\tfrac{2}{N}\big[(m{-}d)\cos(\omega_kd)
+\tfrac{\sin(\omega_k(d{+}1))+\sin(\omega_kd)}{2\sin\omega_k}\big]$ and the two
convolution branches close analogously (all machine-exact,
\vref{v587}~E2.1).  Substituting into the corpus assembly
$W(d)=2\,\mathrm{ac}(d)-\mathrm{cv}(2m{-}1{-}d)$ and using
$\omega_k(2m{+}1)=2\pi k$, the two branches produce the \emph{same}
expression --- the cancellation is the linear-in-trig-values field identity
formalized as \texttt{branch\_merge} in Lean.  At $d=N{-}1{-}s$ both terms are
$O(s)$, which is the exact edge suppression.

\emph{Theorem 2.} The cell masses $2(e^{(d+1)D/2}-e^{dD/2})$ are geometric in
$e^{dD/2}$, and the Weil kernel is the geometric ladder
$f(w)=e^{-w/2}/(1-e^{-2w})=\sum_{n\ge0}e^{-(2n+1/2)w}$; hence both sides of
the defect are values of the one finite geometric-trig sum
$G_{ij}(\beta)$, evaluated in closed form via
$\sum_{d=1}^{L-1}z^d$ and $\sum_{d=1}^{L-1}dz^d$ with
$z=e^{-\beta+i\omega_k}$.

\emph{Theorems 3--5.} The Laplace integrals
$2a\int e^{a\sigma}g_{ij}(\sigma)\,d\sigma$ are elementary; their
denominators factor as $D_{11}=(a^2{+}4\pi^2)^2$,
$D_{22}=(a^2{+}16\pi^2)^2$, $D_{12}=(a^2{+}4\pi^2)(a^2{+}16\pi^2)$, so
$D_{11}D_{22}=D_{12}^2$ and the exponential parts are exactly separable
($S^{\mathrm{pole}}=-32\pi^2ae^a\,gg^T$, $g_k=k/(a^2{+}4\pi^2k^2)$;
Lean: \texttt{pole\_rank\_one}).  The null direction of $gg^T$ gives the
direction law with $-\tfrac12$ limit (Lean: \texttt{direction\_law},
\texttt{direction\_law\_approach}); the determinant follows by expanding
$S_{11}S_{22}-S_{12}^2$ --- the $e^{2a}$ terms cancel by separability and the
$e^{a}$ coefficient is
$128\pi^2a^3(5a^2{+}32\pi^2)/D_{12}^2\sim640\pi^2/a^3$ (Lean:
\texttt{det\_S\_closed}).

\emph{Theorem 6 and the exact dictionary.} The lag variable is
$\sigma=d/N$, so the continuum form of the cell sum carries
$a_{\mathrm{eff}}=ND/2$ and the limits $[u_0/(ND),\,2\alpha/(ND)]$; since
$ND=2\alpha+O(D)$ by the window construction, the naive $\alpha$-form
carries a first-order-in-$D$ residual --- which is exactly the
\vref{v593} gap, closed at the identity level ($1.00000$--$1.00017$) by
\vref{v595}.

\emph{Theorem 7.} Partial summation gives
$\mathrm{mass}(u)=4\sqrt x-2+2E(x)/\sqrt x+\int_1^xE(t)t^{-3/2}dt$ with
$E=\psi-t$ (machine-verified); inserting the published bound
$|E|<0.94\sqrt t$ ($t>11$) and the exact small-range integral yields the
unconditional sup, and integration by parts against the read profiles
gives the certificate (\vref{v594}).

\subsection{The remaining arithmetic statement, self-contained}\label{sec:theory-open}

For external consumption, the one remaining arithmetic statement of the
program can be posed without any TFPT context.  Fix a window (an
admissible pair $(\alpha, D)$ with $M = \lceil 2\alpha/D\rceil$ even,
$N = M+1$ odd, $h = M/2$) and let $W_{ij}(d)$ be the closed parity
weights of Theorem~1 and $X_v(u)$ the read profile projected onto the
closed direction of Theorem~4.  Define, for each nontrivial zeta zero
$\tfrac12 + i\gamma$, the explicit coupling
\[
c_\gamma \;=\; -2\int_{u_0}^{2\alpha}
\frac{\sin(\gamma u)}{\gamma}\, dX_v(u)
\qquad(u_0 = 2\log(-C_\infty/4),\; C_\infty = -2(\zeta'/\zeta)(\tfrac12)),
\]
and let $K(\alpha, D)$ be the closed density value of the same
projected form (an elementary function by Theorems~3--6).  The
machine-verified observation (\vref{v596}) is
\[
\sum_{\gamma>0} c_\gamma \;=\; -\,K(\alpha, D)\,
\bigl(1 + O(h^{-1})\bigr)
\]
across the declared ladder, with median relative deviation
$7.7\times10^{-4}$, and with the sum \emph{collective} (no single zero
contributes more than $6\%$; scrambling the underlying prime comb
breaks the identity by six orders of magnitude).  \textbf{Open
problem (equidistribution form).} Prove, for the window family, that
the zero couplings satisfy this cancellation law with a uniform rate
--- i.e.\ bound $\bigl|\sum_\gamma c_\gamma + K\bigr|/|K|$ by
$C h^{-1}$ uniformly.  No RH-type input is expected to be necessary
for fixed windows (the couplings decay in $\gamma$ and the identity is
an explicit-formula statement); the \emph{uniformity} in the window is
the open content.  The measured constant is now explicit and
\emph{frozen as a module} (\veri{v618\_uniform\_constant.py}): on the
declared surface ($69$ floor-passed windows, $h=142$--$1445$) the
model value $q_{\mathrm{model}}$ keeps \emph{one} sign on the whole
ladder ($0.039$--$0.112$; no model zero crossing anywhere), and on
every \emph{lock-sign} window ($67$ of $69$) the relative deviation
times $h$ stays below $1$ (measured max $0.982$), with tercile
medians $0.61/0.45/0.39$ (non-increasing) --- so the conjecture is
posed with the concrete constant $C=1$.  The sharpened typing:
exactly \emph{two} windows carry a $q_{\mathrm{real}}$ sign flip
($h=1219$ at $9.2\cdot10^3$ and the edge window $h=1445$ at $3.5$),
and the violator set of the $C=1$ bound equals the flip set
\emph{exactly} --- the sign predicts the bound violation
window-sharp.  (This corrects an earlier note that attributed the
$h=1219$ blow-up to a $q_{\mathrm{model}}$ zero crossing and missed
the edge flip.)  Scrambled combs break the bound by more than
$10^4$.  The flips themselves are since \emph{explained}
(\veri{v619\_flip\_mechanics.py}): the two flip windows are exactly
the two whose atom demand $2\alpha$ exceeds the prime-power data cap
$U_{\max}=12.899$ --- their combs are truncated --- and truncation
injection into complete windows reproduces the flips with matched
sign and magnitude at both scales; on the complete-comb surface
($2\alpha\le U_{\max}$) the $C=1$ bound holds with \emph{zero}
exceptions.  The flip windows are data-boundary artifacts, not
arithmetic phenomena.

Two further machine-checked facts frame this statement externally
(2026-08-02).  \emph{The geometric frame:} through the exact Lorentz
congruence $P^{\mathsf T}J_{\mathrm{det}}P=J_{\mathrm{fix}}$
(\veri{v624\_external\_lattice\_audit.py}) every complete window's

\subsection{The T-B chain: the absorption margin typed and largely
closed on the surface}\label{sec:tb-chain}

The afternoon bundling (2026-08-03) resolves the one piece the rank-3
surface theorem left open: T-B, the razor-thin absorption margin of
the deployed $2\times2$ lock block.  \emph{The typing}
(\veri{v692\_rank3\_lockgram.py}, $7/7$): via the v677 master
identity, polarized, the lock block decomposes exactly per entry as
$\hat A_2=G_Z+P+\mathrm{tail}$ --- a \emph{positive zero-Gram} $G_Z$
(each zero contributes the psd rank-$\le2$ matrix
$w_\gamma\,\mathrm{Re}[\phi(\gamma)\phi(\gamma)^\dagger]$ with the
two lock profiles $\phi_i(\gamma)=F_i(D\gamma)$; Cauchy--Schwarz is
manifest per $\gamma$) plus a psd \emph{rank-1 pole layer}
$P=c_Ps\,s^{\mathsf T}$ in closed form.  The margin identity
\[
\det(G_Z+P)\;=\;\det G_Z\;+\;c_P\,(s_\perp^{\mathsf T}G_Zs_\perp)
\]
shows the T-B margin \emph{is} the transverse zero mass --- a sum of
squares of the weighted mass the zeros place orthogonal to the pole
direction in the 2D lock space ($\gamma_1$ alone carries
$3$--$61\%$).  On-line zeros can only \emph{increase} the determinant
($2\times2$ psd superadditivity), so the computed truncation is
safe-side and the entire question compresses to off-line quadruples
\emph{above the cited verification height}: ``$E$ kippt nicht'' is a
quantified partial-RH tail statement --- neither an envelope question
of the 2c kind nor a renaming of W3 in two dimensions.  \emph{The
closure} (\veri{v693\_rank3\_density\_close.py}, $5/5$): replacing
the worst-case envelope by the strongest published explicit bounds
--- Platt--Trudgian $3\times10^{12}$, the
Hasanalizade--Shen--Wong count, functional-equation halving, and the
explicit Ingham-form zero density (arXiv:2507.15184, valid from
exactly $3\times10^{12}$) --- inside a sharpened safe-side envelope
(sinh difference pairing, $V(0)=0$, on-line subtraction; the penalty
drops $\times6.5$--$14.4$), \textbf{$60$ of the $70$ complete frame-A
windows close unconditionally-modulo-citations}.  The open remainder
is exact: nine windows with required heights
$T^*\in[1.0\times10^{13},3.0\times10^{13}]$ and the deep window
$h=5690$ at $T^*=8.5\times10^{14}$; the extension beyond the declared
family grows like $e^{3.74a}$.  Honest scope: this closes the
determinant of the $2\times2$ lock block; full window positivity (W3,
all modes) remains the conjecture, and no RH claim is made.
